title: Good sound but feels and acts cheap. Not your typical Plantronics device!
text:
I love Plantronics BT devices. When my PLT-165 died, I wanted another one but couldn't find one. I purchased this PLT E100 because it was roughly the same size and it can sit in the ear without any additional hooks.

The sound quality is good but it behaves a little funky in how it connects to devices, especially if it's connected to two devices at the same time. Connected to Zoom on my iPad and a call came in on my phone. I could not hear the call at first. Needed to manually connect again to the BT to hear the call. Then, going back to the Zoom meeting, I had to turn the BT off and back on again to get it to transmit sound even though it said I was connected to the iPad. Odd!

It is much lighter (weight) than the PLT-165 and it feels as if it's made out of cheap plastic. The on/off switch is very stiff to the point of being annoying. If it's already in my ear, sometimes I need to take it out again just to turn it on or off. It also doesn't like to sit in my ear the way the PLT-165 did. The ear piece is identical to the other model so I guess it has something to do with the weight difference.

I can deal with all of those minor issues. My biggest problem is that the battery does not last as it should. It will tell me I have 7 hours talk time but it's dead in around 4 hours, or less. It charges quickly but that doesn't help if I'm on the go. I must be careful to make sure it has a full charge before going out or it may not last.

It wasn't expensive. It's got good sound quality. But, it's the first Plantronics headset I've used (with over 25 years of using Plantronics equipment) that I wasn't happy with. It looks like a Plantronics device but it certainly does not work or feel like one! I won't replace it but I definitely I will not be buying another one of this model.

I noticed that there is another name attached to the Plantronics name on their website. I wonder if they have been bought out or joined with another company. If so, that's probably why this BT has been so disappointing.

Update: Macbook Users!!!!!! Please Read!!!!
So there has been an issue with external monitors and Macbooks new update.
-Problem: You plug this monitor to your macbook the 1st time and it works. After it sleeps or you turn it back on it fails to work. This problem seems to only be an issue with USB C to USB C. I used a USB C to HDMI female and then attached the HDMI male to HDMI mini Male that came with the monitor and this setup worked perfectly. The adapter was "Belkin".

-Solution: You HAVE to use the power adapter the monitor comes with. Yes, USB C can do video, audio, and power, but ignore that and just power up the monitor on it's own power adapter. You also have to have your macbook OPEN and not in clamshell mode and with it's power cord attached. So both devices need to be charging. Once you connect it should work. If it doesn't YOU HAVE TO PUT YOUR LAPTOP IN SLEEP MODE then wake it up and this should activate the monitor. Now you can unplug the monitors power and it will run fully off the ONE usb c connected to the laptop.

To close your laptop and use with out the power adapter on both the monitor and laptop, you need to download amphetamine. It's a program that allows external monitors to work when your macbook is closed. Without this program, every time you close your macbook the monitor will not work.

title: High Quality economy binoculars
text: I am impressed with the quality level of these inexpensive binoculars. I have not heard of this Lindafo binocular brand before but what caught my eye was the number 5 rating in the Amazon rankings. The ratings for these binoculars have since gone down a bit. These are easily portable and I'm able to hold them steady due to their relatively light weight. They would be fine for camping, bird watching, hiking or just about any use were a  smaller sized binoculars would come in handy. The optics are excellent. The image quality is bright and sharp with no distortion at the edges of the field. It would make better sense to buy this model over the popular smaller sized 25mm binocular models due to the increased light gathering ability of the 42mm objective lenses. For general recreation use the 12 power magnification of these is fine. The binoculars come with a carry bag and a smart phone adapter. The first day I had these I tried taking photos with these binoculars and my smart phone. These binoculars ability to take photos with a smart phone seems to be more of a novelty item and I'm not impressed with the photos I took using these binoculars. The photos were round and smaller sized. The rubber eye cup lens covers in the front are secured with rubber loops while the two eyepiece covers come off the normal way. I don't think there would be much discernible difference at all between these binoculars and the more expensive 42mm binocular brands. I give these a thumbs up for a purchase choice.

title: Quality of the filter and the Truth about Potential counterfeits
text:
[State of counterfeits in December 2021 and how to completely avoid them]
_______________________________________________________________________________________________

This is an extremely high quality, Brass filter. All version of it are Brass.
Using it for the past few days I have seen Zero issues with image sharpness at all, vignetting or distortion.
Its heavy, Solid and extremely smooth to turn.

However, I have noticed that when using this on a step up ring (52mm lens to 58mm filter) the step up ring makes it slightly harder to turn at specific points.
However, that probably say more about the step up ring than this filter.

The F-Pro version reduces about 1 and 1/3rd stops of light. So you can use this as a 1 stop ND filter too.
Other than that the color is amazing, Polarization is amazing and I am extremely happy I paid premium for this over a $20 filter.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________

When it comes to counterfeits. I'd like to point something out for those who are worried.

If you look at all the reviews submitted through Amazon concerning B+W Counterfeit filters.
All of them. And I mean all of them going back almost a decade, are Always related to the
XS-PRO (Slim Mount) version. Not the F-Pro version.

If you are looking to avoid counterfeit B+W filters on Amazon get the F-Pro version.
There are no documented cases of counterfeit F-Pro.
B+W also has an authenticity checker on their website.

Google "Schneider Kreuznach authenticity check".

Keep in mind the country you bought the filter from Amazon on for the authenticity check country.
If you purchased from .De Amazon, select Germany.
If you purchased from .co.uk select UK.
If you purchased from Amazon US select US
etc.

You won't regret spending money on a quality filter like this.

This is one gigantic advert for ROKU - buy, buy, buy. They throw in the TV for free, basically. I just wanted a replacement 32" for my office, and if returning it wasn't more trouble than it's worth - I'd send it back. I've never had to "activate" a TV. If you aren't paying attention - the first page of "free" activation asks you for a credit card. Huh? Just keep hitting "continue" unless you want to open up an avalanche of STUFF. Got a sound bar because all new TVs sound terrible - but still haven't figured out how the optical line out works, because you can't mess with those settings while watching a program. You get taken off line where you guess what settings you need, go back to the program, it doesn't work - rinse repeat. Wound up using the headphone jack out. I could go on and on. The remote is a joke. No volume control? But plenty of buttons for MORE PROGRAMS! Thank goodness my DirecTV remote was able to clone the beast. Want to just fire it up & watch satellite? Forget it - have to go to the "home" menu to access that HDMI port - right next to MORE STUFF.
Look - I know I'm not the demographic for this appliance. I don't need 500,000 programs and movies. I watch the news, sports, an occasional movie. Period. I just wanted a cheap monitor (it's not particularly great at that either unless your eye line is straight into the screen) to plug in my DirecTV HDMI - and god knows I'm already getting soaked enough by those vampires. The bells & whistles were massively inconvenient and time wasting. If you're like me - old, grumpy & haven't watched a frame of a single mini series - spend a couple of extra bucks & get an LG or Samsung "dumb" TV that's a monitor first, and a content fire hose second. If all new TVs are like this - buy a used one. I'm about to get my old Panasonic plasma out of mothballs. God knows what Pandora's box of junk emails & spam I just opened.

title: Solid barebones beginner mechanical keyboard
text:
If you are in the market for a barebones beginner mechanical keyboard with a lot of great features than this is a solid option. It has RGB, hot-swappable switches, and USB C. Despite what others have said in their reviews you can tear it down into its individual pieces. The plate and the board can be separated, you just have to take pry it out of the case first. To do so you'll want to remove all of the screws, including the ones for the spacebar, and then starting with the corners near the spacebar you'll want to pry it out going back and forth until the board is out. It is essentially wedged in there pretty good so you'll want to take your time the first time.

Some other initial impressions to note is that it's quite light compared to some other boards that I have tried. With switches, keycaps, and some foam the board weighs approximately 1lb 5oz. The board does not come with any foam padding, but you can add some if you want to dampen the sound. Finally there aren't any legs to kick out to adjust the angle so I hope you're happy with the default angle which is lower than some of the other boards that I have tried like the Glorious boards.

Pros:
+ Hot-swap switches
+ RGB lighting
+ USB C
+ 5 pin switch compatible

Cons:
- Software
- Poor lube on stabilizers
- No foam
- No height adjustability

title: Waited 16 years for this TV
text: I've wanted a quality HDTV since first they came out in circa 2005 (was it?).  I am a fairly competent tech person, but I don't know a whole lot about TVs, since they're constantly adding new features and such.  I stopped by Best Buy several years ago and described my budget (which was comparatively really low, ~$600 at the time), and they said for my budget, I should get the TCL 6-series.  I didn't have the funds to pick one up so I kept trying to save up for it.  I've been monitoring them since.  I finally got it, and am very pleased.  I made sure to get the 2021 model of the 6-series, which afaict is worth it.  I heard about the H9G, but heard about supposed quality control problems (same but less so with TCL), so far haven't had a problem.  Also the TCL supposedly had better color accuracy, despite having somewhat less peak nits.  I've noticed some of what I think must be blooming with the local array dimming, (but only in pathological shots like title screens and such, not in actual content) and so I don't really care about that.  I like things to be bright and the TV does that.  The biggest thing about Dolby Vision/HDR I've noticed is not that things are bright, which they are, but that they are bright and accurate and realistic.  Dolby Vision gets rid of the banding that you usually get, because they choose the color palette per shot.  This TV certainly has better blacks than say the $150 Onn TV I've had for a while, although it does crush the deepest blacks a bit.  Also the TV looks better from the side than I was led to believe from some reviews.  All in all I am very happy, but I did *not* manage to get the TV (maybe the 2020 model) when it went on sale for $578 or something at Walmart a while ago.  So I had some purchase pain.  The thing is, I *really* don't have a lot of money, and while I am glad I finally got a good TV, it's not without some regret for the price I paid.  That said, it's been nice getting my dream TV.  I had to note that the Onn had better color performance in retrospect than I had initially estimated, although Onn is made by Element I believe and they have ridiculously good color for the price.  The Onn severely crushes many shades of black, and doesn't get as bright, etc, etc.  So if you have the money and want a great TV, then I recommend the TCL 6-series.  Do note, they are coming out with 8K TCL 6-series TVs supposedly later in 2021, you might want to find out what they will charge for those.  I wish I had known that, although tbh, I sometimes can't tell upscaled 2K from 4K, so I doubt 8K is all that necessary (especially at my 55" size).  Very glad I went with the TCL.  I bought from Amazon, but not Amazon ships from and sold by.  Not sure how that worked out.  There was a hole in my package, but the TV seems flawless.  Also, I cannot tell if I won the panel lottery, since I have no basis for comparison (I don't go to stores due to COVID), but I seem to have, and I'm happy about that.  I'm trying to think if there is anything else I should say.  Maybe that finding Dolby Vision content is kinda harder than I expected, although there is plenty of HDR on Youtube and others for instance.  Also note this TV lacks HDR10+ (an open competitor for Dolby Vision (I approve of open standards)), and also cannot do 4K@120Hz, which I don't care about, don't think my RX580 is gonna care.  You do lose HDR at the max 1440p@120Hz.  Not that I have even used that setting or noticed if I did.  The difference between Dolby Vision/HDR10/SDR is there, and I certainly do like it, but if you are super tight on cash, consider getting a good look at it yourself to see if it is worth it to you.  All in all I am super stoked about this purchase.  I cannot recommend this TV enough to those who have the funds.  I really like the TCL.  Interestingly, there have been more foreign media showing up on my Youtube, which is actually kinda nice but a bit mind-bending at the same time, not sure if it's due to encryption certificates or something like that.  Probably not, but I don't have an explanation for it.  Roku is nicer than I expected, but still a bit simplistic.  I perhaps wish there was more customizability, or maybe I just haven't found that section.  Anyway, I'm dweebing...  Take care!

title: Paramount for mining crypto
text:
There weren't any new games that I was enjoying on my RTX 3080 Vision, so I thought I'd play with mining Crypto. My GPU on a HOT summer day on the second floor, where it's not as cool as the first was struggling. Very quickly my GPU was hitting 108 celcius at 83 Mega Hashes. A couple times it hit 110C.
I put these pads on to replace all of the manufacturer ones first. Then I put pads on the back of the memory chips. The backplate is aluminum but it doesn't make contact with the back of the GPU. It actually traps the hot air coming off the back of the modules. and that's the biggest issue. These touch the back of the modules and the back of the backplate. They turn the backplate into a heatsink which is dissipated by the case fans. My temps went down to 90 Celsius and I gained 13 Mega hashes!
Super worth it. I'll be doing this on all future cards whether I mine on them or not.

title: Capable and budget friendly NVR
text:
So, these NVRs have come a long way since the analog DVRs of yesteryear. I already have a few Amcrest cameras and thought I would try this out to see if it was any good.

Surprisingly, the NVR itself is actually very good. Mine shipped with older firmware as well but I updated it to the latest firmware they had for it (May 2020) and it made a huge difference in using the NVR both at the NVR itself and the web interface.

This NVR (and system?) is different from Nest, Arlo, Wyze, and others as it’s very much a DIY product vs. out of the box solution with Cloud storage. The setup I thought was pretty painless. I just popped a hard drive into the chassis and went through the on-screen setup wizard with the included mouse and I was off and running. The cool part about is that it will search for and allow you to add the cameras during the setup wizard – no manually adding the IP addresses of your cameras as it will find them for you – pretty slick!

Speaking of hard drives. The NVR seems pretty tolerant of the drives you put in it. To start, I first tried a Western Digital “Blue” desktop drive. No issues. Then, I tried (and am currently using) a 5TB Seagate Desktop drive that I shucked out of an external hard drive case. Not sure how long it will last, but at any rate, I would recommend using any drive rated for security camera usage

iOS app and notifications
The Amcrest app (Amcrest ViewPro - iOS) is okay and notifications work quite well. I found that the notifications were on par with both my Nest Outdoor cam and Wyze cam when there was activity – surprisingly very few false notifications. I didn’t even have the notification area configured and it worked quite well out of the box – I would feel pretty confident that if I were to configure a set area it would send me notifications when there was motion. Inside of the NVR, it shows you a picture that the camera sees with a bunch of “cells” that you can highlight and have it only look for motion in those areas.

Additionally, what I forgot to mention earlier is during the wizard helps you set up your NVR for access outside of your home by having you scan a QR code with the Amcrest ViewPro app. It will create what is called a Peer-To-Peer connection to the NVR so no opening up ports in your home router – that part was super easy and works pretty well as far as I can tell.

When you receive and tap on a notification (and there are several options to decide what a motion notification does when you tap on it).

It will take you to the motion even but it adds 10-15 seconds of recording prior to the event itself. I found this a bit cumbersome – but otherwise functional. Finding previous motion events and recording in the app itself was pretty cumbersome in general – so I would recommend only using the NVR itself or the web interface to look at recordings.

This NVR and most Amcrest cameras are actually a re-brand from a company called Dahua – and because of that, you can use Dahua’s programs and apps to interact with Amcrest devices. So, when I’m at home I like to use the Dahua iOS app called “DMSS” which allows you to scroll through your motion events in a list (with a small preview) and tap on them to see the event.

I hope the Amcrest ViewPro app follows suit as this is a better way to find motion events when using your mobile device. The DMSS app will not work with a Peer-To-Peer connection outside of your home so when I’m away I use the Amcrest ViewPro app to connect to my NVR.

Motion Events and Downloading Recordings
Finding motion events is pretty easy. The NVR will highlight the motion events with blocks of yellow. These blocks are present on the NVR itself and the web interface.

However, downloading motion events and recordings is different.
This is an area where I actually ran into some trouble but it gave me the opportunity to engage Amcrest Support via email. (Quick note on support – someone did reply to my inquiry and it seemed it was roughly 24 hours between replies back and forth over e-mail which I thought was fine.)

Prior to updating the firmware on my NVR, I was able to download videos via the web interface, but after updating the option where you specify a start time and end time disappeared.

I worked with their support and ultimately it was suggested that I use the desktop client. In this scenario, I ended up using the Dahua version of the desktop client called “SmartPSS” and using that to download my videos. There is an Amcrest version but I couldn’t get it to work. You can download the videos directly from the NVR itself but they will download in a “.dav” format which requires a proprietary player to see. If you use the desktop client you can download your videos in a “.MP4” format which is a more standard format and will play on almost any device. I really hope in the future Amcrest will fix/add the option to download the videos from the web interface.

Downloading the videos from the desktop client is pretty painless. For more information on how to do this, I would recommend watching this video on YouTube. It’s from an account called “Auckland Security Cameras” and the video is called “How To Playback and Export CCTV Video Using SmartPSS”. The video does a good job of showing you how to use the software to find and download videos from your Amcrest NVR.

In the video description, it has an “extra note” which says the following: “EXTRA NOTE: Pause this video at 2:14 and you'll see a 1 hour default time span which will show up when you click the scissors the 2nd time. Grab the red right edge and drag it to the left so you only get the minute or 2 that you're after.”

As a tip – you may need to “zoom-out” on the timeline to see the ending mark for your video you’re trying to download.

Performance
I currently have (2) 4K cameras recording at full resolution at 15 FPS and (1) 5MP camera recording full resolution at 20FPS and the NVR doesn’t seem to mind. The NVR has a bandwidth monitor of sorts that allows you to see the available bandwidth and how much the cameras are using. In this case – it says I have 88Mbps of bandwidth available and with the 3 cameras, it's sitting at around 66Mbps left so I would feel confident adding a couple of others without issue. I did notice though – when playing back on all channels one of the cameras didn’t and in the frame, it said “Outside of decode ability”. This is fine – because I don’t think I’ll be searching more than one camera at a time anyways.

A quick note on web browsers
When using Chrome the NVR asks you to install a Chrome Application called “Amcrest Web View”. The application works fine but I also found it works just as well without the plugin/application inside of Firefox, Opera, or Edge.

Summary
Overall – solid NVR for money if you’re aware of the limitations.

Notifications work great and I’m pretty darn satisfied with the cost/usability balance. Sure, there are systems that are easier to use and setup – but will cost you at least double what you’d spend on the cameras and NVR, and probably have cloud access fees. This one – no cloud fees, and the cameras are super affordable and would easily allow you to keep an eye on your home or business.

title: Meh sound but great for emergencies.
text:
I picked this up to keep in my backpack just in case. I already have an earlier analog style of the same radio that I really enjoy, so I wanted to check out the “new improved” version.
I won’t go into detail on all the features, just the standouts and what I feel is lacking.
First- the lights are outstanding! The flashlight competes with any I’ve had camping while the reading light illuminates an entire room. Thankfully both lights have a dim setting as well as crazy bright. This is a welcome upgrade from some emergency radios that feature sad little lights you couldn’t use to change a tire, much less see your way through a dark house or woods.
The digital display allows you to tune directory onto a station although sadly, the tiny antenna fails to pull in some local fm stations that any mediocre radio should get.
On to sound quality- it seems that the “upgrade” to this radio included a smaller speaker as this sounds much tinnier than my earlier analog radio manufactured by the same company. This unit does include an earphone plug and the sound is lovely through headphones. I value the upgrade mainly for the large capacity rechargeable battery and the backlit digital display as well as the weather alert feature. While not perfect, this radio has the features I need and is a good addition to my emergency kit, on that basis I recommend it.

title: Works beautifully with modern MacBook Pros
text:
The first unit I received was defective. It only took chatting with Kensington's technical support staff for about ten minutes for them to determine that the unit was behaving unusually, and they advised me to return it immediately. Amazon came through with a replacement in a couple of days.

The second unit has worked better than any other Thunderbolt dock I've tried with my 2020-era MacBook Pro 16" computers. It wakes the computer upon input from a connected keyboard or mouse, the computer recognizes and adjusts to a connected monitor properly and consistently, and—best of all—the dock will drive my LG 38WN95C-W monitor at a resolution of 3840x2160 at not only 60Hz, but also 75Hz, 120Hz, and 144Hz. That it also has a power button to turn the unit off is a nice touch.

I'd change a few things about the design if I could. First, the lights that come on when the unit is powered on are quite bright; I'd like it better if they flashed a few times, or stayed on only long enough to indicate the current state, and then went dim or turned off entirely. Also, I'd prefer that the Thunderbolt port for the cable that connects to the computer was not on the front of the unit, but instead on the back or, even better, on the side. This port layout is shared by at least two other docks released recently: the OWC Thunderbolt Dock and the Sonnettech Echo 11 Thunderbolt 4 Dock. We'll have to blame the OEM supplying the board inside for this design.

title: Best value UST on the market
text:
Overall this is an exceptional short throw projector for those that have the space and are thinking of getting rid of their TV. Straight out of the box, product quality is clear to see. It feels like a high-end piece of equipment, which for $2000+ it is, but in the land of ultra short throws it really isn't. I've never had a VAVA to compare it to but I know it's more compact and a nicer looking box. Everything feels quality.

One small thing, is I wish it had a source button on the remote, so that I didn't have to access my Fire TV through the menus.

I used this on a plain white wall and I have to say picture quality was excellent. You do get a wave at the top though if you have any imperfections in your wall. No way near as unwatchable and scary as people led me to believe with these delicate lasers though. My wall is very uneven and the picture was still exceptional. Colors pop, brightness really good. It's nowhere near as bright as the Bomaker Polaris, but that thing is like the sun when it starts up - practically blinds you. Sound through my soundbar was good also, and plenty good enough without.

Make no mistake, this is an excellent projector and generally available for at least $500 less than the VAVA so I think it's the better buy.

The real thing that tips it over the edge though is the customer service. OUTSTANDING!
Unlike Bomaker, who never replied to my messages, the guys and girls at Wemax are just on it.
They reply super fast, are extremely knowledgable and hunt down answers to questions they don't know, like their lives depended on it. Honestly, I've never been more impressed with customer service than this one. Which is a huge concern when buying high-tech equipment. VAVA responded to my questions too, but nothing like these guys. They were superheroes. It's also great to know that were something to go wrong, I can send it off to them in the US (I believe California) and they will repair it and ship it back free of charge. No sending it over to China to get it fixed, no uncertainty, no costs. That's huge.

In short, a few little nitpicky things. The remote as I said, woulda been nice to have a few more customisable options in terms of picture settings.

But for sheer plug-in and play this thing is a beast.

You won't be disappointed!

title: Good quality Pure Sinewave UPS. Reasonable option if you need Pure Sinewave functionality
text:
[[VIDEOID:5ab3e5384ca489fec86a9143a941f1f7]] Uninterrupted Power Supplies (UPS) have been around for quite a while. But it's only in the past few years that a class termed "Pure Sinewave" UPSes have appeared at the consumer level. They are typically priced at more than 2x the cost of a standard UPS with the same power. So the first question is: Do you need one?

Well, there's a good chance you don't. You see, the power produced by a UPS--which is only produced when the line power goes out--is typically only an approximation of the sinewave that you'd get with the AC coming out of the wall. Think of it as trying to draw a curved line using only horizontal and vertical lines. No matter how careful you are, it will look somewhat blocky. A "pure sinewave" UPS will output a curve that, even under magnification, looks very smooth. The electronics required to do this are more expensive, and, hence, these UPSes cost more.

But do you need it? The answer, for most people, is "no." Most electronics will function just fine with the "blocky" type of approximate sinewave electricity produced by inexpensive UPSes. There are some high-end PC power supplies that don't work properly without a pure sinewave source. And some super high-efficiency appliances (e.g., 90% efficient "green" appliances) can make use of the characteristics of a pure sinewave in a manner that they don't work properly otherwise. But if you're simply looking for a power supply to power your laptop or normal desktop PC when the power goes out, you probably don't need a pure sine wave UPS. Go get a 1500 VA / 1100W standard UPS for less than half the price, and you'll be all set.

But let's say you DO need a pure sinewave UPS? How is this one?

Bottom line: It's very good. First off, because it's not indicated anywhere in the listing: This is made by CyberPower for Amazon. CyberPower has been in the UPS business for more than two decades. They know what they're doing. Typically, they are considered to be real competition for APC (the other big name in home UPS) in the home market.

The UPS features a small CD panel with navigation buttons in the front. ON the back are 8 three-pronged outlets, four of which are UPS backup protected and four of which merely offer surge protection.

You can connect the UPS to your computer. You install PowerMaster+ software to control the UPS. While you can set some options from the LCD panel, it is FAR FARE easier to use the software on the computer. The PowerMaster+ software can also instruct the UPS to shut down your PC in an orderly fashion if the power goes out (to avoid disk crashes, etc.). PowerMaster+ software is available for Windows (10/8/7/Server 2016/Server 2012/Server 2019/Hyper-V Server 2012), macOS (10.14/10.15), and Linux (Red hat Enterprise 8 and 7, Centos 7+, Debian 10.1 & 9, Ubuntu 10.04, Citrix XenServer 7.2 and Hypervisor 8.0). The software is not included in the package--you'll need to download it. (As always, check the latest compatibility before purchase).

The USB-A cable required to connect the UPS to your PC is included in the box, along with an instruction manual.

NOTE: No instructions are given on how to do the initial setup. The UPS will ship with the battery cable disconnected. You must connect the battery cable before it will work. I have attached a video that demonstrates how to do this. It isn't hard, and shouldn't take more than 5 minutes.

The UPS weighs about 60 pounds. That's not too much for a strong person to carry, but if you aren't a strong person you may want to enlist help. Once you have the battery connected, you simply plug the UPS into a wall, and then plug the devices you want to connect to the UPS to the outlets on the back. My unit came with batteries that were ~100% charged out of the box.

In operation, when power is normally being provided from the wall, the UPS is silent. Testing the UPS by disconnecting the wall outlet I found the following:

A) It provided immediate switch over to battery power and the attached devices did not even flicker
B) Under load, there is a whir noise from a fan, as well as an indicator beep (beep can be silenced in settings). This was all typical and reasonable for UPSes.

On the whole, this is a decent UPS that offers pure sinewave output. While not everyone will need pure sinewave output, those owning high end PCs with special power supplies may. Those seeking to use this as a backup to sensitive devices (medical, etc.) may also need this functionality. Compared to other UPSes that offer pure sinewave output, this unit is competitively priced, and has the advantage of being backed directly by Amazon.

title: This little guy just helped save my $3k USD PC, but I am replacing it.

Before the power went out, the lights in my house were flickering like crazy, and then after we did lose power, we had two surges where the power momentarily came back on before going out again. This all happened within such a short period of time, that I didn't get the chance to shut my PC down, switch off the power supply or surge protector, or unplug the surge protector from the wall. While I'm certain this surge protector did save my PC, I'm also fairly certain that it needs replacing, and admittedly, I'm going with a Tripp Lite this time around since they're tried in true in the IT industry. Plus, Tripp Lite offers a pretty substantial warranty / insurance policy. (I've been using Tripp Lites for years now in the IT realm and I definitely trust them more). However, this little Witeem will work in a pinch if you need a cheap surge protector, or need multiple but don't wanna shell out twice the coin for "nicer" heavier duty ones.

title: Echo compatible?  Not 100% true. UPDATED: No Notifications & Blink now charging $$$
text:
****** UPDATE PLEASE READ: After having the Echo Show 5 and Blink Mini camera working perfectly as a puppy monitor, it basically quit working. Let me explain. I used the Show/Blink setup to notify me when my puppy would wake up at night so we could let her out to do her business. It worked well (almost too well) by sending Alexa notifications to both my iPhone and the Echo Show. I eventually turned the notifications off on my phone because I didn't need two things waking me up at 3am. Again it worked for a while, then just out of the blue, it stopped notifying me through Echo Show. I tried everything to get it working again, but I was forced to start using my iPhone notifications instead. Echo Show would still let me view the camera "Echo show me Bella", but no notifications when she would move. Echo Show became almost useless since I can also view the camera from my phone (and also speak to my pup which Show never could do). Mind you, it has been taking 30 second video clips and storing them on my phone. I got a couple that were YT worthy for their entertainment value (search Bella the Corgi).

I put up with the notification issue until BLINK PULLED A FAST ONE ON ME!!! A little over a month ago, I got a notification on my phone that my "30 Day Premium Blink Trial" had begun. I did not sign up for the trial, so I thought nothing of it. The other day my trial expired. I went into my phone to look at the stored videos and now they all are LOCKED!!! When I click on them Blink app tells me I need to subscribe to their service!!!! WHAT??!!!!??

Now the Echo Show and Blink Mini are all but USELESS to me except to notify me on my phone when my puppy moves at night. Echo Show's notifications are gone, and NOW Blink will not record. The whole point of the security camera is to record!! If I were to point my camera at my mail box to catch mail thieves, it would be absolutely WORTHLESS now since I'd have to be at the ready to view it live. Anything not live is locked up and held for ransom by Blink.

Amazon (who also owns Blink) is getting greedier by the day. Shame on you for taking away the basic functionalities that I bought it for in the first place!
******************

Using the blink app on iOS you can use the "Talk" button to talk through the camera, however, this is NOT possible when using Echo show (5" latest version) that is bundled together with this camera.

title: I apologize to Manufacturer, Vendor and Amazon
text: This sound bar was packaged well and had no indications of being used or marred in any way. Everything looked like new. Setup was a breeze and only took minutes. Loved all the input selection choices that it has. One drawback that I noticed quickly was that the LCD display on the remote would washout depending on the angle it was viewed at and in a dim or dark room it couldn't be read at all. Since the sound bars operation was to be programmed into the cable remote that was a minor concern. The sound was very good. I say "was" because I sent the item back. As this was my first sound bar I ever owned I had an issue with the audio dropping after a few hours. I spent hours researching, turning off eco mode on both the bar and remote, going in and turning off TV power saving settings, changing inputs, I thought I tried everything. It wasn't until a few weeks later, after I had purchased a different model, that I realized that the issue was my cable box. Apparently it has a power saving feature that cannot be accessed or changed from the menu. I never ran into this issue because as long as you are using the remote while watching TV it doesn't happen. However, when you tune to a music station at night to go to sleep it goes into power saver after 4 hours of no interaction. This is some stupid TiVo thing. If I play music via Pandora  it plays all night without issue. If I try to save data by playing a Music Choice station it powers off after 4 hours. How dumb is that. So, basically I returned something thinking it was defective which is why I apologize to all involved. I hate returning things especially if it isn't broken. All I can offer is that if I need another sound bar I would gladly purchase this one again.

title: Beats My Old Sony Walkman
text:
I purchased the V112 to replace my old Sony Walkman radio. The old Sony was developing a problem with it's headphone jack making the audio intermittent. Plus, I was replacing the triple A batteries about every 1 1/2 months. That wasn't a big deal but over the course of two years the batteries would cost me more than the cost of the Retekess.

I like the V112 because it is light, compact and well built despite it's plastic feel. It is rechargeable. The programming is easy and stores more stations than I need. Plus this pocket radio has better static free reception. I listen to mostly AM radio.

This pocket radio got only a 4 star rating and not a 5 star because the audio quality it not as good as the Sony. Using several different headphones on each the Sony and the Retekess, I found the sound to be much more warm on the Sony. I did this both at home and while walking.

In summary, the Retekess comes in better in operation in just about every category over the old Sony Walkman but the sound quality is not as pleasing to the ear.

title: Somewhat easy setup/not that easy
text:
I fought with setting up the two cameras I purchased for about 3 and a half hours. I contemplated sending them back nearly 10 times in my head, luckily I'm persistent. When setting up the camera, they would not connect to the router. Didn't matter how many times I repeated the same exact connection process, via their manual. I had to then assess my router to see if it was the problem. I even updated the firmware on my router during this process. Everytime I would enter my password, it wouldn't be able to go around the security. What ended up happening was I had to remove ALL security on my router, just letting it raw-dog connectivity. Once all security was removed it then connected to the router. I then went through the process of enabling security back onto the router, using the SAME EXACT PASSWORD as before. Then the Cameras would connect to the secure connection. Absolutely makes no sense why it wouldn't, and then why it would work. I couldn't find any information on the forums about it, so I figured I would post this here in case someone else has the same problem.

The cameras work really well for the price. I have one mounted very far from my router. It had difficulty picking up the wifi signal for a while, but as time has gone by it does connect every time. The mounting screws that were provided are complete trash. Upgrade those bad-boys before you install. The screws will snap. Ask me how I know.

The night vision works well as described. About 20 or so feet from the camera you can still see pretty good. I have the one with the spotlight on it... which i think the normal night vision, you have further visibility than with the spotlight enabled.

In order to have playback, you will need an SD card. They're rather cheap. Just buy them now and not put it off. No sense in climbing that ladder more than once.

Last thing, here is a fun fact. You can enable a motion detection alarm to sound whenever movement is detected. You can also record your own voice to act as an alarm. Mine happens to say, "NOT TODAY SATAN, NOT TODAY!"

title: Unbelievable Customer Service
text:
On 12/03/2021, this was the highest rated USB 3.0 hub on the Amazon website with a 4.7 and 80% 5-stars. I made all my Amazon purchases based on ratings and price - always looking for the "best buy."
.
These user measures were no guarantees for quality and durability, especially USB 3.0 hubs. I have purchased almost every reasonably price and highly recommended model through the years. All proved defective between 1.5 to 13 months. Devices failed to read; read/write speed became unbearably slow; and ports went ON and OFF sporadically. Reliability and long life span were inherent problems with this class of tech products.
.
Is the WENTER an exception? For now, the hub does not exhibit any of the above mentioned problems. So, we shall see for the next few months, when it is put to the test. When issues come, I will update this evaluation.
.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
.

This is my 2nd pair. I had them for about a year before my dog chewed on my first set. Then I tried the T12s. They were ok. They did not feel as comfortable in my ear nor could I hear the bass in songs like I used to. I listen to a lot of drum n bass, so I have to hear the lows! 😊
I see the reviews about their buds falling out. It just means your ear holes are big, so you have to test out the other size ear pieces. I changed to the biggest set so they create a kind of suction? and I can hear the most bass when they're sitting a little further from the ear canal. You have to follow the directions of initial placement and then turn them to get the right fit.
Talking: I don't have a problem, but these buds pick up everything. You can't talk with the window down while driving. My friends can tell when I'm washing the dishes or blowdrying my hair. 😂

I got another pair for work so I can block out my coworkers. The noise cancelling is excellent. 😉

Overall, I'm very happy these earbuds and I haven't had any issues with them like other reviewers. I've bought four sets so far. I haven't encountered any "lemon" earbuds.

title: Great low cost option
text:
[[VIDEOID:142f06cc78f8cdd8b6551ec5f8d8ab60]] The picture quality was quite impressive for the price. Did a comparison between this and the vava short throw. To be honest most people will be happy with either one. The only difference showed when they were set up side by side.

Picture quality.
Both are excellent. The image quality of the wemax was slightly cleared. But the colors on the vava were more vivid. The colors could be adjusted to match if you want to take the time to do so. I did not. The unit I had wouldn't focus the upper left corner of the screen. It was minimal but that was where the title showed up and the blurry annoyed me. Otherwise the contrast was good. We were casting on a painted wall for the comparison.

Sound
The vava was way better in this area. The wemax was good enough. For our use it will have external audio. So sound didn't matter. The wemax speak is more than enough for most basements or living rooms.

Size
The vava is bigger and heavier by far. We need a unit for ceiling mount. The vava is considerably bigger and heavier not just a little.

Remote
It works. Directional pad and a couple buttons. I like that it's bluetooth to no need to find an ir receiver.

Interface
Wemax has android over whatever they are calling the software on the vava. However in true android bugginess we were not able to get to the onscreen menu after it did an update. That was very annoying. It's kind of hard to adjust the screen colors if it turns off the picture to show you the adjustments. They aside. It was android tv so it did the job of housing your apps and allowing you to cast to it.

Warranty
Only has a 1 year limit, while vava is offering a 2 year repair / replace warranty.

Customer service
I'm not sure who to fault for this. We tried to exchange the unit due to the unfocused upper left corner I mentioned earlier. Amazon said no exchanges so we had to return in. It took weeks of calls to amazon to get our money back. We were never directed to contact the seller so I really can't put this on them. Because of the hassle we are apprehensive about buying another especially since it only has a 1 year warranty.

title: Successful install 870EVO ssd in Lenovo Thinkcentre desktop !
text:
I'm no geek, but I did it. I downloaded the Samsung data migration software, and watched numerous
online videos. There is a wealth of info in them. Some of it useful. As instructed, I installed the drive
using the cabling I purchased seperately as an ssd install kit from Inatek co.

Once the cloning was complete, I wanted to make the SSD my boot drive. Many approaches to doing
that. I went online and found a video by a Scotsman that was very informative. I had already cloned
my old hard drive onto my ssd, so I had no need for taking the precautions he suggested.

The nugget of the video was the explanation that now I could remove the old drive, and use the original
power wire, and sata connection to power and operate the new SSD. Which I did !

I turned the computer off and disconnected the AC cord, removed the old drive, and connected the SSD
in it's place.

Plugged the AC back in, and hit the power button, and It booted flawlessly !

So far so good, but I'm not going to overwrite (reformat) my old drive. It is my insurance against any
software mishap. my new drive is 1TB, my old was 500 gig.
I wish I had known that disconnecting the old drive automatically resolves boot issues.

There may be instructions to that effect, but I missed them.

UPDATE! : Had I read the instructions included in the product features, by scrolling down the main
page, I would have seen the words "UPGRADE WITH EASE", and the 2 steps to do so !
Step 1: clone the old drive to new ssd using migration software, and step 2: swap in new drive for old
and boot !
I was too hasty .

title: Tested the TUK against klipsch 5's and Audio Engine HD6.  One TUK to rule them all!
text:
Not a bluetooth speaker, not a hi-fi system but something in-between. I tested out the TUK vs the Klipsch 5's and the Audio Engine HD6 - and liked the TUK most of all. I tested them with a turntable, bluetooth, and USB connected to a laptop streaming high-res files from amazon music HD.

Klipsch 5's -- Bass was loose and rambling and just way too loud. At low to moderate volumes, they sounded good. Attached to a Audio Technica LP60 turntable, the Klipsch 5's sounded better than the TUK when using the Klipsch's built in phono amp. Overall the Klipsch's did just OK on vocals and brass instruments. The fives look really good. After I returned them, it seemed like I maybe needed to update the firmware to allow for a different bass settings --- these things should have some tone control built in.

TUK -- These really sounded pretty descent. Very clear, and the bass was far more musical than the Klipsch. The ribbon tweeters had a high-end quality to them. At high volumes, the TUK started to wear out. The phono amp was good, but maybe a small notch behind the Klipsch, as the klipsch had a nice "warmness" to them. I did NOT try to pair these with a Sub, but doing so would have made these an awesome little stereo. If you live in an apartment having these with a sub connected to a TV plus a turntable would make you very happy. My comments above don't quite tell the whole story, but the TUK's (in my opinion), are a real step up from the Klipsch's and the audio engine hd6.

Audio Engine HD6. These also sounded good, but lack a phono amp. After many hours of listening, I decided that these are meant to a computer speaker that you don't crank up much. Sound quality was just below the TUK's from what I could judge. They lacked much of a soundstage.

TUK's are great speakers enough to fill most living rooms. Just wish they looked a little cooler.

BTW - I ended up spending $5K on a somewhat more proper hifi system. For simple set-ups, I would suggest either the TUK at 799 plus the sub for 289 for $1,100 spring 2021 or the KEF ls50 W for $2,500 and see if high-res streaming works for you on the KEF's.

(I did not include the KEF's in my write up. since the above three are at a similar price point)

title: I still prefer SONY Walkman simplicity though pricey and features reduced
text:
After 35 years of owning Walkmans, some thoughts on the Sony E394 compared to earlier models mentioned in comments and questions.

I many ways, this review mirrors the one that I wrote for the E395 (a black, 16GB model - pictures which I am using again) that is no longer available from Sony and whose product page is no longer on Amazon. There were numerous comments suggesting failure of the front buttons. Sure enough, after a year, the front controls on mine began to become unreliable as well. For example, pressing the play/pause button to pause a song would send one into a completely different section of the menu hierarchy. I still use that one in my vehicle where the Walkman's controls are turned over, via usb, to the vehicle's touchscreen. Anyway, those, it seems, have been ditched, by SONY and let's see how this 8GB red model holds up.

Playlists and transfer of files:

There are many of us that prefer to organize our pictures and music manually by creating folders and via the "drag and drop" of files, rather than depending on an app such as iTunes or Windows Media. I put my files in folders and use the "folder" option at the "very" bottom of the Walkman's music menu. It plays all the songs in that folder and you can rename the files with a number in front of the file name if "forcing" a particular song play order is important thus, no lost playlists and no proprietary software required. The Sony Walkman is a master at simply appearing as another drive on the computer. If you so decide, create and put your own individual folders, which now can also serve as playlists, in the music folder of the Walkman. Just another option.

Reduced features:

Sony has, indeed, removed many features from the Walkman. Most of these features, along with the video ability probably will not be missed on a bike ride, jog, or exercising.

Menus:

Navigating the E394 is simple and intuitive. The new E394 seems a little slower moving through menu functions and between songs. Sony decided to add a "browse by album cover" feature. The album art is not displayed very well. Unless you have memorized, visually, the album art itself or you have less than, say, a dozen or so albums, this, it seems to me, is not a useful feature.

Build quality:

The build quality is certainly less "jewel" like, but I think its lighter weight might just make it less susceptible to damage if dropped. The controls are sensitive, but the return of the outside "hold" switch is nice. Power it down and set the hold which prevents it from accidentally being turned on. To turn it on, it's one step, just release the hold switch, the unit turns on immediately (no more long double press and wait). Sadly, unlike its immediate predecessor, the front controls on the E394 are now flat (lack relief) again making it difficult to find the controls by feel.

Volume:

The volume control is now back out on the side. I like this as you can adjust the volume while songs are playing and you are browsing other menus. The volume with the enclosed earbuds is fine. In fact, at higher volumes, it is uncomfortably loud. It also works fine with my BOSE noise cancelling headset as well. Your volume, of course, will depend, in part, on the impedance of your headset. Turn off the Bass Boost. Play with the equalizer settings including the custom function.

Vehicle use:

Using it in the car has two options. On my vehicle it is recognized via usb and I can use the vehicle touchscreen or steering wheel, etc.. If your vehicle does not recognize it, use the 3.5mm headphone jack to enter the vehicle's aux input. This also allows you to use all the menu functions of the actual Walkman as well however, no longer hands free. If you want to charge your Walkman simultaneously, use the vehicle's 12v power outlet and a USB power converter with a usb A to micro usb cord. (I've attached photos of both setups). The latest Walkman has the Android type micro usb. Buy a 12v usb power adapter, a short male to male 3.5mm headphone cord, and, if needed, a usb A to micro usb charging cord (I often use a muti function retractable unit).

https://www.amazon.com/AmazonBasics-Dual-Port-Charger-Adapter-Android/dp/B072C7R4CD/ref=sr_1_1_sspa?crid=3LX3WSZ7D8WL5&dchild=1&keywords=12v+usb+adapter+car&qid=1623378704&sprefix=12v+usb+ad%2Caps%2C151&sr=8-1-spons&psc=1&spLa=ZW5jcnlwdGVkUXVhbGlmaWVyPUExRDZDQjdXWjk4RENVJmVuY3J5cHRlZElkPUEwNTgzNTMyTzQzVkdHT1RXQVlIJmVuY3J5cHRlZEFkSWQ9QTA1NzE4NjFVTE9XOTVMMkxRV1Amd2lkZ2V0TmFtZT1zcF9hdGYmYWN0aW9uPWNsaWNrUmVkaXJlY3QmZG9Ob3RMb2dDbGljaz10cnVl

https://www.amazon.com/AmazonBasics-Male-Micro-Cable-Black/dp/B07232M876/ref=sr_1_3?crid=VMVR1BHUUP0Y&dchild=1&keywords=usb+a+to+micro+usb+cord&qid=1623378877&sprefix=usb+a+to+micro+usb+cord%2Celectronics%2C150&sr=8-3

https://www.amazon.com/ASICEN-Retractable-Lightning-Charging-Blackberry/dp/B074CW4QTQ/ref=pd_ybh_a_23?_encoding=UTF8&psc=1&refRID=JJ842ZFMMZD96R60VG3W

https://www.amazon.com/AmazonBasics-3-5mm-Stereo-Audio-Cable/dp/B00NO73IN2/ref=pd_sim_23_6?_encoding=UTF8&pd_rd_i=B00NO73MUQ&pd_rd_r=9fc115b9-a661-11e8-a85b-ad9aadebc9ee&pd_rd_w=2Gfj4&pd_rd_wg=UOtpa&pf_rd_i=desktop-dp-sims&pf_rd_m=ATVPDKIKX0DER&pf_rd_p=a180fdfb-b54e-4904-85ba-d852197d6c09&pf_rd_r=BN7ADAD5G9D3TSDY1S7J&pf_rd_s=desktop-dp-sims&pf_rd_t=40701&refRID=BN7ADAD5G9D3TSDY1S7J&th=1

All my old Walkmans are still operational, though some barely, and the new E394 suits its purpose for me if one wants a unit with physical controls, rather than a touch screen, and prefers "flash drive" type file management to carry around working, exercising, etc. rather than risking damage to a $1000 (or more) phone, and also wants to pass on the battery killing bluetooth with the sketchy connectivity and poor sound generally found in this price range. There is still a market for low cost mp3 players. There are plenty of them out there but, though cheaper, all seem to have reviews for functionality or reliability no better or most of them worse than this SONY.

Hope this helps.

title: A Worthwhile Addition
text:
Before purchasing the SPDIF Purifier 2, I read the company website's information, reviews from internet enthusiast websites, enthusiast magazine reviews posted on the internet, and some posted opinions by people who had actually purchased the product. The buzzwords used in the company's website may excite the imaginations of audiophiles but I wouldn't blame a soul for being skeptical. The thirty day trial period offered by Amazon meant that I could get a realistic in home opportunity to judge whether it would be money well spent so I finally fired up the credit card and took a chance.

The Purifier 2 is described as restoring the digital information to proper form before it goes into your DAC. In my two channel system, modest as it is, it certainly made a difference. The most obvious improvement is that it lowers the noise floor of my system. That makes the presentation of the sound stage bigger from top to bottom, left to right, and front to back. Vocal harmonies and instrumental duets become distinctly separate. Instruments occupy their own space. The dynamic range or the limitations of dynamics in a recording are better defined. The decay of notes are more distinct and longer, particularly cymbals which will seem to shimmer more than before. Even if you've only played "air drums", percussion instruments are easier to follow. Bass notes became better defined and tighter, more "punchy" if you will.

I suggest that a Purifier 2 makes more sense as a value purchase to improve digital playback a good system than adding a new digital cable. The point of diminishing returns shows up sooner in digital cable applications. If the signal is polluted to begin with, no amount of copper or silver conductor is going to achieve very much other than draining your wallet.

Those who are fortunate enough to afford CD players or DACs with the same features as the Purifier 2 don't need one. Everyone else should consider whether or not to take advantage of the thirty day trial and see for themselves if it makes a positive difference.

title: Looks great but has serious flaws
text:
First, like many of you working from home, I purchased this keyboard to complete a home office setup. My primary use case is for work related typing. I connect to my laptop via a Bluetooth connection. I completed my setup with the Seenda illuminated wireless mouse.

Pros: Sturdy, rigid construction in a beautiful space grey finish. Cosmetics are appealing and build quality is of solid construction. Switch keys are low profile, require minimal travel and are great for those that prefer these types of keys.

Cons: My biggest complaint with this keyboard are the connection issues with my laptop. The connection is made via Bluetooth however my daily routine requires me to remove the device from my device manager (Windows) and re-pair the keyboard. I do this no less than 4 times a day. This is extremely frustrating and disruptive as I primarily use this keyboard for work related typing.

My second biggest complaint is that there are times when certain keys will 'stick' and result in an unintended string of characters such as thissssssssssssssss. Again, for work related typing this is completely unacceptable and is especially concerning when I am typing numbers. I work in a finance capacity where 'fat fingering' an extra digit or 8 can have serious implications. I have contacted Seenda's support team and they have advised me to remove any devices that may be interfering with the Bluetooth connection. Not easily accomplished but even after removing all things electronic and/or built with metal components I still experienced this issue with BOTH the keyboard and mouse (also connected via Bluetooth). For these two main reasons, I cannot recommend this keyboard as a reliable tool for work use. Other cons include the low brightness of the RGB backlight as many of you have also mentioned, the battery run time especially when RGB colors are activated, and minor gripes with oily smudges on the keys after little use.

I really wanted to like this keyboard but unfortunately I will need to replace it with something more reliable. My issues could solely be with my unit in which case I would gladly be willing to give Seenda another try.

title: 48v Lithium Battery Torched it!
text:
I'm building a go-kart for my grandsons with twin 2000watt 48v BLDC motors. I need 5 volts to power an esp8266 that will provide a speed governor, monitor battery voltage and so on. I was hoping to use this Step-Down Buck Converter to get the 5 volts. HOWEVER, a fully charged 48v lithium battery puts out 54 volts and when I connected that voltage to this converter it torched it.

Just to be sure I connected another converter to a 12-volt LifePO4 battery and it works great. Then, of course, I connected that converter to the big 48v battery and torched it, too.

One issue - The converter has very nice screw terminals for AC line input. However, DC input is just two small holes that are only accessible from the bottom of the board. They are labelled Vi+ and Vi-. Not a showstopper but a small hassle to solder wires into these holes.

So - When Amazon description says, "DC 5V-50V" That means NOT 54 Volts!

title: Halfway incompatible with Lenovo ThinkBook
text:
I bought this device to connect 2 external monitors to my laptop for an at-home work station. I wanted to make the 3 displays (2 monitors + 1 laptop screen) extend across each other.

To start, this product does allow for this, which is a huge plus since a lot of these types of devices don't seem to offer the 'extend' capabilities. It also has USB-A and C ports for a wireless mouse, keyboard, etc. Instructions aren't needed as everything is pretty self-explanatory.

Aside from simply existing and somewhat functioning, however, this device is a dud. I've used it now for about 2 weeks and every single day there is at least 1 time when the adapter loses connection and all of my screens go black. Then everything I had opened across the 3 screens gets shoved onto my laptop screen as the other 2 monitors reset their connection to the adapter. It is very annoying, and there are no easy/cosmetic ways to fix it, as it appears to be an internal problem with one of the connecting cords.

Another problem is that it does not work well with wireless mouse or keyboards. When I connected both my mouse and keyboard to the adapter, there was very noticeable lag in both devices to the point that made it unusable. I would type a sentence and only half of the letters would be recognized, and they would only show up on the screen about 15 seconds I had pressed the buttons. The mouse also lagged so much that I might as well have tried moving the cursor with my mind.

In any case, I will be returning this and getting a different adapter from a different company. I may just fork up the extra money and buy a quality hub from an established retailer.

title: Gorgeous image quality, no freezing or other glitches
text: After trying and returning the Sony X700 and X800M2 because of freezing problems, I bit the bullet and spent a little more for the Panasonic. So far, I have used it about 50 hours watching 4k disks, standard blu-rays, and older DVDs. No freezing problems. Fairly fast loading and quiet operation. There are two drawbacks to be aware of, neither of which affect performance and picture quality. The remote is poorly arranged and not backlit. It's very easy to accidentally launch Netflix, when you're in the middle of a movie and want to pause for some reason. The housing of the player is shiny black plastic. It looks and feels cheap, especially compared to the much heavier Sony X800M2. A final thing you might want to consider involves the playback aspect ratio of certain (but not all) DVDs. Because the player upscales, the TV thinks it's getting a 4K image. Most TVs lock the aspect ratio for 4k sources, which means your DVD will display with both vertical and horizontal letterboxing. The only way to eliminate the vertical letterboxing of DVDs is to manually set the player to 480p output -- which kills the upscaling coming out of the player. Note that newer 4k TVs will do their own upscaling of 480p material. So not all is lost. But it's a real pain to have to manually change the output of some DVDs and then have to change back to "auto" when watching either blu-ray or 4k blu-ray disks. Again, this is a problem only with some DVDs, not all.  In spite of these drawbacks, the picture quality is a sheer joy. I have an XBOX Series X, and I can attest that the picture from the Panasonic is noticeably better than from the XBOX. The XBOX isn't bad, but the Panasonic is clearly better.  You will have to be your own judge as to whether it's $400 better if you already have an XBOX or a PS5.

title: Everything I expected
text:
I have had this machine for ten days now and feel comfortable giving it a review.

It has been six years since I last purchased a computer, it was also an ASUS. I expect this purchase could last that long. This will be my third ASUS laptop and second ROG gaming system. I consider myself at the intermediate skill level for tweaking computers and solving minor problems (that does not include swapping parts).

I did adequate research on the ASUS web site and various, other reliable sources to know what the latest versions and ratings of central processing units, graphic cards, memory (RAM and SSD) and this laptop was close enough to the latest version of everything to satisfy me.

I read other reviews here on Amazon about loud fan noise – here is what I experienced: if you are sitting idle (not playing games, no graphic card or CPU intensive software running, and simply browsing the web or streaming a video) the fan is at low RPM. I set my system for *performance* using the “GameFirst” and “Armory Crate” apps provided by ASUS. When you are using graphic intense games or a CPU heavy software application the fan will increase in RPM to help cool these devices inside the laptop. Without the cooling, they can get extremely hot in a short period of time and that would not be healthy for either the CPU or graphics card -or anything else inside the laptop, to be accurate. So, yes, you can expect fan noise during intense application use or gaming. Since I game with a headset, I do not notice the fan noise (unless I take the headset off). There is no unusual “tinkling” or other noise coming from my fan.

The graphics are awesome, I will upgrade my monitor soon to get the most out of the laptop and graphics card capabilities. Yes, you will want to use the HDMI output to a larger monitor to get a better, more enjoyable gaming experience.

The laptop did not come loaded with excessive software; the anti-virus was not my choice, so I uninstalled it. Setting up Windows 10 is easy since Cortana walks you through the initial setup. I already had a Microsoft account (you do not have to have one if you do not want one) so everything was quick and easy. I next went through the Windows settings and turned things off for more privacy. I then linked my existing ASUS account, and I could see all three laptops in my registration history – neat. Over the following several days I found other things I did not use, or turned off, and for several days now I have left it where it has been, and I am completely comfortable with it.

One last thing. I am not using the ROG Keystone because I do not think it is necessary for my use of this laptop. The choice is yours.

Overall, this ASUS laptop was everything I expected with no surprises. If you are not computer savvy and want to buy this machine – talk to a relative or friend who is more knowledgeable to help you have a great out of box experience and, for a few days, you can reach out to them for answers to questions or help you “tweak” your machine.

title: iPhone preferable to this Garmin device
text:
Old school technology but even so, it's not easy to use or free of serious flaws. I returned the device.

I have had no problem with other GARMIN devices including my trusty cyclocomputer. All connect easily to my iPhone & MAC via Garmin apps.

MAPGPS 64sx has impressive gps accuracy with the option of selecting multiple satellites & decent battery life. I like that it's light and small enough to put into a cargo pocket. However, something basic as searching for an address will not work because it does not recognize the state until you purchase an additional map, CITY NAVIGATOR NT, at $100 (nonrefundable). I purchased the nonrefundable map but the GARMIN CONNECT app failed to activate the purchase due to a persistent "temporary" server error that GARMIN SUPPORT could not fix. My chat was terminated and told the Engineering Team would follow-up but no ticket was generated and I never heard back. Frustrating after spending countless hours troubleshooting, no help from Garmin, and I'm out $100.

The map resolution is quite weak especially when compared to a modern smartphone. Lack of touchscreen makes moving the maps slow and arduous.

When you purchase be prepared to also buy a MICRO-SD 32Gb card to enable map updates & synchronization. You will also need two AA batteries, preferably LITHIUM, since no batteries are enclosed. The rechargeable battery pack is extra. You'll also need a screen protector. Prepare for setting up the phone by loading the Garmin Connect app to your smart phone and Garmin Express on your computer. You will connect to Garmin Express on the computer via an enclosed USB cable that provides sync but only recharges batteries in the device if you purchase the optional battery pack that many reviewers call junk. Reportedly rechargeable Li AA batteries are the way to go.

Even though I'm out $100 for the map download I feel relieved of being able to return this nightmare device. THANKS AMAZON! Like another reviewer who is directionally challenged I am going to learn to use my smartphone to hike the wilderness & cities with an enhanced battery backup and great new apps. This website discusses that option: https://blog.gaiagps.com/iphone-vs-garmin-gps/

GOOD LUCK!

If not, set it up to the way you like it in the beginning and then forget it as the app does not sync all the time with the soundbar,  It's frankly a pain in the neck.  The sound however is top notch, for theatre sound combined with a big screen TV with Dolby vision, it's amazing.  Why go to IMAX when you have this setup.  The bass and subwoofer is really loud and boomy, for me I had to drop the bass down minus -3 and the sub minus -7 so as not to vibrate all my hanging art work off the wall.  Plus it was scaring my dogs.  Even on music, when you set the EQ to music, it does a good job of stereo separation, because of how wide it is.  It's really good.  Time will tell if the elevate mechanism that rolls the two side speakers will last, but that's why we get the extended warranty, right?  In any case, the price is good at sale prices like $ 799.  I don't see it really a good value at the retail price.  so if you see it on sale, it's a good buy.

title: Works PERFECTLY.
text:
Ignore Carolyn's review; what they might not understand is that in order to be able to use MS Pro Duo with over 32GB capacity with a PSP:

2. even after that, it takes a few tries; what worked for me was copying over the .IND files from a working stick and then formatting.
I bought this stick to replace one of those garbage knockoff PhotoFast dual-SD to MS Pro Duo adapters, because the loading was slow as hell and failed 70-80% of the time. title: Underpowered - Returned because it couldn't keep up with 2019 16" Macbook Pro
text:
This item is advertised and written about as working with Macbooks. It has only a 90W-capable PD Thunderbolt port, though, and could not keep up with my 2019 16" Macbook Pro. The MB Pro apparently consumes 96W when going at full speed like running games on Steam. When the laptop was going at max power, the SD7500T would just completely stop working - it wouldn't charge the laptop and no other items, such as a trackball, connected to the dock would work either.

Kensington should be putting a 100W PD port in this device. 90W is underpowered. Also, Kensington is not alone in this oversight. Other manufacturers are building underpowered Thunderbolt docks. I can find USB docks with 100W PD ports, but no Thunderbolt docks. I wish these manufacturers would pass closer attention to laptop power specs. I don't understand how this happens.

title: A cheap camera for a midrange price.  No thanks.
text:
First day I used this camera the image quality was acceptable. Nothing like advertised, but I didn't care so much. Next day I used the camera, the image quality degraded significantly. I couldn't figure out why. I changed the lighting. I tried manual focus. Even installed Logitech's camera app (though I firmly believe that no product should require bloatware to function.) Nothing would correct the INCREDIBLE blurriness.

Finally I figured it out. The camera only focuses on faces within 1.5 ft of the lens. Once your face is 1.55 feet away, the focus goes to crap and nothing (that I've tried) will recover it. I've never liked working with my nose to the screen. I use a sit/stand desk and my face is always ~ 2 ft from the screen.

This camera is overrated, and I don't appreciate my time being wasted troubleshooting something that is priced to work out of the box.

title: Updated Review: HORRIBLE - STAY AWAY---- Great, Now That It Works..
text:
UPDATED REVIEW: TLDR Listen to Reviews, Horrible Customer Service, 90 Warranty ONLY - You Have Pay for Anything After that! Garbage Equipment. Had Two of these Die!!

I should have listened to reviews of this CM1200 Cable modem! First modem I got was garbage and after a month of trying to trouble shoot why my new network setup was't working, it turned out to be the modem. So I got that one replaced with a like kind CM1200. Worked OK for the 5 months I've had it, but I didn't realize what torture I have been living with by doing every other day restarts until the unit completely crapped out. Intermittent dropouts of network connectivity, constant reboots of the modem to get it connected again, which progressively got worse and worse until I had to restart the modem at least every 2 hours just to have connection again. I finally got to the point where i bought a competitors modem (Arris SB8200 Cable Modem Only, and LOVE IT!) and I have been actually sleeping at night again. I literally had dreams at night that the network was down and I had to get up to get it working and couldn't. Never lost sleep over something so ridiculous before, but I did. I've had my SB8200 high speed modem for two weeks and its a joy to come home and not have to hear my kids tell my that the internet has been out again for the last 4 hours.

Never again Netgear; you have burned me for the last time. ON TOP OF THAT, the whole pay for service on a product that is less than a year old is INSANE!!! This was the service call:

"Hi whats your problem"
"My modem is losing constant network connection."
"Is the light on for etc, etc, etc, etc?"
"Yes, they are all on at the moment, but after a couple of hours, I lose connection even though the lights are on."
"Oh, your equipment is fine, so it's not that. But if you want to purchase a service agreement we can forward your issue to our troubleshooting team...."
CLICK.... I hung up on that B.S.!

WTH is that!!! Company essentially holding me hostage with a $180 piece of garbage paperweight and they wont honor a one year warranty on unless I pay for a service contract. Absolute crap I tell ya. Never again Netgear, never again. I said never!! Stay away from this product, and essentially any of their others. I've had a gaming router of theirs before too, and it had similar issues that I replaced that with a TP Link Deco x20 Mesh Router, and it work awesome. Just dont buy these guys crap, you will regret it in the end.

FIRST REVIEW: So the first cable modem I got had to go back. Constant internet drop outs, restarts, reboots, start over! It was a headache for two weeks trouble shooting. I had upgraded my internet service, cable modem and then mesh routers within two weeks. The cable modem/service were first and connection was intermittent. So figured it was my older gaming router and I needed mesh network upgrade for the house and kids demands for connection. Replaced with wifi mesh router and it was a crap shoot for many days. I thought the new router was no good, but then I got a replacement cable modem to rule that out. Turns out my Cm1200 was bad. The replacement has been working great and now I have to update my review on the Wifi routers that I lambasted. Knocked off one star on this cable modem due having to troubleshoot and replace the original purchase. But so far so good. Hope it stays that way.

title: Works great!
text:
The MacBook Pro docking station works wonders. I was able to connect multiple peripherals and they all worked connected at the same time. I was able to connect 2 HDMI monitors with ease. Once I saw that the combination of two monitors worked, I decided to push a little further. While the 2 monitors were connected I added a usb keyboard and mouse…worked great while monitors were on. I found no lag at all from the mouse or keyboard. From there I decided to connect a USB external hard drive, and was able to access files from the drive as well. I decided to see how the docking station would work with all these extra items connected, and watch a movie from a USB thumb drive. I connected a USB thumb drive and the computer recognized with no problem. I started the movie I had saved on the thumb drive and it started up just fine. One thing I noticed is that the movie would briefly lag for a split second once in a while, but overall the movie was watchable. Not sure if the lag issue is due to the docking station or the thumb drive, since the drive is about 4 years old. I was able to manage all of these connections without the MacBook being connected to a power source; fully on battery. I connected to the power and everything works just fine. The movie issue was still there, but not sure if the lag happened less [or more] often or not.

Overall I am very happy with this docking station because it does exactly what it is meant to do, which is to increase connectivity. I would have ranked it 5 stars, but I did find it disappointing that I was unable to connect my USB-C monitor to the docking station and get the MacBook to recognize the monitor. It appears the USB-C input is designed for a power input. The docking station is small, lightweight, and very portable.
