title: Dead on Arrival
text:
I got a TCL 4k Roku tv a few years ago that I've really liked. I decided to splurge for an 8k tv so I could enjoy some of the hdmi 2.1 and earc features that I had been lacking. Amazon delivered this with a freight truck delivery to my garage. From there, a friend and I carefully unboxed it, assembled the base and got it set up. You will definitely need two people for this - but instructions were clear and it was very easy.

I begin going through the setup process - connect to the Internet, set up my Roku account. Everything seems to be working perfectly - the menus look very clear and bright - but then, suddenly, as I confirm the email with Roku, the picture becomes distorted. I wait a few moments, the screen becomes unresponsive. It slowly becomes entirely white and nothing is discernible on screen. I turn the tv off, unplug it, wait a moment. Maybe it was a fluke. A very strange crash, who knows. Now the screen is entirely white save for a few vague shadowy areas I assume are menus that should be displayed. I can hear the audible confirmation of menu navigation, etc - clearly the system is functioning but the display is completely unusable.

The photo, it may be hard to tell - but the screen is undamaged insofar as obvious cracks or abuse.

While this is a very one-star experience, I'm awaiting TCL's response (their support is closed till Monday). I'll update this review as I find out more. But where it stands now: not looking good.

Update 12/6/21: TCL has responded very quickly to my support request. They were very quick to reply (on a Sunday, no less). They had admitted that the device will need to be replaced and I should pursue that with Amazon (although they did say they could handle it directly if I preferred). Amazon replacement request was quick and painless - they'll drop off a new one for me in a couple days and take the broken one away at the same time. That's about as easy as I could hope for a replacement of a product this size. Will update once I have the new one set up.

Update 12/10/21: Amazon just delivered the replacement. All seems well now! Having just set it up, I'll be testing it over the next few days. So far, I've run a white screen test and it's respectable - very slight banding on one side but cannot be noticed unless you're testing for it. Will be tweaking and testing in the coming days. Adding a star since I now have something working. Kudos to Amazon for making the replacement relatively painless.

Update 12/21/21: TV is working (mostly) as intended. Picture quality is very good. There are a few instances where there appears to be a bit of "bleed" with the backlighting on a few scenes - but it's hardly noticeable unless you're looking for flaws. The one issue I've had a few times: I have this hooked to a Sonos Arc via the eARC port. The volume button on the tv remote correctly shows a change on the Arc, but no audio comes through. Hard-restarting the tv (turn off, unplug, re-plug in) solved the issue both times. I suspect this is a software issue and may be specific to my setting (I have powersave off and it sits in rest mode instead of true power-off). Otherwise, great tv, no regrets. Adding another star. Due to the original defective unit I received, a few of the very minor concerns, I think it has earned the four-stars given the premium this unit currently demands over other units from TCL.

title: A Decent, Durable Carry-On Bag
text:
The official description calls this a "convertible duffel bag backpack." The first thing I wish I'd known in buying this bag is: it's backpack sized, not duffel bag sized. If you're accustomed to carrying a large duffel bag sufficient to hold all your clothing, toiletries, and entertainment for a three-day weekend, this bag isn't big enough for that. It's the right size to stow in an airliner's overhead compartment, and will carry enough clothes and goodies for a few days, if you pack abstemiously.

That said, I actually like this bag overall. It has two large external compartments, two small ones, and an internal pouch for small items like your cloth respiratory masks. If you pack carefully, and don't bring lots of gewgaws, you can live out of this bag for two or three days, longer if you pack some travel-sized laundry detergent. The tightly woven canvas fabric is water-resistant (though not waterproof), so it's durable through multiple travel conditions. This is a good piece of small luggage.

And it has multiple ways of carrying it. If you've made it this far in the description, you already know it has shoulder straps like a backpack, a handgrip, and a detachable shoulder strap. This means that, if you're already carrying another piece of luggage (in my case, a computer backpack), you have multiple options for how to carry this bag. You aren't burdened by carrying it in any single way that might wear on your body later. All three options are built to resist damage from regular handling.

I do wish the bag was larger. I hoped I'd be able to carry my clothes, workout gear, and the book(s) I'm currently reading in the bag; instead, I had to make value judgements about what to leave behind. But if you know that ahead, this bag makes good luggage for weekend trips, overnight jaunts, and business travel. You can carry it with other bags, or on its own. And you'll probably carry everything you need for quite a while in just one bag, if you choose wisely.

title: An Artist's Tool
text:
If you’re reading this review, you already know what you’re getting with the Instax system. It is a fixed focal length instant print camera that produces approximately 2.5” square, low contrast images. It’s not for landscape or action photography, it’s for fun. And that’s exactly what it is, a clunky camera to pull out at a party or in the kid’s classroom and make snapshots. Te pictures that the camera produces are delightfully retro looking, harking back to the Polaroid days (who remembers those?). , about a dollar per shot, the pictures are a relatively inexpensive way to share memories or break the ice, whichever is needed at the moment.

The camera is uncomplicated. Turn it on by turning the ring around the lens, paying attention to the light detents that indicate On for normal photos and Selfie for closer shots. That’s it…press the terribly positioned shutter button (I’ve wasted too many shots from an errant knuckle or finger firing the camera) and wait for the film stock to be ejected. Sit and wait as the image magically comes into view and enjoy it. Repeat. Now the question becomes, what to do with these little beauties? An artist could create some thoughtful work anchored in these images. What to do, what to do?

title: Surprisingly good for a low price.
text:
I won't lie, I really expected these to be a let down. They surprised me. Immediately I was impressed by how the case clicks shut - no accidentally falling out (my Sesh Evos have jumped out of their case when dropped on a bed... it happens). They fit securely in that little lightweight case, so I can toss it in my bag and not have to hunt for a stray bud. Unfortunately, what you give up for that light weight is the Tile feature the Evo's have, so don't you dare drop a Dime, you'll have to see where it goes to find it. The other drawback to the case is that the outside of your earbud is exposed through the case, but I don't see that being an issue with my usage habits (it's not a step down from what I already have, at least).

The sound quality is classic Skullcandy, clear and balanced. For the price tag I didn't expect thumping bass or extremely rich sound, but it doesn't disappoint. This is the Ink'd or Jib equivalent as a wireless bluetooth unit. It lacks the powerful sound my Sesh Evos have at the same volume settings, so of course my phone throws a 'loud sounds are bad m'kay' warning at me as I bump it up a little louder - but they get loud enough for drowning out kitchen gadgets, lawnmowers, Harleys, or screaming kids playing MMORPG games on the pc's behind me. YES!

The noise cancellation is spot on, excellent, can't hear anything but the whoosh of my own heartbeat with them fitting snugly in my ears... except gamer kids, of course. Which brings me to fit: right out of the box they fit me perfectly, but the extra buds gave me options. The lightweight buds also feel secure and don't threaten to fall out if I yawn changing pressure or structure of my ear canals... so that's a win for me.

Sound quality for phone calls is really nice. Great for discord chat as well. Crystal clear.

I'm impressed, and delighted that they were on sale when I got them. Well worth jumping on that deal even though I have other wireless earbuds. I might even get a couple more pair for those screaming kids... except then they'll scream more.

title: Convenient Alternative Power Supply
text:
We're an off-grid acreage property up in the mountains.
Our power is generated by a combination of Solar & Wind.
Typically, our system provides more than enough power.
However, come wintertime when the sun is low, skies are often cloudy, and steady snow fall repeatedly covers over the solar panels… it's a great convenience to have alternative power sources available (even short-term).
The Sikon Portable Power Bank has been one of those conveniences. On good Solar-Wind days we charge up the unit and store it on the alternative-power-source shelf… then, it's there when we need it.
In addition, its compact size allows us to take it anywhere we need in the residence as well as anywhere on the property. Small enough to easily tote about, and yet powerful enough to give multiple 'Full Charges' to a variety of devices.
The only thing (so far) that we'd ask to be changed is that there are no feet on the unit's elongated horizontal bottom side. There are indeed feet at one 'end' of the unit which would allow it to stand vertically… however, we have never needed nor wanted to utilise the unit it in that posture. It's far more convenient for it to lay flat having the input/output ports facing outward instead of 'upward'. Additionally, the cooling fan is situated at the vertical bottom where the feet are. It seems that it would be a better configuration to allow the fan to face outward instead of downward… then there would be nothing to interfere nor impede its function (such as the floor, the ground, a carpet).
note* to Sikon, this would be quite an easy fix (attaching additional feet to the horizontal bottom) thus giving customers even more optoions when using this power bank. Get that done and you'd have an even better item to offer. BTW: the feet should be rubber, not hard plastic. Rubber would act as shock-absorbers & minimize/eliminate hum-buzz when the unit is utilised on a hard surface such as a desk or table.
Otherwise, we're pleased so far. Thank you

title: Wireless Keyboard Mouse on one USB - had issues
text:
Years ago I had a Belkin unit for the PS2 interface - for up to 6 computers - and only used it for 4 computers. Then as the USB devices became the norm for the mouse - I would have to use converters USB to PS2. Eventually I gave upon it. I started looking at when there was a good USB KVM switch every so often.
Recently I got both a Raspberry Pi and a Jetson Nano, and the need for that switch was becoming strong enough to look - yet again. That is when I found this device.

I read the reviews on Amazon and this device had been "glitchy" in some of the reviews, so I was a bit wary of what I would get. The photos that it had all the cables helped - as my old Belkin cables had been an issue at times. So I ordered.

The box arrived and did not seem to have much weight. The box did contain all the cables you would need for having two monitors and a USB cable for Keyboard mouse setup.

I thought - I would try using my favorite mouse keyboard combo that uses a single USB stick to operate as my mouse and keyboard. I setup my main computer and could see that it was recognized - but after 10 seconds - it stopped recognizing it - I found that if you unplugged the USB from the KVM and put it back in it would start again but then stop if you stopped using it for about 10 seconds...well there went one star off the rating.

So - I had to pull out my oldest wireless mouse with a wired keyboard and hook that up to see how that went - and this was working. The KVM has two USB ports for the Keyboard and Mouse - and apparently they have not caught up to the single wireless combo yet.

The video claims to support 4K monitors - however I am still on the old 1920x1200 type monitors - so I do not have the hardware to validate the support - and I do not have a 2nd monitor setup in my usage - I needed just to get the One monitor as the monitor for the Jetson Nano and Raspberry pi, along with a work laptop extended screen and my desktop computer's main monitor.

While I had the Combo USB plugged in - the "Hot-Key" setup to go between monitors did not work for me; When I used the individual USB Mouse and Keyboard cables it did work - So I can have all the devices on and can switch between them as needed. The Nano and Raspberry Pi 4 - seem to support the 4K standard - so there is the first pressure to start looking at.

The devices I have are USB 2 - which this device says is what it supports. The technology changes over time - USB 3 is much more prevalent and 4K as well.

The device should suit my need for a few years still, and then I may have to look at these again.

title: Solid radio at a fair price: GMRS repeaters, oh my!
text:
This is my fourth Radioddity and my first GMRS/FRS from them. Having sold my two Midlans (which served me well on disaster deployments when I was a teenager), I was looking forward to receiving this walkie-talkie. There's a lot to like here.

Build quality lives up to what I expect from Radioddity. Ergonomically the radio feels good in the hand, and the button and keys feel top-notch.

Sound quality is excellent and the built-in FM radio is a favorite around the house with non-radio enthusiasts. Brief TX/RX testing showed capability for both clearly in a highly developed area with different elevation (roughly 70ft. difference) at a half-mile distance (using GMRS). That's pretty decent considering the conditions being just about as bad as plausible.

The thing that really makes this radio stand out to me and distinguishes it from most if not all "bubble pack" GMRS/FRS combo radios at the big-box stores is the GMRS repeater capability. This is a clear sign that this is a radio made by people who make more than just consumer products: this is a mass-market friendly yet highly capable device.

Other features that I really like are the USB-C charging capability (i.e., no custom charger, and USB-C means fewer cables and battery banks for emergency or outdoors use), removable antenna, and *potential* CHIRP programming capability down the road. The fact that Radioddity is actively working on firmware updates is a promising sign that they're enthused about this release.

I'll likely buy a second. It's well worth the price when compared to what you could find at a big-box store in this category.

title: Nice monitor, but has a low-quality power adapter, which could force you to throw it in the trash.
text: Screen quality is very good and I really liked using it.... for about a month.  Unfortunately, I did not realize that they put a super-cheap, low-quality, power adapter port on it, which uses a mini-USB on the monitor and plugs into a standard USB port on your computer for power.  After about a month of relatively light use, the mini-port on the monitor came loose and twisted-up inside the case.  It was about a week after my return-window expired, so I didn't know what to do with the thing, because the port was totally unusable.  So, I took it apart and looked at it, hoping I could repair it myself.  What I found is the mini-port in this thing is only attached on one side to the board in the monitor, so if you don't hit the port exactly straight and go easy on the push, when you plug the power cord in, it will literally bend and twist the port up-inside the case, making it impossible to plug the power cable into it... and it is impossible to fix the thing once you have done that.  In the end, I wound-up throwing it in the trash after only 5-weeks of use, 3-weeks of which I used it very little at all.  I would not recommend buying this monitor at all, simply because I have seen and experienced for myself what a cheap, low-quality power port they have put on this thing.  It may work alright for you, if you are super-careful with the mini-port on the power adapter, but if you miss it one time and push too hard, your money is going straight into the trash can.

title: Every earbud is a series of priorities and compromises *UPDATED*
text:
***UPDATE: BUTTON FUNCTION MAPPING OPTIONS TOO LIMITED***

Ok after a couple of weeks regular use I've realized the limited button mapping is a real problem. With a bud that has only one button we should be able to map any function to any action. This is not possible. Should be an easy fix but jaybird does not seem motivated to do so. As a result I've found myself trying to shove and hold the one button to change volume at speed on a bike on a gnarly trail. The powerbeats were brilliant for this as they have a rocker for volume. Also the jaybirds have a real problem with wind despite jaybird's efforts. Finally when running with the vistas I can hear every footfall transmitted into my ear. I still think they sound MUCH better than powerbeats, and are probably ok for some exercise activities. But not great for demanding running or biking activities, which is my primary use for a bud. I might keep these because they sound so good. But I'm going to have to get another pair of powerbeats for serious activity.

***END UPDATE***

The priorities you insist upon and the compromises you can live with will drive your earbud choice. If you are looking at the jaybird vista 2 chances are you are going to use this for exercise and quite possibly vigorous exercise - that certainly is my priority in earbud functionality. Other people may value price, design, sound, anc, call clarity or battery life more.

I am coming from powerbeats pro. I lost those. I think they may show up but until them i had to get something else. The fact that I bought something else might tell you something about the powerbeats. I mountain bike in nasty conditions and it is essential that my earbuds be secure and tough.

Here is what I think according to how I value bud qualities

1. These work great as exercise buds. They are very secure during vigorous exercise. Their spec dictates that they should be able to withstand nasty conditions. Time will tell, obviously. The powerbeats were very secure as well and also stood up to many months of wet, sweat and abuse.

2. Sound. These sound really good. Better than the powerbeats. The powerbeats sounded adequate but had typical beats sculpting and boosting. These sound much more natural and nuanced. I would love to hear them against the master&dynamic that have much larger drivers and tout their audiophile chops.

3. Connectivity. These set up and connected no problem and there has been no dropping or interference. The powerbeats were theoretically better because of their apple specific chip and sometimes connected to my iphone like magic but often one bud wouldnt connect or one bud would fail to charge properly. So annoying. These charge reliably no problem.

4. Comfort. The powerbeats were very comfortable for extended sessions. These are comfortable for awhile but after that my ear canal and pinnae become aware of them and before long they get a little uncomfortable. The available adapters are limited so you are kinda stuck if your ear is sensitive or has atypical anatomy.

5. Controls. I think all exercise centric earbuds need to have more comprehensive on bud controls. The setup on the powerbeats was simple, elegant and effective. The vistas not so much: there is one button on each bud. The button takes a lot of pressure to activate and the control schemes are not that intuitive with limited customization. So making changes while on the move is possible but not easy or ideal.

4. ANC. The powerbeats had nothing, not even any passive 'sealing'. These offer both moderate passive sealing and fairly effective ANC.

5. Design. These have a really sleek looking and elegant design. The powerbeats were nice too in a very different way. These fall somewhere between something 'bespoke' like master&dynamic and something dull like the sony or bose offerings.

6. Calls. So far i have had a couple of people mention that they couldn't hear me so well. The powerbeats always provided very clean calling performance.

7. Wind. The app has wind blocking modes and the buds themselves apparently have some sort of wind muting material. Forget it wind (like cycling or riding in an open jeep) is a real problem. This is probably too much to ask of earbuds but suffice to say that whatever efforts jaybird made in this direction have probably fallen short.

8. The app is ok but shouldn't be a selling point. It's better than the powerbeats that had no app at all.

So for core requirements both these and the powerbeats are excellent for vigorous exercisers. These sound better, connect more reliably and provide good anc. The powerbeats were far better with on-bud control, more comfortable, and provided better call performance. Given the +/- comparison I'd buy these over the powerbeats again.

title: Works great on a Mac, buttttt
text:
I have had no trouble with my 8TB drive working on my iMac. Yes, I had to reformat it and that took a little research online to figure it out. But it works great. So great that I'm purchasing the 16TB drive today because I've almost filled the 8TB up. I haven't tried to use it with Time Machine - I have a different drive for that - but I have no doubt it would work. Instead, I use it as extra space, loading all my media and documents on it.

I love it. I know there are a ton of 'Doesn't work with a Mac' reviews, but I can only assume the steps it takes to reformat the drive scared them off. (Because yes, there is that slight moment of panic when you follow the directions and your computer warns you it's going to erase the entire drive.) But once the drive is reformatted, I haven't had one issue with it. I had MacOS Catalina when I bought it. I now have MacOS Big Sur. Still no issues. (Except for it getting filled up LOL - but that's my fault, not its ;) )

Update 3/8/21: For those who have BigSur on their Mac - the power distribution via BigSur is perfectly f'd up. So whereas before my update to BigSur, I could leave my external hard drives plugged in and when it started up the next morning, everything was fine, now with BigSur, I have to unplug my externals when not in use. ANNOYING - especially since my iMac retains its connection and won't let me eject them easily unless I turn it off! And this isn't Seagate's issue - this is VERY MUCH an Apple mistake they aren't fixing. What happens if I don't? The computer won't start. The loading screen will get to 25% and stall. Once it even slid off the edge of the screen. I have to then force the computer to stop. And then restart. Then it starts up (Usually). I love Seagate, but am not happy with Apple. I'm getting to the point where there aren't any computers I can trust. I won't do Windows and this will be my last Apple machine.

We seriously need an OS that works, is stable, and won't steal our data.

title: Don't believe every review you read, especially negative ones.
text: Don't believe every review that you read...and only take isolated reported connectivity issues with a grain of salt, especially when they are incorrect.  i.e. bluetooth 5.1 connectivity distance etc.  Most connectivity issues in my 35 yrs of tech experience are due to "user error".  Beyond that most can be, and are corrected with a firmware update.  Now that being said, my opinion of course here on this unit follows. I have only had this 2nd generation Beosound A1 for a day, so keep that in mind.  But right out of the box, this is the best sounding truly portable speakers that I have ever heard, period. Amazingly so, in fact that I have ordered a two more to fit an application that required exactly what these A1's offer.  Beautiful clean sound that is loud enough in a large hockey puck style footprint the can be placed under a kitchen cabinets trim, virtually out of sight.  How awesome it that?  I had zero connectivity issues, and as a matter of fact I was surprised how well the connectivity worked with my iPhone, iPad, and 12" MacBook.  Just as you would expect from a Bluetooth 5.1 device!  I cannot and will not comment on Alexa connectivity because if I wanted Alexa capability I would just fire up one of the useless Alexa units that I have in my closet.  I can only suspect B&O added Alexa capability because they have some licensing deal with Amazon.  As for battery usage I have only had it for a day.  But if it comes close to the 18 hours as listed this is even more a winner.  And of course this is really portable so you can just plug it as you do your phone to fully charge in 2.75 hours.  As for the microphones to be used as a conferencing type device....pretty cool.  Though I have not tested them.  It will be a bonus if they work as well as the rest of this device's features. You have to keep in mind that if you want Alexa, Siri, Google, and tele-conferencing capabilities you ALWAYS have to purchase dedicated devices for those needs..  If you can get a device like the B&O A1 (2ND GEN) that is "primarily" a portable battery operated speaker that you can bring to the beach to be just decent at those other things then you are way ahead of the game.

title: Little size, little price, big value
text: If you need a pair of backup headphones to keep in your bag for all the times you forget your main ones, these are a great option. From the tiny size to the built-in keychain loop on the case, you can tell that these were designed with portability in mind, yet they don't really feel like they're missing anything. They have a charging case with strong magnets that hold the buds in really well. They have auto on/off functionality. They have microphones. You can use the buds individually if you want. There's even a single button on each bud; you're supposed to be able to perform all kinds of functions with different combination presses and long presses, but fair warning, anything besides the single click to play/pause is tricky to pull off and involves crushing your ear, so you might want to stick to your phone for controlling the music. The sound quality is good — nothing mind blowing, but definitely above average — and the comfort/fit are pretty par for the course for in-ear buds, with the standard three sizes of tips to choose from. But what really makes these buds stand out isn't their sound or comfort, but the sheer portability of this little package combined with its value, which is where Skullcandy usually shines. For the price you pay, you really get a lot. So these won't be replacing my AirPods anytime soon, nor can I necessarily recommend you use them as your main headphones, but they're a great price and great for traveling.

Then it needs to be tuned or adjusted from the stereo and then you can adjust the gain and frequency crossover on the rear of the unit. The subwoofer does need some time to “Break-in” to get it just right but it rocks the windows and vibrates the walls. For a 10” size it does reach down to 32Hz and has that resonant low sound that you would get only from a 12” or even a 15” sub. Price was well within the competition. A 12” Klipsch sub was on sale at Costco for the same price but it had a smaller cabinet and was not a Synergy Black Label. This is a step up from those bargain models

title: Needed a New PSU for My new MSI Nvidia RTX 3070ti
text: I walked into MicroCenter the other day and would you believe it, they had 3000 series Nvidia GPUs in stock. So I bought an MSI Nvidia RTX 3070ti for my rig. The first thing I did when I went home was go to a PSU calculator website to see if the EVGA 600 Bronze would be enough. It was fine for my Intel i7-9700KF CPU on an MSI Z390A-Pro MB running with an MSI Nvidia GTX 1660ti. But I wanted to make doubly sure before I installed my new $1000 graphics card. And wouldn't you know it, when I ran expert mode and entered in all my peripherals, the EVGA wasn't enough. So I went onto Amazon to see what Amazon Prime would ship next day... To my surprise, they had a highly-rated, value-priced Gamemax 750W aRGB 80+ Gold on sale that could arrive next day. So I went for it and am I surprised and elated at how it just fit into my rig powering all my components with no hiccups. It's quiet and the aRGB fan complements my rig's lighting to the point that you can't tell that they're not all synced up unless you look really, really closely. So PSU's are the unsung heroes of computer rigs. They do what they need to do day-in and day-out. Nobody notices them until they're not working. So since I just installed the Gamemax 750, I don't have much else to say other than it works and works well. Now only time will tell if this is a quality purchase. I will say that I'm pretty confident given the large number of positive reviews. Needless to say, I'm happy with the purchase and look forward to many years of fully-powered computing.

Writing this review to share my experience with OnexPlayer. This is my second attempt with portable gaming PC. I have been chasing this dream since the since the first GPD Win came out. 1600 USD is steep price for simple iGPU and 8 inch screen. There many options out there for gaming on the Go! Like Zephyrus G14. Trying to justify this as portable netbook is really not worth your money either. You can barely type even with dedicated keyboard (purchased separately). I would only consider buying this if your true passion is gaming. There is nothing quite like it. In my personal opinion nothing comes close when gaming on PC titles on the go!

If your decided on buying this keep your expectation low. As the driver for iris intel is still being updated with lates games. If your trying to play with newer AAA titles there is a high chance it could have bugs. I can name two title I know off. (Immortal Fynex Rising and Ghost Recon Break Point). But 90% of my steam library is PLAYABLE! I used the SD card slot to install all my steam games. It seams to work really well. As for other game store like Epic and Ubisoft. I’m having issue with the games if using the SD Card as a STORAGE. If you use the local storage it’s fine. I can play Assassin Creed Odysseys and Ghost Recon Wild Land in there lowest setting and 50 percent resolution. I know when I say that you will think that it looks horrible! But if you factor in the size of the screen and resolution it’s still 10x better than Nintendo switch! I can play FFXV At 50 FPS the game still looks good 2500x1600! There are plenty of titles AAA that are playable! I have 50 games in steam that I still need to finish. This range from Batman Series to Far Cry and Dirt Series Games. All this games are played FPS between 35-60 FPS. I consider myself as a casual gamer. I don’t really play hard core e-sports titles.

Battery Life is mediocre. 2 hours max! you can lower the TDP on the bios to stretch your battery life. A works well on 2D Title aka Sonic and Emulation games. Other than that you will be most likely tethered to an outlet just to game on extended period.

Comfort is also is one it’s low points. This thing HUGE! coming for Nintendo switch user! Lol. It’s really unwieldy when trying to game for extended time. The unit is heavy! If your going to use this you really need to brace the unit on top of table or your lap to increase comfort. Gripping this thing also somewhat awkward. It’s not quite ergonomic there is really no support yet from other third parties. The screen protection is also slim picking at best. It’s only the primary reason why I purchased the external keyboard.

I will update this review, the more I used the unit. I will add my EGPU Experience and long term use.

title: Tricky Requirement for this Cable to Daisy-Chain
text:
The M2 MAX conference room speaker system works quite well and can daisy-chain a 2nd unit (only 2 total), however they do a tricky thing and made the daisy chain cable a proprietary cable and charge $30 for what is really just a basic 3.5mm TRRS-TRRS (tip, ring, ring, sleeve) cord.

They made the 2nd ring (closest to sleeve) have minor resisted cross to the sleeve so some voltage can be passed through (~1.6V), but not full continuity, where a traditional TRRS cable does not. We did not want to dissect our $30 cable to see exactly what they did to make this connection, but figured would share the testing results of this cable and give a complaint about a $30 10' cable that should have been only ~$5-8.
Just our rant on this - and Amazon does not allow our business account to leave reviews, so left this under my personal account because was so annoying.

title: With reasonable expectations, you won't be disappointed
text:
Oh man! What can I say?!
I hesitated many times before i write this review. I have so many mixed emotions, i didn't know what to think of it. At same time i wanted to be as impartial as i could in my review to help other decide if this worth the extraordinary price tag or not. This definitely would be the question you'd ask yourself throughout every sentence you'd read in this review: Is worth 3+ grands?
Like probably many others, i read so many reviews about the Devialet Phantom Gold, watched whatever youtube video about it out there. I wanted that convincing argument that if i spend my hard earned dollars on this thing, i won't be left with disappointment. The hype about it was definitely there, but also saw the big let down in other reviews. I wanted to experience this thing firsthand but without feeling the buyer's rumors afterwards, so buying from Amazon with its 30 days free return was a no brainer.
The phantom gold had some scary reviews about intermittent, but serious connection problems. There were also reports of lack or poor midrange frequencies. Some called it flat! Some other proclaimed "audiophiles" bashed it in comparison to their high-end speakers setup. That had me really rethink the crazy idea of spending this much on a speaker that may have not just flaws, but severe ones on top of it may not be do great after all. The other thing i didn't like is the sole glossy white color option, which will not look great in my setup. In all, my thought process was, if i have to spend this much, it better damn be PERFECT.
I contacted Devialet directly about my concerns of reported issues and the possibility of a black version. They were quick to respond but in a diplomatic way not acknowledging any issues but assuring that they stand behind their product. They also confirmed what I already new about the only white color option. But acknowledged that many people are asking for a black version.
Fast forward one year, and Devialet releases the Phantom I series, with better firmware, same level of sound quality and power, more stability and ways to connect, and the kicker... Matte black option! Not to forget the wireless remote which was optional with phantom gold series. Of course Devialet had to do the Devialet thing and tack another $300 instead of dropping the price on the previous phantom series.
I quickly made the plunge. 5 days later with Amazon prime delivery, the mighty speaker was finally at my door!
I won't go through the unboxing since it is as intriguing as in the numerous youtube videos. I will admit this though, I took a selfie with the thing!!! I don't know exactly why. I haven't posted it anywhere nor showed anybody, i just did! Maybe to mark this historic moment...Yes! That's the kinda impact this thing can have on you.
Ok, enough of the literature and let's get to core of it: powered up the speaker, paired it with its remote, then with my phone using the Devialet App. As expected there are almost no indicator on the speaker telling what is it doing. But it's no problem cause it just works. One other thing i should mention, which also was a selling point for me is the Devialet integration of Spotify, making it seamless to play your playlist on the Phantom I.
The phantom 1 takes about 10 to 20 seconds to boot up. It let you know it's ready with a deep, faint but super clear realistic sound.
I should say i was a bit disappointed seeing streak marks on the chrome finish. Probably from a last minute poor cleaning/final touches job from factory. Remember, i was expecting and deserving perfection for the amount I paid.
I had prepaid and even fantasized for almost a year about a playlist i would want to hear this mighty speaker play. I won't start listing tracks or songs here as that's a music taste thing, but i will say i was confused and somehow disappointed. The songs I thought had decent bass on my Bose headphones or Klipsch 12" Subwoofer didn't sound as good nor get accentuated by the phantom dark chrome. I would even say they somehow sounded flat! On the other hand the songs i haven't given much thought, did sound great and so pronounced!
Bottom line is, I had to recalibrate my ears and adjust my expectations in a realistic and data driven way rather than going blind behind the hype around this (let's not forget) single wireless Bluetooth speaker.
So yes, i was disappointed and that's mainly cause I created this fantasy about this speaker that if i play a fart in it, it should come out as "Wow! That's sounded awesome!"
Sorry, it does not. If you play poor tracks, they will still sound poor even on the Dark Phantom Chrome.
Even with my initial disappointment, i still (kinda) made up my mind that this speaker is a keeper. This became more obvious when I started exclusively playing High Fidelity tracks also some "remastered" old tracks. That's where the phantom really shined for me. Its unmatched very wide dynamic range makes it so responsive to very low frequencies (very deep bass) to high frequencies (high pitch trebles) while still keeping the mid-range. And all this from one single compact speaker. Add to that the Devialet proprietary ADH (Analog Digital Hybrid) processing that makes it as close as possible to zero loss conversion. Or in English terms: Pure sound.
I recall other reviewer going through this disappointment to exuberation phase and attributing it to "giving time for the speaker to break in". I'm not sure this is an ordinary speaker that needs that. I do think though, people will have to recalibrate their listening to it being the new gold standard, and avoid comparing it to multi-speakers setups.

Question remains. Is it worth $3K+?
I'd say it depends on what 3K means to you. To me, it's borderline but yes.

Final thought: I do contemplate the idea of adding a second phantom chrome and making a dual phantom system.

5 Stars

title: Best ANC earbus on the market
text:
Ok, lets get a couple of things out of the way. You're never going to find ANC ear buds as good as over the ear headphones. If you want 100% ANC look at Bose Quiet Comfort, or Cowin's. That said, the Bose QC ANC are the best when it comes to ANC. I also own the Airpod Pro's and while they prevent 80% of noise, The Bose is at 90%. Additionally the Bose ear buds have a quality of sound that is rich and full. The Airpod pro's also sound great but the sound is not as rich as the Bose ear buds. I purchase these ear buds for two reasons, the ANC and the sound quality. I still carry my Cowin's over the ear headphones for overseas flight as I get 12 hours without charging and they truly drown out all sound. I use the the Bose and Airpods while traveling on shorter flights, train and ship. I am an Apple user owning most of all their toys, but I also own two Dell computers and a Samsung Tablet. I am therefore familiar with both OS and Android. In this case I would strongly recommend Bose if you are purchasing for the ANC technology. The only company that comes to Bose sound quality is Sennheiser, but no one has better ANC.

As a side note for those of you who own airpods and airpod pros and are complaining about them falling out of your ears, go purchase airpod ear hooks. You can buy them on Amazon.

title: How to configure router without signing up for Netgear account
text:
1. Connect router to power but DO NOT connect to your modem. Allow 1-2 minutes for router to boot completely
2. Using your phone or computer, connect to the new router
3. Open up a web browser and go to routerlogin.net
4. Sign in Username: admin Password: password.
5. Once you are logged in go to the Internet tab, if it asks you to use the Netgear Genie set up wizard, say "No, I will set it up myself".
6. For my spectrum modem:
- "Internet connect does not require login"
- Account and domain name leave blank
- Internet IP: Get Dynamically from ISP
- Domain Name Server (DNS) : Get Automatically from ISP
- Router MAC Address: Use Default Address
7. Click the green apply tab to apply settings
8. Click on the Wireless tab
9. Here you can rename your network (SSID) and set your own unique password. I chose to just broadcast the 5Ghz antenna so only the fastest network shows up when people look for your wifi. You do this by unchecking the "Enable SSID Broadcast" under the 2.4Ghz network.
9. Make sure Wireless Network (5GHz a/n/ac) is set to "Up to 1733 Mbps" and Channel is set to "Auto".
10. Click the green apply tab to apply settings
11. Connect the ethernet cable from your internet provider's modem to the yellow WAN port on the router. Allow 2-3 minutes for internet access. You can go to the internet tab and click test to verify that you have internet access.

EDIT:
If you ever need to make any changes to your settings after connecting to your modem, disconnect your modem from the yellow WAN port and toggle the power switch to off. Wait about 30 seconds and turn the router back on. Connect to your router using your phone or PC and go to routerlogin.net. After any changes are made, make sure you are logged in, connect the WAN port back, then press TEST under the internet tab once connected to your modem.

EDIT for dropped WIFI signals:
The wifi will quit about 2-3 times a day when using only the 5G and channel selected to AUTO. Try selecting Channel 44 and see if the dropped wifi improves.

title: Do Not Need the App to Setup This Router
text:
I purchased this router in anticipation of Starlink arriving in the area. I live in a very rural part of New Mexico where Internet is expensive and not very good. I have over 15 different devices online at any given time and this router was a great upgrade over the one provided by my ISP.

Despite claims by some reviewers, you do not have to use the Nighthawk app and/or account to setup this router. Simply connect to the router via Ethernet and navigate to the default IP: 192.168.1.1 with a user name of admin. The router will prompt a change of password and you can move forward from there as you would with any router. Of course, if you are using a conventional ISP, the app would probably be much easier to use for setup. I had to enter fixed IP, DNS and other gateway information to connect to my provider.

The user interface is extremely easy to use and offers you clear, easy access to any feature you need. My Tablo for instance needed to have some manually configured port forwards in order to reach it remotely. This router was easy to configure these ports.

title: Expensive high quality minimalistic backpack
text:
I loved this backpack.

I ended up returning it because it didn't fit my new laptop (Dell G7 15.6"). I ended up having to buy a 17" laptop backpack to fit it.

First impression: this bag is beautiful. (I got Lunar color). Genuinely one of the most visually appealing bags I've ever seen or used. And on the topic of design: This was my favorite organizational design of all the bags I've ever used. I loved the internal sleeves, the top inside pocket, the side access front pocket. It's hard to describe how nice it feels to use. Like it's something that a less well designed backpack won't necessarily feel "bad", until you use this, and it just feels really "good".
Second impression: this bag is sturdy. Much sturdier than I thought it would be. While I didn't get to test it in much rain or anything, I can't confirm, but I would feel safe running home in the rain with this.
It was also pretty comfortable, but nothing crazy.
Something to keep in mind: this is a no-frills bag. No crazy security, no internal wires, no fancy suspension, not ultralight (actually a tad heavy). But if you're looking at this bag, that's probably not what you're looking for.

Overall: I really really loved this bag. It was honestly difficult to have to return this, and if I had a laptop that fit, I probably would have kept it. At this price, I think a lot of people will complain that it lacks "features", but for me the beauty of this bag is it's simplicity. If you're looking for a minimalistic bag that's actually high quality and well designed, this is it (and yes, you have to pay more than a $20 H+M bag).

An alternative is the Fjallraven Raven 20. It's around $80 I believe, slightly less well designed, less comfortable (no padding), slightly less sturdy, a little bit smaller, and less visually appealing (messier). If you're looking to upgrade from a Jansport, that may be a good option.

title: Installation is terrible, and it is easy to permanently damage the protector
text:
I was impressed with the QR code that directed me to installation videos. I watched several before I attempted to install on my iPad. The instructions seemed straightforward, but I realized as I gathered the materials as described in the videos, I didn’t have all of the installation parts noted on any video. Some were missing, some were not labeled the same. There were three videos, and none of them lined up as being the set of instructions for me.

I tried to use what I learned, and apply it to the written instructions contained in this package. Sadly, one of the missing items was the rubber bands to hold the protector in place as I set it to line up with the iPad. It made it a bitch to attempt to line up appropriately, but I thought I managed. From there, I successfully removed the side that adheres directly to the iPad screen. That went fine, and I was optimistic. Then I attempted to remove the second film (opposite side of the protector). The stickers for hinged installation caught on the actual protector and caused the edge of the protector to curl up. Nothing I did would get it to stay adhered. Of course, the other item missing from my package was the item that is supposed to remove bubbles and smooth out the protector.

Since there were two protectors, I decided to just try again, and not stress over damaging one. I figured I must have done something to cause it to happen. Repeated the process, with almost identical results. This time, instead of a corner, it was a section towards one end that was damaged. Again, I improvised a smoothing tool, since mine didn’t have one, but it did not work. Now, a few hours after the second installation, the edge of that one is curling too.

I still have this damaged protector on my iPad until a different replacement I bought arrives later this week. The curled end is annoying, but better than using the tablet without a protector. Because I’m using it, I can also give feedback on the protector itself.

I like the “paper” feel of the sheet. I have arthritis, and my fingers don’t always go where I intend on a touchscreen or with a glass protector. This has lessened my “oops” moments while typing and playing games. Just two days with it is noticeable. It also reduces glare. I have a glass protector on my phone, and I can tell a noticeable difference in the two.

The only drawback (other than the obvious installation issues) is that it seems to collect dust a little faster than a glass protector. But if I was going to keep it, the pros would outweigh the cons. Had I been able to get either of the installations to work properly, I’d happily keep it.

If you receive this and are missing any of the installation assist items, I’d recommend reaching out to the seller and asking for them. Otherwise, your odds of damaging the protector are much higher. Once you’ve installed it, if it’s not damaged, it’s good protector, especially for the cost.

title: Has its Ups and Downs
text:
UPDATE after 8 Months
----------------------------
I've used this modem for about 8 months so far and for the most part it's been okay. My only issue is that it drops connection about once a month and will stay that way until I perform a reboot. This started happening a few months ago. To reconnect, I unplug the modem for a minute, then plug it back in. After that, it stays connected for about another month. If this becomes more frequent, I will consider switching to another modem.

ORIGINAL Post
------------------
I recently moved and found out, much to my dismay, that Comcast is my only hi-speed internet option. I
refuse to pay them any more that I have to, so buying my own modem was a must. This modem was reasonably priced compared to other brands and met the specs I needed.

Installation was easy enough, but came with very little documentation. I am a full time IT engineer, but I think most people should be able to set this up without a problem.

Once connected, I tested the speed and it performed well. I have an 800 mhz plan and got speeds exceeding that.

My only wish is that it had more than a single ethernet port on the back. I have an Eero mesh router which has to use that port, so I have to plug in my ethernet switch into the Eero mesh instead of directly into the modem. This makes connecting to the modem's setup screens a bit of a pain.

I am very happy with this purchase though.

title: Everything's amazing except the resolution--and restocking fee
text:
The "hub" aspect of this monitor is fantastic. Everything plugs into the monitor itself—all your USB gear (mouse, keyboard, backup drive, microphone, whatever you've got)—even ethernet! And then ONE cable connects to your laptop, and even charges it.

The screen is immersive and curved just the right amount, and the color fidelity is sensational. The problem, though, is the resolution—the number of pixels per inch (ppi): only 110 ppi. For comparison, the MacBook Pro's screen is double that in each direction: 218 ppi.

If you're used to a Mac, the Dell's image is upsettingly blurry. You'll be in great shape for photo and video editing. But for reading, editing text, or using apps like Indesign and Illustrator, you'll really mourn that low resolution.

I wound up returning this monitor. (BEWARE! They changed me a $235 "restocking fee" after I returned it!! There is NOTHING about this on the item page.)

I bought the LG 34WK95U-W UltraFine 34-inch screen instead (it's ultrawide but NOT curved). It's got 163 ppi, which looks razor sharp, and I'm in heaven. (It's also much more expensive; now you know that there's a direct correspondence between resolution/size and price!)

The LG isn't a connection hub like the Dell; it has only two standard USB jacks on the back. But by adding a little $12 USB dock to the back of the LG, I still get the convenience of having only ONE cable connect to the laptop!

title: 🤯Fair Warning!!… Sound may turn up to FULL BLAST on its own!
text:
I ripped my earphones from my ears and uttered some very choice words as they flew across the room announcing “INCOMING CALL”!! I was enjoying some calm music recovering (or trying to!!) from a rather intense day. That all ended when my husband called and Ms Tozo10 decided to SCREAM FULL BLAST, “INCOMING CALL!!”.

Needless to say, if you value your hearing you might want to reconsider these earphones, as there seems to be a glitch that auto adjusts the volume—-never lower, always higher. …And these things are FREAKING LOUD!!! This isn’t just happening when people call—albeit that wins the prize for the loudest they’ve turned up on their own!! The volume just seems to have auto adjustment issues in general.

Setting aside the near heart attack this evening, I will write a few PROS & (a few more Cons) as to not completely destroy their reputation, bcs these are actually pretty good earphones.
*On a side note, on my own I am comparing these with Tozo T6, so I’ll make some notes about T6 alongside my eval.

PROS:
✔️Decent sound quality (not near as good as T6). T6 ARE A NEWER MODEL
✔️Works with iPhone X, as do T6
✔️Love the dots indicating remaining charging case battery power
✔️In the week I used these they had PLENTY of battery power (better than my 10 month old highly overrated AirPod Pros). I have read a handful of reviews saying the battery power on the T10 & T6 does not stay this good for very long, but I cannot vouch for that at this point.
✔️Earbuds are slightly smaller/lighter weight than T6. Slightly more comfortable to wear. (I still prefer the airy AirPod Pro type buds as far as breathability).
✔️Touch control pad is less sensitive than T6 (Good thing!!)
✔️These stay in my ears well, as do the T6’s. Both stay in better than my AirPod Pros.
✔️Can use one earbud at a time, as you can with T6
CONS:
✔️VOLUME auto adjusts (AKA AUTO BLASTS to FULL VOLUME!) at random times giving victim a potential heart attack.🤯
✔️Case feels a little cheap (not a dealbreaker).
✔️Earphones cover a majority of the ear and can get a little sweaty, as do T6
✔️Battery case needs a spring to slow down the lid closure (not a deal breaker)

I’m trying several pairs of Tozos, and so far I’ve used T6 and T10. Overall, I prefer the T6, with the exception of the ultra-sensitive touch pad. I don’t move around much so it’s not usually a problem. Both models have some Volume control issues, however T10 is worse when comparing volume LEVEL glitch. T10 buds are slightly more comfortable bcs they’re not quite as big as T6, but it’s not a big difference.

If sound quality is a priority, T6 are *hands down* better than T10. If you move around a lot, T10’s are less sensitive to touch, thus better for movement, but know that the superior sound quality of the T6 is just not present with T10’s.

☑️I’m now trying Tozo NC2’s. Will return here to add more to my evaluation after I’ve had more time to evaluate them. So far;
✔️Sound quality is excellent, love the “surround sound”
✔️Comfort level is the best of all 3, but shape needs some softening on edges. Not a dealbreaker.
✔️A little problem I noticed, as have others…. when you adjust the L earphone it is too easy to toggle the NC feature. That touch area is too sensitive and should be moved down to the stem.

✔️Also, if you don’t have a really good fitting bud, it can automatically activate the voice assistant! The buds moved around and made my phone automatically dial a woman who interviewed me for a job!!, my health insurance company, Instacare, and my dermatologist!!! I’m hoping with a better fit it will not do this anymore. This is a dealbreaker if I cannot lower this sensitivity. No way to remove VoiceAssistant feature as far as I can tell. I don’t want that feature.., I sleep with them on. Holy moly can you imagine how many accidental calls I could make?

***Side Note: I am REALLY missing the SOUND QUALITY of my T6’s, but I may or may not have showered with them on🤣 (and no they are NOT waterproof, despite the claim) and I’m letting them dry. Day 5 post shower, the volume is actually returning after letting them sit. Time will tell if they sound as crystal clear as they once did.😭

Tozo has some great things going on with their earphones, but need to fix a few very fixable glitches… and they’re going to kick Apple & Bose #%%! …Especially if they can keep up the PHENOMENAL sound quality of the T6’s. (Btw…T6’s sound way better than my AirPod Pros. Esp bcs I like a base-y sound [it gives some ppl headaches tho].

Tozo is a brand to watch. Their earphones are competitively priced and their sound quality is superior to much more expensive brands, esp in T6 model.

title: For home stereo use if you have no pre-out or sub-out
text:
I didn't purchase this from Amazon as I found a better price from Walmart with free shipping as I bought two.

Previously purchased the Kicker KISLOC, however, ended up with background noise even after grounding between my subwoofers and stereo. Most of these devices are meant for car audio applications but thought I would give it a try. So returned that device, discouraged.

Later came across this device (Russound ADP-1.2), which I found online at Walmart for $31.99 I believe. This worked fantastic for high-level speaker inputs and converting to RCA signal going to two subwoofers. I could not detect any background noise. It was completely silent(no background, static, clicking) for my application.

I imagine this would work well for an amplifier application should your home theater receiver or stereo receiver not have built-in pre-outs and you have an application that requires it.

Recommend 14AWG or a little smaller connecting the high-level speaker inputs to this device.
Found a clear spot in the back out my receive to mount the using double-stick 3m foam tape. Kept the High-level leads fairly short.

Recommend this product for home stereo use.

text: We purchased this for our home primarily because our 6 year old Linksys wifi router did not send a strong consistent signal to an upstairs TV. We tried a remote extender, which was an improvement, but we were still annoyed by lots of buffering. The Asus solved that problem wonderfully. Our internet service is 100 Mbps, and that upstairs TV now gets 38Mbps consistently, which is plenty to watch shows (before it varied from 2-14Mbps). Our yard goes back about 200 feet, and I have been building a shed in the far corner, and listening to podcasts while working. The router, with a 2.4 Ghz connection, sends a good signal and my iPhone is able to maintain a two-bars wifi signal. The computers on wifi are getting a full 95-100Mbps signal from the routers 5G signal.  The improvement for smart TV watching is noticeable. No more buffering, but also the apps launch quicker, and while watching a show, the thumbnail pictures while scrolling forward work much better.  The browser setup went easily, and the interface is much improved over the older Linksys screens. I was able to do the initial setup painlessly and quickly, but later my son-in-law (an IT person) went through each screen to check for security and firewalls done right. I would buy again.

Anyway, I'm leaving a review now because I finally figured out how to connect them to my TV. A year ago I tried unsuccessfully to connect them either to my TCL tv or my soundbar. What I found out was that these earbuds will connect to Fire TV sticks. I HAVE a Firestick. It took 2 tries because the bluetooth timed out the first time. But right this minute I am listening to a Youtube video on my TV while I write this review. They don't sound as good as my headphones but they're not bulky on my head. It's a good trade off. Now I'm excited to see if they still work when I listen to DVD exercise videos.

text:

The 4" mid-range sounds great but needs a partner to give it a full soumd stage under a big screen TV. I might also ad that for a center channel speaker I had to put my ear to the 5.25" woofer to know if it was carrying any sound. It was of little help to the mid-range, and where it did help, it added more muffle than clarity.

If you travel these are for you. The noise canceling is perfect. During a flight, the plane just disappears. It is completely silent. If someone texts you, music dims, Siri announces the persons name, and reads the message automatically. No stopping to dig out your phone and look at the message. And, you can reply hands free. Great, great, great when your hands are full. I wear these for 8 hours straight and do not take them off, extremely comfortable.

There are a lot of other features that work with the iPhone that are great, you just have to experience it. But them, 10/10.

title: Unusable and bad design
text:
When I went to connect my TV antenna cable to one of these 90 degree connectors, the threads did not engage because the inner conductor wire in the cable would not fully seat (Picture 1). On closer inspection, the depth (where the conductor wire seats) is very shallow. I used a piece of wire to measure the seating depth; as shown in Picture 2 looking at the blue mark or arrow, one can see that it is significantly more shallow on this product (gold connector) compared to one purchased elsewhere (silver connector). The cable could easily connect to the silver connector (Picture 3).
Consequently, this product is unusable with normal cables. Its design is such that there is no sleeve usually present to allow contact and make a reliable connection. Rather, there is a small insulation collar and then a metal plate that the conductor wire must precisely touch/mate against. Anything deviation, such as a variation in the length of the connector wire, number of turns to tighten and even repetitive use would lead to a poor or no connection at all. There are considerable negative reviews here complaining about this product and this may be the root cause. If you use this connector, be prepared to purchase matching cheap coaxial products from the same manufacturer/vendor. It will not work with those purchased from audio or higher quality electronic stores.
I purchased three thinking that they could be used on my other TVs. I plan on returning them. The rating should be zero stars!

title: You Hear That?!...It's The Sound of Color
text:
With this cable, the veil was lifted so far back I can finally hear the visible spectrum of color in music!

Full disclosure, I am not one to subscribe to cables making anything sound better. I believe you have good performing cables and you have poor performing cables. If a cable is well designed, you've reached the pinnacle of the cabling and nothing else is gained. Everything else is bling.

That being the case, I enjoy a good looking interconnects on good looking equipment, and this cable looks fantastic! The build quality is absolutely premium and it certainly looks like minimal machine use was involved in it's creation. This cable in my setup is being used from my PC to DAC to amp to floor standers in my office. I did not have jitter or interference issues needing cleanup over USB with my previous cheap cheap cable, and that remains the same with this interconnect.

Verdict: Nothing more is gained other than getting the quality that you should be in the first place when spending more on a quality audio cable, but sometimes it's nice to have nice looking things. In this case, nice looking and well built doesn't have to hurt your wallet.

Its an incredible experience. Even low resolution youtube videos look good. 4K and 8K videos are outstanding. Projector is big and heavy - when compared to the small LED based projectors. Projector has a nice classy look, in case you want to permanently mount in on a table or something. Projector will match any decor in your room. The built in sound bar is good. I set it to the "Adaptive Sound" mode. Music and dialogues are crystal clear. Bass is what you can expect from a sound bar of this size. I believe there is built in bluetooth, so you can connect it to a receiver if you want more sound. I am very happy with the built in soundbar. Wifi is also built in.

title: READ BEFORE BUYING!
text:
UPDATE: 17 months after original purchase and the motherboard has died. It will not signal the PSU to power up the case, it will not boot, and it will not get to POST. MSI's warranty is only 12 months. Let's hope it didn't take out my 5600x with it...

ORIGINAL REVIEW: In order to save yourself hours of wasted diagnostics, and a possible wasted RMA, before you try to boot on this new motherboard go to MSI's website and download the latest bios, copy the file to an OLD Fat32 usb stick, rename the bios file to MSI.ROM, insert it into the flash bios port, and push the flash bios button to begin the 10-minute bios update (psu switched on, but computer off - after starting the flash the case fans/lights will turn on and the flash bios led will blink). I spent too much time trying to diagnose a no-boot, no-post issue with this motherboard when it shipped with an old/faulty bios that would not initially boot with my Ryzen 5 5600x.

After that it seems to be a decent board for gaming, and fit my accessories great. If you're using 3200MHz DDR4 be sure to enable XMP in the bios so you aren't limited to 2133MHz.

title: Battery life insufficient, hardwiring doesn’t help
text: I’ve had nothing but trouble with the battery life on this ring video doorbell. I wanted one I could hardwire so that I wouldn’t have to constantly charge and change batteries, but the hardwiring on this product only charges the battery and the charger can’t keep up in cold weather.  In the winter our overnight lows can drop into the high 20’s which is really not that cold compared to other parts of the country. We get a few days that don’t get above freezing, but again not that common. On cold days the battery drains quickly and can’t recharge fast enough which means the product is useless on those days. I even upgraded my transformer to be sure it was getting adequate power. I called Ring support and they recommended reloading the firmware. That seemed to work for a few days, but then it was back to the same old story. Plus it was a bit warmer those days, so I couldn’t isolate the variables. For an outdoor product this thing is terrible. The only “solutions” I’ve read have involved turning all the settings to minimum so that the features just barely work. I had most features set to default, they weren’t even on max settings. What’s the point of having features that are temperature dependent? I would not recommend this product.

title: Serious and fun
text:
These headphones are a great combination for both general fun listening and for mixing. The only headphones that I’ve had to reference from is the Sony mdr7506 and the audio technica ath40. The Sony’s are very flat… extremely flat, so much so that they are underwhelming and not very fun to listen to, but great for mixing. The ath40’s definitely have a higher amped up eq to them, as some put it a V signal - with increased bass and treble and low to mid everywhere else, which is fun to listen to immediately but I found not as good for mixing since the V signal when pushed would produce a lot of harmonic distortion in those areas resulting in listening fatigue.

These akg’s have the best of both worlds. They are relatively flat with a good hz range to get the job done and the low ohms gives that range a good overall boost without being fatiguing. Akg does have a reputation for having the bass on the low side though and unfortunately these feel similar, although it is more along the lines that the bass doesn’t feel wet but more dry (less sub bass/spatial). But! The good thing about these headphones is that they scale very well, they can be pushed with any eq settings and they respond appropriately without any harmonic distortion or distortion in general and are clearly more than capable of producing anything else you would need, whether it’d be to push the bass up a bit higher to compensate or to push it with crazy sub bass spatial surround sound for fun. Despite the dry bass, these are universally more pleasant to listen to, the bass is still prevalent with the rest of the eq being balanced but also enhanced and pushed forward by the decent soundstage these headphones create, which is a surprise considering they are closed.

Only complaints is 1. the coiled cord is short and not the softest rubber so it is not very elastic, 2. the head band does not have much foam to it which can be uncomfortable and 3. They are not the most portable, with only being able to swivel to the their sides, but as a result of having less moving parts these feel solidly built.

title: Decent Earbuds for the Price.. Microphone is nearly non-functional
text:
The main reason I ordered these earbuds was to allow me to hear and communicate in video meetings and conferences without the bulkiness of my over-the-head headsets. I needed an earbud that had an accessible microphone and connects with a 3.5mm jack, both of which were included in this product. (Note: I am using these earbuds with an Astro Mixamp connected to my PC.) After receiving these earbuds, I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of packaging for such a cheap price. The carrying bag is quite nice, and the feel/look of the earbuds is nice as well. Now, after using the earbuds and testing them with voice recorders, I am disappointed to say the microphone is nearly non-functioning, which was one of the main reasons I purchased these earbuds. I haven't seen many reviews talking about the microphone so I thought there wouldn't be an issue after seeing all the positive reviews about the quality of sound, but in fact, I was wrong. The microphone barely picks up your voice while wearing the earbuds normally. The sound comes through very distorted and choppy. Also, the overall sound quality is also just OK... Maybe I'm spoiled by the daily use of high priced quality headphones, but I wasn't blown away by the sound quality. I gave these earbuds a 3-star rating because for the price, they're not a terrible option for what they can do, but I'm sure there are better alternatives for earbud/microphone combos out there for around the same price.

title: Perfect for ITX cases and worked well! Low cost solution for splitting fans
text: Works very well for splitting pwm fan header on itx mother board with only 1 cpu fan header and a second fan header where I needed to run 7 fans. As one user pointed out both side have to be plugged in. One side goes to the fan header. I chose CPU fan header to split so all fans ran at the same RPM. The other side goes to a sata power connector. The first connection on this board should be the highest RPM fan that you have if using multiple. This way when the fans calibrate it will read the highest RPM fan at the first section. Connect the 4 pin PWM fan to this section and all subsequent fans in sequence. RPM shows fine in iCue software. You will not see each fan but one reading for all fans. iCue allows a calibration of the fans which is optimal for ensuring the system recognizes the appropriate RPM for say noctua fans that run at higher RPMs than other brands. That should be your first fan. Any others will run at full speed within their respective RPM ranges as designed even if less than say a 1600 RPM noctua fan. 100%  for a noctua ran at about 1538 rpm. Within the fans plus or minus tolerance of RPM deviation.

text:
They've removed the listing for the cameras I bought, but I have 6 of these. The picture quality is fine for the price. The real issue with these cameras is the motion detection and the app.

Motion detection is inconsistent and often delayed in notifying you. I'll get alerts for motion that happened an hour ago, and I can't stop them from coming in. Sometimes I get no alerts for motion at all.

The Wi-Fi is hit or miss. I have repeaters all over my house and strong signal where these cameras are posted. Every one of my cameras reports signal in the 50% range.

*Edit - about the app
The app is just awful. It's called "Adorcam" and I suggest you read up on it yourself - 2.6 stars on 50k+ reviews. The app is so bad that I will likely replace the cameras.

The biggest problem for me is the motion detection. Some reviews mention that the motion detection in the camera is inconsistent. The issue that I have is that the motion detection is delayed from the app. Very laggy... I'll get alerts for motion 30 minutes to an hour afterwards and I can't stop them by disabling motion detection, because that only prevents FUTURE alerts. So the delayed alerts just keep rolling in one after the another.

I've tried to disabling motion detection, and that is also inconsistent. I've tried sitting the motion detection to the different modes, the app seems to just respond to motion when it wants to.

Another issue is arming the cameras for motion. If you want the cameras to do their motion detection at certain times of the day or during certain events like leaving the house, you have to do each camera individually. There's no setting for arming/disarming them all at once. I have quite a few cameras, and it's a pain.

This would be a five star review if they would just update that app.

Auto-calibration can be done in a snap, and setting parameters is also a breeze. This stabilizer is great for those who want full control of their shooting.

This is an honest review and I have not been paid to write it, which is a huge problem with Amazon reviews. Just Google “buy Amazon reviews” if you don’t believe me.

For starters, it can be charging while it is being used, and as far as I’m concerned, that’s a necessary feature that many similar products lack. It’s because I have a car that is destined to be a collectible classic, so I’ve kept the stock stereo, which has a cassette player — but no auxiliary input, yet I was a “early adopter” of MP3 technology, hooking an original iPod to my stereo via a cassette adapter, then another, then another, and so on.

title: Make Sure That.....
text:
This review is for the NETGEAR CM500-100NAR DOCSIS 3.0 Cable Modem purchased for $29.95 in December of 2021.

I recently upgraded my Internet package to 100Mbps download with Xfinity which meant I had to upgrade my cable modem. Since DOCSIS 3.1 modems are expensive selling for over $100, I selected a compatible fast DOCSIS 3.0 modem. Decided on this refurb model. Note that this model is the same as the Netgear CM500-100NAS (CM500-100NAR the 'R' stands for Refurbished).

First off, make sure that whatever modem you buy is listed as compatible with your Internet service provider AND supports the rated speed of your Internet package. This modem supports download speeds up to 680Mbps download.

Also, note that you will need to call your Internet service provider to provision the new modem. You cannot simply swap out your old cable modem with this one and expect it to work.

Overall, happy with the purchase. It's much more cost-effective to buy rather than rent the cable modem. If the cable modem works during the initial setup then 99.9% percent of the time it will work forever.

So,

(1) make sure that this modem is on the compatible list from your Internet service provider.
(2) That your service package is below 680Mbps download.
(3) Call your service provider when you provision (install) the modem.

Good luck!

title: Value is so-so but for those serious about records, it's better than a crate.
text:
Right off the bat, the value of this is pretty rough. Almost forty bucks for essentially a few pieces of wire and wood. The cardboard case with foam liner almost feels like better quality than the actual product! It was a shame to throw it away but it did a nice job of protecting the product. I was expecting the actual unit to be a little more heavyweight ... the wooden slats feel like particleboard but I am assuming that they are solid wood, as the description says.

My biggest gripe about this is how hard it is to adjust the pegs. Once the pegs are inserted into the little holes, they are VERY hard to remove ... so if you want to to raise or lower the amount of records, you will have to do some twisting and turning and manipulation of the pegs to remove and move them. I heard a crack when I first tried this, so I figured I'd just leave it where it is. I think this would be better if it had some grooves or channels cut into the bottoms near the holes to keep the records upright. I find that the records tend to slide down a bit at a 15 degree angle.

The thing I do like about this, is it allows me to pick out a bunch of records to play at a party or whatever, without having to pick through the columns of records in my shelf. I can pull 8 or so albums ahead of time and put them into the product, which makes them easily accessible. You can also put about 20 albums in the unit and let people look through as to what they want to play vs. having to bend down and pull out of the shelves. It's a good 'now playing' holder as well.

It doesn't take up as much real estate on a shelf or table as a crate or longer record holder would. I can easily fit it on the shelf with my amp and my turntable, whereas a crate would never fit. It can tip over when loaded up with records, so just be careful of that. I like that it has little foam pads on the bottom, which help it from sliding around and also from scratching the surface it is on.

The wood is dark-ish and looks a bit retro ... like 1970's retro. If you have a more modern system like a TT or shiney plinth, this could contrast negatively. If vintage and retro are the vibe you are going with, it would fit right in. The wire parts aren't as silver as they look in the photo ... they almost look dull gold or tarnished pewter.

Overall, the vinyl resurgence is really driving up prices for accessories. If this was for sale as a dish drying rack, you could easily find it for under $5. However, because vinyl collectors will buy it, it's almost $50 which in my opinion is way too expensive. It's quality is okay but nowhere near the price being charged. Still, it's better than a crate and will fit into your small space setup nicely. Your records will still be at an angle a bit unless you stack them in which would make it much harder to flip through them. I'd say to buy this more as a party tool ... or something that allows you to select albums for listening vs. storing albums full-time.

title: Didn't work on my 13" Mac Book Pro
text:
I hate giving 1-star reviews, but this product just did not work with my MacBook Pro. I had to access data on a CD-ROM and thought this would work because it was USB-C. When I inserted the disc it made lots of attempts to read it (the motor whirred and span) but nothing ever came up on the Mac - it just was not recognized. I tried a regular music CD, and that didn't work either - same thing - lots of whirring, then nothing. I had the Music app open and I was able to use the Eject control in it to eject the CD once. Other times it failed. I then tried a DVD thinking that maybe I had it all wrong and this was *only* a DVD player, but that too did the same thing - lots of whirring, no action in the OS. Kill Bill Volume 2 will just have to wait. The instruction pamphlet says that you need an app to use the player and if you don't have one to contact them and they'll give you one, but that doesn't make sense - if I stick in a CD-ROM it should pop up like a disc volume in Finder. I can only think that either the unit I received was actually broken, or this drive is no longer compatible with macOS Big Sur. For reference, I have a MacBook Pro (13-inch, 2017, Two Thunderbolt 3 ports) running the latest version of Big Sur.
Thankfully, Amazon's return policy is very good and I dropped off the drive at the UPS Store. I'm now gun-shy about buying another one of these things as I expect almost all of them use the exact same internals, so I'm going to try and find another way to read these CD-ROMs.
