title: May not work for your device
text:
I bought this so I could add a remote tap for Earphone Station to my sound bar audio feed. After playing around with this for a while, and troubleshooting all the hardware in my setup, I determined that this cable splitter was the culprit. The fit in the TOSLINK on my TV was "iffy" as any jiggling caused the audio on my sound bar to drop in and out and even sitting stationary, it would have noise occasionally. I could never get it to work with my TOSLINK to Analog converter that I was using to feed my Headphone Amp.

I suspect that since this is a passive device (not powered / amplified) you're reducing the light amplitude of the signal by 1/2. This may be ok for some devices especially if they're tuned to accept lower light levels, but my Digital / Analog converter was not having it and my Samsung soundbar just barely worked.

I went ahead and ordered a powered splitter (powered splitters work the same except they take the signal and re-drive the outputs at full level on their own amplified output so there is no signal loss). I plan to keep this since it wasn't that much and I may be able to use it for something in a future project.

title: Defective design? Gain is set too high. Also, my unit was defective.
text:
Bought this a little over a year ago, and recently noticed some "hiss" from my speakers from a few feet away. I have low sensitivity bookshelf speakers, so was really stunned I was hearing the noise floor of the amplifier.

I contacted Denon and dropped it off at a local service center, and they told me my phono stage was kaput? Like, I never even used the phono stage? Am I being taken for a ride? Whatever, three weeks later and I pick it up, and my unit works like new. However, the hiss is still there.

I notice that if I use a line level input (2 Vrms) my unit gets DEAFENINGLY loud at 9 o'clock on the volume knob. This is just insane. I can only move the volume knob 20 degrees from zero before it's just too loud. This seems like a flaw with this unit, as I have read others had the same fault with theirs. The gain is either set too high, or the volume pot they use is exponential, meaning there is no fine-tuning the volume, it's just "loud" all of a sudden.

If you want to use this for quiet listening, go for Yamaha, as they have a loudness dial for this exact purpose. The Denon is just not engineered correctly.

title: FAKE USB CAPACITY - BUYER BEWARE
text:
A coworker purchased this "RUICHENXI 1TB USB Flash Drive 3.0" in order to store media for viewing on a television via a Micca MPLAY-HD Mini. I was suspicious of the price when he told me he only paid $20 for a 1TB USB 3.0 Flash drive when the going rate is roughly 7 times that price ($140 and up).

My suspicions were proven true when I attempted to transfer over 32gb of videos to the drive. It created all the icons for the files but when I tried to open the videos in VLC not a single video frame played. And when I tried to open any accompanying subtitle files (.srt) they wouldn't open in Notepad++ or Notepad. When I removed the USB drive and plugged it back in, everything that was "transferred" after it reached the 32gb limit disappeared. I formatted the drive multiple times and tried again one file at a time, and as soon as I reached the invisible 32gb file limit the same thing happened. As you can see in the included screeshot, when you look at this drive in "Devices & Drives" under "This PC" it appears to have 947gb of disk space. I eventually scanned it with ChipGenius v4.19 which revealed that this "1TB USB Flash Drive 3.0" is in fact a 32GB USB Flash Drive 2.0.

title: Does just what I wanted.  But a pain to install.
text:
We have a three-story urban home, with the broadband line entering on the top floor. Even with a range extender installed on the second floor, our reception was spotty, especially on the ground floor. Since we don't use many wifi devices, and have only a medium-speed broadband connection, I didn't see a particular need for an expensive WiFi6 mesh router. So I saved a lot by getting this Orbi.

Have had it two weeks now, and it's turned out to be an excellent choice. Download speed significantly better, and a huge increase in upload speed, on all floors. No more dropped connections, buffering streaming movies, or blind spots in the house. Couldn't be more pleased.

Installing it, however, was another matter. Evidently when the ORBI was first introduced, you installed it via a web browser. Then Netgear created a phone app for installation. But the company left instructions for both types of installation on its support site, not indicating when, or even if, you are supposed to use one or the other. The instructions do try to steer you away from using the browser, yet there seem to be many operational adjustments you can make only through the browser. For example, the support site gives a detailed two-part instruction for installing Orbi if you have Verizon FIOS, which we do. I did the first part, but couldn't access the browser to do the second, which sets the Orbi in "AP mode" (whatever that is). I finally took a chance and used the app to finish the installation anyway. Surprisingly, it worked. I'm still not sure I did everything correctly, and the whole installation ended up taking hours -- unnecessarily, in my opinion.

So if you have the patience to deal with a possibly confusing installation process, I think you'd be pleased with the Orbi.

title: MINE CAUGHT FIRE
text: .  Recently, I bought this case, and today I was finally able to boot up my Fiance's PC.  Note.. This was to be a birthday gift for her.  I have built about 20 PC's for friends, family, and other people I know.  I am no novice to the world of PC building.  Upon firing up her PC, everything was fine for about five minutes.  Then one of the fans on the case sparked and shorted out.  Causing electrical smoke to carry throughout her PC.  I had just finished building it with all new parts.  I had ran tests on the PSU and everything in my  actual PC.  everything was fine, but the case fan sparked, and then melted the cables.  I heard a click, the bottom front fan stopped lighting up, stopped spinning, and then caught fire.  I unplugged everything, and set the entire PC outside.  I waited on it to cool down because I now have minor burns all over my hands.  I pulled all of her parts out of the PC.  Every single piece is now covered in smoke.  Her hard drive sounds horrible now.  I am unsure if anything else works in it at this time. Her nearly $1500 build is probably ruined because of this case.  I am so incredibly frustrated.  What would have happened had I not been home?  What would have happened if I did not take it outside.  There is melted fan cables inside the case I am sending back to you.  Hell, one of the fans that proceeded to melt sheered right through itself and is no longer even attached.  I have attached a ton of images to show you.  This case could have burnt my entire apartment complex to the ground. Everything in the office now reaks of electrical smoke.  As far as damages to the rest of the PC goes, It scorched one of the cables on my PSU which I will have to trash now.  Once I began to delicately remove cables, the USB 3.0 cable that is built into the case, ripped my USB 3.0 header off of my motherboard, so now I have to get a new motherboard on top of it.  It has made the rest of the cables a nice smoky brown (It was a white Corsair PSU with all white cables).  Pretty much looking at a possibly junked out $1500 PC because this case decided to go inferno.  My Fiance and I are now going to sleep at our neighbors so we can air out our apartment(we both have asthma).  I have never had an issue like this in my entire history of PC building, upgrading, and part swapping.  I ordered this case because it had a ton of positive reviews.  I am unsure if those reviews are fake bot reviews or what, because the experience I got is not what the reviews stated.  The parts I now have to buy include a new main motherboard cable, a new motherboard, and probably a new hard drive.  On top of my hands now having burns on them, I have to take off of work because of all of this.  My fiance, our cat, and I have to sleep somewhere else because our apartment is currently hell to breathe inside.  This has been single-handedly the worst PC part experience I have ever had.  To tell you how tailored I am when it comes to PC building, I check recommended current and voltage for all of my parts and test the current and voltage on my PSU.  That is how I know it was the case/installed fans that are the problem.  I want reimbursed for any parts that are potentially damaged, because of your quality assurance's negligence.

title: Excellent camera for home use
text: So this product is perfect for our front porch. It is usb powered and we snaked the wire up to our outlet on the second floor porch. The things I love about this camera: it’s shareable between my cell phone and my wife’s phone, you can customize where you want the motion detection to pickup and not pickup motion (our camera points towards road and I can literally draw a line in the app to just the sidewalk and in towards my house), you can turn the motion detection light on or off (we like to keep ours off), the night vision is great, pickups up great audio, you can also speak into your phone and it will play your audio through the camera to a would be burglar or just saying hi to your family, has a siren option you can alert your neighbors if somethings wrong, and the play back feature is great. You can adjust how long after detection of motion you want to keep recording. We have it set to 45 seconds and it’s good on memory. We bought a 64G memory card for the device and we can go back weeks of videos. We only have one camera but will be getting one for the back yard. title: Hands down, the worst Plantronics earbud ever
text:
The sound quality is great! Both I and the people on the other end agree on that.

The battery life isn't bad, but is nowhere near as advertised (it's just Plantronics' standard 6 hours talk time, 24+ hours idle time, nothing special). It's no different than the battery life of the first Plantronics earbud I ever bought back in 2010.

Edit 2022-02-08: Over time, the battery life has gotten A LOT better. Insanely so! I use the earbud at least once every day and it sits idle on my ear for at least a couple of hours at a time every day. I've only had to charge it every 2nd to 3rd day, and when I charge it the little thing goes from dead to "7 hours talk time" in one hour or less, even when trickle-charged from the USB port on a computer.

If anything this earbud is outfitted with the exact opposite of background noise cancellation. While driving with the windows up, a motorcycle passing with 3 lanes between us was so loud that the caller had to ask me to repeat what I was saying because of it. The caller even identified it as a motorcycle engine. While standing on my back porch, the sound of small dogs barking at least a block away was so loud that the caller commented on it. I could barely hear it, myself, but the caller heard it loud and clear enough to be bugged by it. In other words, this earbud actually cancels my voice in favor of grossly amplifying faint background noise.

The answer/redial button is on the butt end of this thing. The volume up/down buttons are on one edge. The sliding power switch is on the opposite edge from the volume controls. So, if the thing is powered on, there is absolutely and positively no way to turn it off without fumblingly hitting the redial or volume buttons (because you have to brace the earbud to make the switch slide). There is no mute button at all.

It's better than nothing, and definitely better than the idiotic full headset crap most bluetooth device manufacturers are trying to push instead of standard hands-free earbuds. Even the company that used to be Plantronics has few or no attractive and unobtrusive earbuds for sale on their own website, in 2021.

title: No way to have a seamless transition when battery dies
text:
UPDATED REVIEW 1/5 Stars (4/13/21)
In addition to all the other problems with this, they are super annoying in trying to both turn on and turn off. You have to hold them for 5-8 seconds, if while you are holding the button in the center it shifts to either the left or the right, you have to start all over again. They are poorly designed for shutting down or starting up. On start up you get blasted twice with the BOT. Once to say Welcome, then a pause and it says connected. The volume of the BOT is much louder than the volume of the Headset for listening to the audio on the television. I would NEVER recommend this nor will I ever purchase this brand or anything from this maker again!

UPDATED REVIEW 2/5 stars
OMG this is the worst ever!!! There is ABSOLUTELY NO warning until the battery is dead and then the warning is SOOOOO L.O.U.D!!!! Talk about ear damage. You have the level safe for listening to your program and then the BOT comes on and says "LOW BATTERY" while she Y.E.L.L.S!!! at you, and then, she does it again 30 seconds later. That's it, two 30 second warnings, and then it is D.E.A.D. NO sound!!! There is literately NO timely warning -- (as in an appropriated 30 minutes to let you at least finish what you are doing? Nope!) Low battery should be stated when you turn it on if there is 30 minutes or less left of battery life, not while you're in the middle of using it, and then to give you no time to finish what you are doing?? That's terrible! This is MOST ESPECIALLY true since this pathetic headphones do not have the ability to change out batteries so you can be charging an additional pair in between. Because of the headset is SEALED and one battery for the life of the product, you can't just have a spare pair of batteries waiting to change out as needed. Environmentally irresponsible to not have batteries that change. Health Irresponsible to raise the volume level to tell you the battery is low. And seamless viewing is obliterated without the ability to have an additional pair of batteries in the waiting.

These are NOT consumer friendly!!!

ORIGINAL REVIEW was 4/5 stars
Overall, this is a good headset that does provide the 40 hours it states... actually, I was able to get 40 hours and 22 minutes, so I definitely can't complain about the length of time. (No, I didn't do all 40 at one sitting, but I did keep track so I could see if it gave the 40 hours it claimed), that said there are some things I think could use an improvement.

I am replacing a previous pair of wireless headphones for TV. I always had one set of batteries in the charger and one set in the headphones, when the set in the headphones died, I could immediately replace and not miss a beat of music or an action of movie. Unfortunately, for this headset the battery is integrated into an enclosed sealed non-replaceable location. That means to charge the battery, you must stop what you are doing and charge the battery back-up to speed. ... too bad for you if it's in the middle of the best part of the song, or an action intense part of a movie...cause there is no way around the lost connection when you cannot have a spare battery waiting and ready.

I wonder -- Have headphones in general changed or is it just this particular headset? No idea, but for me that is a bad replacement for continuous use. The other flaw with this is that batteries don't tend to last as long as the product, which means on my old system, I just bought new batteries and it kept going (I didn't replace the headphones because they don't work, but because the new TV won't work with an RCA jack and I needed to switch to an Optical set-up) This means that when the batteries on this set eventually do die, I will be throwing away a LOT more product than what might actually need replaced. Very wasteful and harmful to the environment.

In addition to the lack continuous battery ability, the ear pieces themselves take a bit to get used to. ... no, wait...I'm still not all that comfortable with them, but tolerate them. I have ear piercings, the headphone padding presses the earnings into my head; my original pair did not do this. The padding was big enough on the previous pair to fit around the outside of my ears and not sit directly on top of them pressing them to my head. The padding was also comfortable enough I could wear them for longer periods of time than I can wear this pair. This pair the padding is very stiff and small, squashing my ear (and I am a small person, female and only 5'1", I can't imagine how they would fit a man).

Next, they claim to have 100 foot ability, eh, I don't know that I entirely agree with that. My original headphones had the same range and I could travel farther in my home without disruption of the signal cutting in and out or static on the line. I waled from my office 12 feet to the restroom to wash my hands and they cut out! Twelve FEET, that's not 100. Granted it was from a room to a room but still TWELVE FEET! My original pair I could go down stairs and start a load of laundry between while the advertisements were on hear what was going on and be back to watch as the show resumed without missing a beat, all while my husband was on a conference call so I wouldn't interrupt his work, or while he's sleeping and I'm doing tasks but not with this, I need to stay in the same room.

The transmitter is nice and small, so it doesn't have a big footprint taking up space, so that's a nice feature, though it may also be why they don't reach the distance my original headphones could reach.

So, in conclusion, they do most of what they claim even if they aren't nearly as comfortable as I would like and I do miss the seamless transition when the battery needs charged. For me lack of comfort and the fact I will need to throw away the entire headset just because the battery finally dies and will not further charge making it a waste to the environment, means... I will be in the future looking for a different set up and not getting this item again.

title: Dual monitor mode works well (Windows)
text:
Considered the 7-in-1 hub, which only had the one HDMI input. I had been using one monitor, plugging and unplugging a second HDMI cable to my work laptop when I work from home but kept getting screen flicker and was concerned that continual messing with the cord over and over led to this. Needed a solution that had two HDMI inputs.

I went ahead with the 8-in-1 hub and am very glad that I did. The main selling point over the 7-in-1 is the dual HDMI inputs, and there is Ethernet input too if you’re hardwired, which is more reliable over wireless. Work-issued Dell Latitude 7410 detected both of my 32” LG monitors no problem. Now I don’t have to keep plugging and unplugging the HDMI cables whenever I undock, which is a plus. Just the USB-C, which is quick and easy to disconnect when I need to take my laptop on-site. Can use extension from laptop for a third screen or duplicate as well.

The power pass charging via USB-C is handy, though I have two USB-C ports so don’t need it necessarily. But for one plug and go this option is nice to have.

It’s a little more than I wanted to spend but things are working well thus far and it had what I wanted, so it’s worth it to me. It solves my problem as I reconfigure my home workspace with the dual monitors and other peripherals, almost all of which are accommodated by this hub (too many USB-A items for the hub, but no fault there to this hub; that’s a me problem!) and I have another little hub running those other items.

It does run a little hot, so I hope that doesn’t affect long term usability but that will remain to be seen. Hoping to get a number of years use out of this and expect as an Anker product that should hold true.

Overall a great little hub that covers my needs well. Notably this is a machine running Windows 10. I would have a look at other reviews re: Macintosh if you are on OSX as it sounds like there are limitations within OSX with this hub.

title: Looks good; top layer peels away easily
text:
I figured I had nothing to lose by trying these.

The good news is that the print quality looks the same as a real Brother TZ tape.

The bad news is that the print layer does not adhere very well.

You can easily do the following test yourself to prove that what I say is correct. Print a label using Brother tape, and then print the same label using this tape. Remove the backing and stick both samples onto a surface. Then, take your fingernail and peel each one off that surface. What you'll find is that the Brother tape peels off with both the top layer (where the text is located) and the bottom layer (the substrate containing the adhesive) coming off together. Unfortunately, this cheap tape comes off in two pieces, with the text layer coming off in a mess, ruining the tape. The Brother tape can be re-stuck, something I do once in awhile when I don't get the label aligned very well.

So, the adhesive that sticks the label to the surface works and sticks about the same, but the other adhesive which keeps the letters on the substrate is weak.

I may try a few tests to see if I can "set" the adhesive on this cheap tape by hitting it briefly and carefully with a heat gun.

So, for casual use, these tapes will probably be fine, but if you are putting labels on something that will be in your pocket (like a phone or camera) or will be in any other environment where the label will be touched frequently, I don't think you'll like this product as much as the real Brother labels.

title: Works Great, Easy Setup
text:
I started with a 5-bay NAS from Synology (DS1019+) which gets a lot of use between backups, general file storage, media server, etc. Even though I filled my DiskStation unit with 5x12 TB drives I knew there would come a point where I'd need more storage. This handy DX517 unit made it really easy for me to add 5 more bays to my NAS using the eSATA port.
I believe Synology uses a proprietary eSATA connector, and yes, the cable's not very long, but for my case it was plenty. I have the expansion unit right next to the main DiskStation, but I have plenty of slack in the cable where I could move it to another shelf or further away if needed.
The setup was very quick and easy and the included instructions are equally straightforward. It probably took longer for the unit to shut down and restart than how long it took me to setup it up. And once restarting, the expansion unit automatically powered on and was recognized along with the two additional drives I put in. Also, very easy to either add space to an existing storage pool, create additional pools, or to have a "hot-spare" drive on standby.
I have seen some videos on YouTube with some cautions regarding expanding a storage pool with drives in the expansion unit, but I've had no issues, and keep them both on the same battery backup and run SHR with two-drive redundancy to be safe (along w/ cloud backup).
Long story short, setting up and configuring this expansion unit was a breeze and I've been nothing but happy with this unit so far.

title: Headphones in speaker jack crack and pop. Displayport sometimes cuts out
text:
Lenovo's quality seems to have taken a major hit recently. I have a Chromebook C330 I bought several years ago that I love, and works flawlessly. But the last two Lenovo Chromebooks I bought have both had problems that caused me to return them.

This one has problems with the headphone jack. Music crackles and pops so that it sounds like hifi music is being played on an old record player, or on a cassette tape. I tried the same headphones with a different PC and the problem went away, so I know it's the laptop itself that is causing the problems and not the headphones. In addition, the USB displayport randomly cuts out and the screen goes dark for a few seconds.

This is the second Lenovo laptop in a row I've had to return because it has been defective on arrival. The first one was a Chromebook S330 with display issues. I don't know what's happened to Lenovo, but their quality seems to have taken a major hit lately.

Needless to say, the next one I buy will not be a Lenovo. After two bad experiences in a row, I can only suggest that you look for a different brand. Unfortunately, the recent quality problems with Lenovo laptops do not seem to be limited to Chromebooks, given the number of articles online mentioning issues with the Thinkpad Carbons.

Lenovo, like other vendors, sources their parts from multiple vendors. So even within the same model laptop, there's no way to know which screen you are getting, which keyboard you are getting, etc. It seems Lenovo must be using some less than reliable vendors lately. Bottom line is it's a crap shoot. You may get one that has all legendary quality of old IBM models. Or you may get one that has multiple issues because of lack of quality control in their vendor sourcing. It's not worth the hassle. Do yourself a favor and simply don't buy a Lenovo until they fix the quality control issues that seem to be rampant across their line of laptops right now.

title: Use Auto mode
text:
These fans look fantastic and definitely help keep the cabinet cool. I'm planning a second set for another cabinet already.

In "Smart" mode, the fan may cycle around your set temp too frequently (another reviewer commented about this and I noticed it too). The fans are quiet on the lowest setting, but they aren't silent, so when I set my controller to 80F, the fans would kick on and off several times a minute while the temp bounced between 79F and 80F. When the AV components are on, the temp is typically high enough to keep the fans running, but when they're in standby there's just enough heat to make the fans cycle constantly. This is annoying if you're using the living room for reading but not watching TV, for example. The solution is to stick with Auto mode.

In Auto mode, there's a cycle interval, so the fans come on at 80F and then turn off at 76F or 78F depending on how you set the interval, so the fans don't cycle quite as frequently. If you're sensitive to the noise of the fans, this is the better setting to use and works more like your home thermostat does.

title: Great 2nd monitor, so so on the stand stability
text:
How nice to be able to quickly, easily add a monitor to my iOS device or my Windows device.

It worked perfectly: plug in to my iPad, and voila: a second monitor I can use to mirror my iPad, or extend it with the apps that support it. Note that even though this monitor has a touch screen, the touch screen does not work with iOS. So, it is strictly a read-only device with iOS. On the other hand, when I plug it into a Windows device, it works great as a second monitor AND the touchscreen works exactly as I want it to work. For example, when plugged into my Surface Pro, I can swipe from the right on this monitor and get the exact same results as if I had swiped from the right on the Surface Pro itself.

I can’t stress enough how much I like being able to interact by touch with this monitor. It’s so much easier to be productive when both of my displays are touch-responsive.

My main complaint, and this was rather frustrating: the case/cover/stand that came with this monitor seems quite flimsy. I had a very hard time figuring out how to set it up without the whole thing collapsing. I eventually figured out a way to get it to stand up, but it could easily collapse if bumped just slightly. All in all, it works great as a monitor. I just wish the cover/case/stand were more stable.

title: Worked as advertised. But...
text:
First off I would like to say it is a decent value for money. Definitely easy to install. Adhesion was beyond what I had expected. It definitely stuck to my Western Digital SN 850 2280 M.2 NVME SSD that was used in my Playstation 5. Now it definitely prevented the SSD from giving me the over heating error that I received with the SSD bare. I tried to transfer 7 files/games from my system main to this my WDSN850 SSD M.2. it definitely helped performance overall I don't have numbers but I can confirm that I'v experienced overheating during the Playstation 5 OS beta from 2.0 to 3.1. After applying this Heatsink it was gone. It did its' job with one minor problem. It's size.

Now while I was able to install and put the Playstation 5 shell covers back on I was not able to close the NVME M2 port with it's factory panel which was just a thin flat piece of metal. It was completely functional as a Heatsink but it lingered in the back in of my head that my PS5 was missing a piece of itself, so I had to remove it and got one that fit. That item's review will be posted after more testing. This is a decent value for your money super easy to install on any system including PS5. it's a standard installation. But the heat sink pad ended up being very sticky and hard to remove from the SSD. Why was it stuck so hard? I couldn't tell you. I've had install several different Heat sinks and they were all pretty easy to be removed, not this one. If you want it on there it's going to stay the bands that came with it was basically to help it set in place before adhesion took place. I'd buy it again for another project just not "my PS5". However if you can live without putting that piece of metal back you definitely can use this for your PlayStation 5, however I have a mild OCD that forced me to replace it.

title: Positive changed to how I record video
text:
My channel is BBQ/food centric, requiring a top-down method of filming. I have tried many of the "inexpensive" arms, all with mixed to horrible results, like slowly sinking, claiming to be able to handle 2-3 pounds, but shifting around with far less weight. What I really needed was an inexpensive arm that could hold my camera and a ring light, this one does the job. Unlike some of the other arms, you can actually see the teeth where the joints articulate, this prevents me from torquing them down incorrectly, causing a slip or break, even though the gears/teeth are plastic, as long as you unscrew the handles enough, they shouldnt grind together, and once tightened, they'll stay in place solid. The arms themselves are metal, though, im sure it's painted aluminum, they should be sturdy enough to perform. This doesn't offer the same flexibility or instant articulation like others, but since I need more of a static mount, this will do the job nicely. It's silent, too.

The only two con I see right now is the metal bolts for the articulating joints appear to be surrounded by plastic matching the bolt size, this may be detrimental, but right now, not a concern. The other is that there is no shock absorption method on it, so if your table isn't really heavy or dense, bumping will make it shake, non issue for me personally, as the last overhead I had was rigged up to a chair back in front of the table I use. but it at least should be noted.

There are other, much higher dollar options out there, but since my channel is starting, budget is pretty tight. I imagine I will be buying one or two more in the very near future.

title: Large bag fitting a lot of equipment but still fits under airplane seat as personal item
text:
In the past I used a $70 cheapo camera bag and it could hold 3 sections of gear. I always have my travel tripod inside to prevent damage, and I have a few lenses, camera body, laptop, misc camera accessories. The bag lasted 9 years and it was finally starting to fall apart, so I went looking for a new bag. Unfortunately the original cheapo bag I owned had been discontinued.
I tried 4 other camera bags on Amazon and unfortunately they all had one major issue for me - I could not fit my gear anymore. It seemed that most newer bags expect to put the tripod on the outside to save space on the inside. All new bags seemed so follow this new trend of being slim which I did not want. I needed space to hold a lot of gear, yet still remain large enough to fit under an airplane seat. Not many bags do that now - they all want to go small and light.

Eventually I came across the Lowepro 500 AW II. It was more expensive but at this point I had no other options. When I got it, this bag did exactly what I needed! Plenty of space for 3 sections of gear+tripod! Materials felt pretty good and durable. Had plenty of extra dividers I didn't really need but it's a bonus. And I actually tried fitting it under the airplane seat and it works!!!

If I had to say what the negative/inconveniences were for me:
1. The camera section opens from the back instead of the front.
2. Not as much space to hold small accessories in the front zipper compartment or the inside/laptop compartment area. But they do give you a separate pouch which you can put your accessories inside there and it's velcroed. You'll be able to attach it somewhere inside the camera compartments.

These are just minor inconveniences specific to me though so it may not apply to you.
But this bag checks all the important boxes I need in a good quality durable camera bag so it's perfectly fine!

title: It just works ..with some sensible asterisks
text:
Asrock x570 taichi motherboard here with bios p4.10 wtih 5900x cpu

Currently ALL four of my dimm slots are occupied by one of these 32GB CL18 3600mhz sticks. Having said that with many motherboards with ryzen 5000 series cpus ( unless there is something I'm missing and I think Wendell from Level1techs from youtube mentioned something about this) ..any time you populate all four dimms instead of only two, there is a reasonable chance you won't be able to run your at both the rated mhz speed...AND the advertised timings ( in this case 18-18-18-whatever)

850 watt titanium seasonic PSU here btw on clean power. Cpu is set to auto..no overclocks, suspend to ram is disabled

In my exact scenario. My system will not boot Linux Mint 20.1 cinnamon at 18-18-18-34 at even 3333mhz with all four sticks plugged in ( POSTS...though just fine) where as before with only two sticks I can run 18-18-18-34 at 3400mhz and everything just works flawlessly all day long even under hardcore loads ( cpu at 90+ percent and ram consumption being maxed out with Openshot exporting a bluray movie which is very easy to do as ram consumption will easily clear 64GBs at around the halfway mark depending on the individual movie and how much cgi it has)

Perhaps there are some ram brands/makes/models that can do better than this with all four dimms populated on an x570 chipset ryzen 5000 supported mobo, but I'm not unhappy with my purchase either. I had a feeling what Wendell said might be true and kept my expectations fairly balanced.

I'm currently running at 18-18-18-24 at 3200mhz with all four of these ( 128GBs total). I'm new to overclocking ram in the x570 motheboards ftr...so take all of this with a grain of salt and zero carb zero sugar Truvia while you're at it xD. Regardless Simple things like loading any webpages, refreshing Thunderbird email, etc all work like a champ, very snappy speeds.

With ryzen 5000 series, I've read all over the net where it's really the fastest overall system performance with choosing as low number/latency timings as possible with 3200mhz ( I've read there is a Crucial Balistic sport or some similarly named ram kit in a pair that will handle 3200 mhz at CL 14-14-14-14-32 1T timings...keyword...ONE pair..I doubt it will with both pairs ..a total of four occupying all dimms on an x570 or b550 amd motherboard)..... , or as tight/low latency number timings as possible with 3533 to 3800mhz.

Good job to the seller for fast processing and delivery. Price could have been around 10% better, but what are ya gonna do? Complain given the stupid nand shortage aka lack of supply versus hardcore demand going on ( applies obviously more to gpu's and some cpu's too)? Na. cheers everyone

title: Solid product with solid functionality that will be perfectly fine for most users
text:
I wanted to take the time to review this because most reviews/questions on here are from either "power users"/IT people who (at no fault of their own) use too much jargon for the average user, or dissatisfied customers who did not understand what they needed/what they were buying.

I am working with a 2020 M1 MacBook Pro running OS 11.1 Big Sur (my newly purchased personal computer) and a 2-year-old Dell Latitude 7490 running Windows 10 (my work computer, issued by my employer). I use the MacBook's keyboard for Mac keyboard input, and I use a wired Dell keyboard for PC keyboard input. I like to use my Anker wireless ergonomic mouse for both computers. This is a matter of personal preference. I like to use my single 27" Lenovo monitor interchangeably (not simultaneously) with the Dell and MacBook. I also use a CAT6 Ethernet cable.

THIS DOCK WORKS GREAT FOR ME! Sure, it could have a few more features, a few more ports, and it could ship with a higher-wattage charging cable. But it works great with both computers for passthrough charging and peripheral sharing. I can have my monitor, Ethernet cable, and wireless mouse receiver hooked up to the dock at all times, and whenever I plug the USB-C passthrough cable into either computer, I am able to begin using the monitor, Ethernet connection, and mouse pretty much instantly. The hub offers really speedy USB connections that upgrade the speed of my Dell's ports for external HDD reading/writing, and expand the input/outputs for my Mac's ports. This is value added for both computers.

Now some more technical minutiae for those interested (note, I do not claim to be fully literate in this terminology, I am just doing my best to keep up...)

The key here is that I did not want to get a KVM switch box, so I opted for this as a cheaper and simpler solution -- I really don't care about instantaneous switching when I can just unplug the passthrough USB-C cable from one computer and plug it into the other. Doing this, I can seamlessly switch between computers on the monitor, all while using the same mouse and Ethernet connection. At max there is 5-10 seconds of waiting for the mouse to be recognized when I connect one computer or the other. Maybe that's too long for some users, but it's just fine for me. Hell, I remember when it took 2 minutes for an email inbox to load on a dialup modem and I am only 25 years old. This technology really amazes me.

For users of a Dell laptop such as the Latitude 7490, the included passthrough charger is only 60W, not 100W. The hub supports up to 100W and you can upgrade to that. If you don't, the Dell will be just fine, but if you want "peak performance" (whatever that means from a very mediocre laptop with a 10-year-old processor) Dell says you should make the upgrade. I'll consider it down the road, but for now the 60W works fine for me.

And a couple notes for Mac users, particularly those using Big Sur and/or an M1 Mac:

1. THIS ETHERNET ADAPTER WORKS WITH BIG SUR!!! You may be aware that Apple rendered obsolete the ASIX Ethernet adapters when implementing Big Sur, and that running an ASIX Ethernet adapter on Big Sur/M1 requires disabling a security measure under the hood of your system. You may even be shopping for a new adapter right now because yours was rendered obsolete by the upgrade. The good news is that this is not an ASIX chipset, it's a Realtek chipset, and those work just fine with Big Sur. No muss, no fuss, no need to get under the hood. Just plug and play. (Edit: I had legacy KEXT kernel extensions enabled before I purchased this so that I could run ACE for Audio Hijack, and I'm not sure if that's helping with the plug and play. But, that is much more acceptable from a security standpoint than the workaround required for ASIX adapters.)

2. Certain peripherals running through an Apple Thunderbolt 2-Thunderbolt 3/USB-C dongle may not work with this hub. By way of ridiculous example, I have a very old PreSonus FIREPOD FireWire 400 audio interface that I am too lazy/stubborn to upgrade because it works just fine for podcasting purposes. Unfortunately, in order for that interface to work with my 2020 MacBook, I have to run a FireWire 400 - FireWire 800 cable from the interface, into a FW 800 - Thunderbolt 2 dongle, into a Thunderbolt 2 - Thunderbolt 3 dongle. This ridiculous chain of dongles will not work with the Anker hub, but I'm not sure it will work with *any* hub. When I try to plug it in to the Anker hub, my MacBook displays a notification that the Thunderbolt device must be plugged directly into the Mac. Since the Anker hub is handling all the other peripherals that I need to connect to my MacBook *along with the charging aspect*, I have a port to spare on my MacBook, and I can easily connect the dongle chain to the second port without breaking a sweat. Everything works at that point.

So yes, this loses a star for not shipping with a higher-wattage cable and the above dongle compatibility issue, though the latter is probably not Anker's fault. But at $90, this seems to be one of the most competitively-priced and functionality-packed devices for most users -- and it's from a very trusted brand. I would recommend this to many home users who may also be teleworking during the pandemic, and who need a functional solution to share desktop peripherals between two computers that both have USB-C passthrough charging capability.

title: Failing at the basics: sound quality
text:
Below you will find my opinion on the 2-pack Rocksteady Portable Bluetooth Speakers. If you found this review useful, don't forget to hit that "Helpful" button.

Pros:
-- Easy pairing via bluetooth, not harder than any bluetooth device pairing.
-- Good build quality, they look sturdy and have a nice feel when you handle them. Top and bottom are made of plastic, but the sides seem to be made of aluminum.
-- Typically you place these on hard surfaces (desk, bookshelf etc.), but as a bonus you can also wall mount them.
-- Versatile setup modes. Can work as singles or as a pair. When working as a pair, you can configure left speaker, right speaker, or both playing the same channels.
-- AUX input for external audio. Nice.
-- Illuminated buttons on top with all functionalities you need. Bluetooth, wireless streaming to the other speaker, play/pause, next, previous, volume.
-- One interesting thing to note: since these are essentially two different speakers, you can set the volume at different levels even when they are paired. Very useful to correct uneven distances from the listener (the speaker furthest away can have a higher volume to overcome the larger distance).
-- Impressed by the bass richness, based on my expectations by the physical size of the speakers.
-- Battery life is very good. You can go for hours on full volume.
-- The manual is very well written and easy to follow. Makes the setup process much easier.
-- Comes with chargers and audio cable.

Cons:
-- Connecting the speakers with each other (as a pair) was successful using my iPhone, but when I did that with my computer (bluetooth USB dongle) the sound of the speakers would break every 1-2 seconds. My computer worked great with one speaker, but when they become a pair (one speaker streams to the other) my computer just couldn't. Looks like it's picky about bluetooth devices.
-- I'm disappointed by the sound, and a bit surprised by all the excellent reviews praising the sound. I can definitely hear a buzz when playing music, almost as if the sound is clipping. Like an open hi-hat where both cymbals are cracked. It's more audible for highs. I wouldn't say these speakers have a great sound.

The 2-pack Rocksteady Portable Bluetooth Speakers are a good choice mainly due to their versatility and flexibility. You can have two separate bluetooth speakers or one pair of stereo speakers. You can connect them either wirelessly (via bluetooth) or using standard audio cables. The sound, though, failed to keep up with my expectations. And since this is an audio product, I will remove 2 stars for the subpar sound. Unfortunately I can't recommend this product at this price.

Thank you for reading my review. If you found it useful, don't forget to hit that "Helpful" button.

title: I love this product - Won't be disappointed
text:
I've been working from home since COVID. My home is about 3200 sq ft and I was not getting good signal in my office. I original purchased a Netgear EX7500 in April. It worked well at first, with some hiccups but eventually I caved. It was not reliable, certain devices failed to connect, some it would say connected but didn't have internet. I received several good reviews for Eero so on a whim I caved and bought it (retail for both the Netgear and a pod of three Eero are about the same). I am so glad I did. My wife and I both work remotely full time now. Since I installed these, there have been zero issues at all.

Set up was easy although it is not perfectly clear. The app is user-friendly so if you make a mistake it is easily fixed.

Signal strength is almost always perfectly strong. I haven't seen much latency or lost speed. Might want to pick up the latest model if you plan to use this for something like 4k gaming - but for those who are not professional gamers this is going to work amazingly. (I have a one gig internet package and I'm getting about 95% of that even with several devices connected.)

Save yourself the headache. If you want mesh coverage just get this product. I know, Amazon is taking over the world and now it is releasing products to increase its margins. I get it if you don't want to add another Amazon device, but if the other products did as well I wouldn't recommend this one. If you have an Amazon Alexa device, you can also monitor and control your Eero pods through it - good if you want to limit kids' internet usage. (Last side note: in the App you will see all kinds of things hooked up to the internet. Don't worry too much about it. Most unrecognizable devices are harmless things within your authorized devices that you just didn't know were connecting to the internet.)

title: Sound Quality is meh - not worth it
text:
Some context: I am not an audiophile but do appreciate high fidelity sound and true noise cancellation.

These guys are incredibly overpriced and while designed really well, the sound quality itself was a bit of letdown for me. Before buying the AirPods Max my primary headphones were AirPods Pro and Bose QC35 - two of the most common "daily drivers" I'd assume. So when trying out the AirPods Max, I was expecting a much higher quality sound, but I personally couldn't tell a distinct difference from the QC35.

They're heavy. Not the best for walking and listening.
I work from home and always try to pace around the house on calls that don't require me to be on screen. Walking around with these guys takes some getting used to, to the worst be totally a noticeable difference in weight as compared to other competitors.

It comes with an oddly shaped case that is kind of a pain to have to carry along since the headphones have to be in the case to turn off. This is definitely a very "Apple" move, but I'm failing to find any logical reason they'd plan it this way - could it just be a ridiculously bad oversight?

The volume control knob is nice. I often turn it in correctly. Definitely worth checking the settings right away and adjusting the knob and button actions.

Bottom Line: The physical construction of these is incredible. They feel luxurious but a little heavy. The noise cancellation is decent. But the sound is not impressive, in my opinion after about 2 months of use. So if you want a physically beautiful, high quality set of headphones to just keep at your desk, and don't mind just "decent" sound and a wildly high price, buy these. If not, check out Sony, Bose, etc for cheaper premium headphones that will deliver similar if not better sound quality.

Set up was easy and accomplished within 10 minutes. This included getting the complimentary initial cloud storage set up. I am currently not using the optional SD card but plan to when the complementary cloud storage ends to test the two to see which way I choose to use.
So far I am very impressed and happy with this top notch, affordable camera.
I am also impressed with the included but optional magnetic mount. I really like this idea and believe it will really streamline the charging process making it easier to remove and replace.
Once I get a good database on the charging and best position for image quality, I will make my final decision on the placement.

title: Exceptional camera for the price!
text:
I'm a huge fan of Amcrest cameras, and this 5 megapixel camera might be one of my new favorites, especially for the price! This is a power over ethernet camera, so make sure you either have a POE switch, or buy a power injector. I love that this camera is quite small, can easily be wall mounted, and has all the necessary features in a POE camera.

I love that all of the Amcrest cameras are both accessible using the Amcrest app, but also through an RTSP stream, so if you have your own DVR, like Blue Iris, this camera will very easily work!

One big tip that I will give everyone using any POE outdoor camera is to take care to protect the Ethernet port from water. If you have the camera under the eave of a roof, then you will not have any problems. But if your camera will be fully exposed to the rain and snow I highly recommend you protect the cable by putting it in a box, or even just a zip-lock bag that is zip-tied closed and upside down. Water and ice will always find a way into the Ethernet jack, and since you are running power across the Ethernet cable, it is very likely you will burn out the jack if you don't protect it. I now put all of my outdoor camera jacks in a bag, and I haven't had a single issue in years now!

As for other features of the camera - it has a great infrared light, so the night vision is great.

Overall, this camera is absolutely worth twice the price, so if you are looking for a good POE camera, you will be very happy with this!

title: Poor tuning freq - Port noise
text:
[[VIDEOID:8f21c566fed4a53a360a6dd34f507f4d]] Got this box for my daughters car.
I normally custom build my own enclosures but she was pressed for time and it was easy to just have this one shipped.

We had two Fosgate P2D2-12s to install in it. As other reviews have mentioned, the P2 & P3 series will not simply drop in for install.
You must trim the hole bigger. One reviewer suggested that it was just the liner over spray but that was not the case for me.
I had to use a coarse sanding barrel on my dremel and destroyed two sanding barrels to get both holes to work. The liner materials get gummed up in the sand paper.
I could have used a jig saw but I like my subs to just barely slip into place for a tight seal. So the dremel was preferable to me.

All in all, the box build is solid and great for what you pay but....
I wish I would have paid a little more and got the Skar box which has a better tuning frequency.
If you listen to rock or country, this box may be ideal for you but if you want deep, low bass... it's not tuned low enough for that.

I tested this box with the subs installed and the tuning sits right at 45 hz. Not sure who came up with the idea that it's tuned to 40hz or lower but it simply is not.

Being at 45hz, is just does not hit the lows very well. Anyone that says different, has probably never heard their subs In a properly tuned enclosure. So they think it sounds great.
These subs were previously installed in a custom built box that was tuned to 35hz and it absolutely slammed. In this box the Fosgate subs sound mediocre.

Lastly, there is a "lot" of Port noise (chuffing)
If it's in a trunk, you may never hear it but if it's in the cabin with you, you'll hear it.

It is compact for smaller spaces and the overall build is solid but just wasn't what I'd hoped for.

Video is of the box is in my 2006 Durango on approx 2,500 RMS watts to test before installing it in my daughters 2018 Chrsyler 200

title: Not amplified
text:
Updating my review 12/23/21 at the request of the seller. They offered to refund my money, but I want others to fully understand what you are buying.

Pros: seems well constructed. Very small (see photo). Provides 1080p higher definition when signal is good. It is an indoor/outdoor antenna. It’s omnidirectional which is great because you don’t have to move it to pick up specific stations, though in general you get better reception if you point a directional antenna.

Cons: This is not an amplified antenna, so the signal strength can be pretty low. It must be unobstructed (either window or outside would be best). We live directly across the water from most of the local TV stations but cannot get a strong signal. We’re only 35 feet above the water, so there could be some low hills and trees blocking some signal strength. We’re about 7 miles away from a major city.

I’d love to test this on my roof. That might solve the signal issues. I’m going to test it in my RV on the road. Cheers.

* The case offers good protection and includes a handy power level read-out, so you can monitor the amount of energy remaining and anticipate when to recharge.

title: ATTN HD599 users: worthy replacements on a budget
text:
I've tried several non-genuine Sennheiser earpad replacements for my HD599's due to the scarcity of the official brand online. These are the last in a long line, while I wait for a shipment of officials from overseas, and my search for a worthy backup has finally ended.

These earpads do not trap and muffle the sound like so many other replacements, which seem to be made for a different type of headphone drivers. These are soft, light, barely noticeable on the skin and if you're budget conscious then I cannot recommend them higher for HD599's. And while the color of the pads is not an exact match to the originals, it's close enough to not look terribly out of place.

In summary: thank you, Geekria, for making a replacement that doesn't drastically alter the sound quality of these particular headphones. I cannot speak to any other model, just the 599s.

edit: When I bought these I had a pair of genuine 599 earpads on order. Those finally came in and I have to reiterate: the Geekria pads are a worthy substitute. The Geekria are just a millimeter or two thicker, a tad more firm and fill out the velour just a bit more, while having a less pronounced slope. I'll be keeping them safely stored away for the next time my genuine pads fall apart.

title: Great smart watch for basic functionalities, updates can make it even better
text:
I have small wrists, and was happily surprised that it fit me! It even fit my 8 yr old daughter when we tried it on her.

The watch works well for time, step counting, and heat rate monitoring. I consider those the basic functionalities. I did not try the sleep tracking as I was not interested in the feature and would not like sleeping with a watch on my wrist.

I connected the watch to my phone without any major issues (I did have to restart bluetooth a time or two, but it was no different than any other device setup, except that it was done through the app and not through the phone bluetooth directly). It was handy to get text messages (no photos) on my arm when my phone was in a backpack nearby.

The watch is simple and intuitive to use.

App functionality definitely has some room for improvements, but the critical pieces are there, and for the price it has plenty as-is. The 101 help/guide info gives me a website error- not sure if it is my phone or the app itself.

I did wish that there were more customizeable options for the watch face, though it's a minor complaint that could be changed in a future firmware update. There are 3 default displays you can choose from, which is nice, but I wanted to switch from 24 hr time to 12 hr time, and there was no option for that. I also really liked the standard watch face option, which showed HR but not # steps (I would rather see steps than HR, or both would be ok).

Overall it's a great little watch and meets my needs and desires.

title: Easily installed in 2009 Acura MDX
text:

I tried the 'baking' method to fix my HFT, which now works but it drains your battery. Also the HFT unit is only for making / receiving calls, it does not stream bluetooth music in a MDX.

So I found about this BT45-ACU unit (there are different versions for a US or a Canadian MDX), which I found a YouTube video on how to install it. It took about 30 minutes to install the unit, install the microphone and get the unit working in my vehicle.

Just gotta make sure the connections snap together correctly and securely. Now I can stream music from my phone thru my NAV unit (it uses the XM1 channel) and also make receive / calls without worrying about a battery drain (my HFT unit is disconnected, even though it works).

**Update** 8/5/2021
So, almost 6 months in and this AVR is perfect!! Without a doubt, at this point, it has been flawless! Really enjoying it for movies, streaming and TV. Watched 'A Quiet Place II' and the audio and picture were amazing. The audio is crystal clear. From dialogue, to low rumbling bass, to high volume gun fire and explosions, to the tinkling of a beer glass hitting the floor and breaking. Just Amazing. I have Klipsch speakers. I don't have Klipsch front Atmos towers, yet. But that will be the next purchase. (Just bought them!!)
If you buy one or you buy something else, put fans on it. I bought, from Amazon, the AC Infinity MULTIFAN S7-P dual 120mm Fans and put them on top and the receiver runs cool to the touch.

* Update regarding the last 2 sentences of my first review below in March of this year.*

*4k 120Hz PlayStation 5 performance is flawless! My son played a few games and everything worked as it should. He was very impressed with the video performance and the sound quality that this AVR produces with my new Sony 4k HDR TV. He's an avid gamer so that is accurate information from someone who knows. Hope this helps anyone with questions about PlayStation 5 compatibility with this receiver.*

I read dozens upon dozens of reviews and comments before I decided to buy this receiver. It's too bad that we live in a time where buying electronics is such a 'crap-shoot'. Is it going to last a week, a year or ten years like the Onkyo did? I have never owned a Denon product before so there was a little apprehension in the purchasing of the X3700H. As I said, I came from an Onkyo that has been flawless for the past ten years or so but with a TV upgrade, the Onkyo was outdated. First I tried a manual setup using my flawed hearing (I'm Old) and it didn't sound as good as it should, so I did the Audyssey MultEQ XT setup and Wow, it sounds amazing! Actually, I'm going to use the Audyssey setup again and refine the seating positions and mic locations to fine tune it.
This Receiver gets slightly warm but not hot as others have said, so I put a pair of 120mm fans on top, just in case and the metal feels cool to the touch.
So, a month into using the receiver and no problems, flawless performance and glad I made the purchase. I hope it stays that way.

*As to 4K 120Hz performance I can not comment. My oldest son will be here to visit in a couple of months with his PS5 so he'll test it and I will update my review then.*

title: Important: If you do a factory reset, you have to "forget" the unit in UniFi or you are doomed
text:
I have 5 of these deployed over about a 20 acre property. Once you get them set up, the range is awesome and the UniFi mgt system is great. Once you get them set up. Because I am deploying remote units, I do the initial setup at the main router before I deploy them. This turns out to be tricky. Here is what I found works for both mesh and wired uplinks.

1) Open the box and connect the unit to your network via ethernet. UniFi will discover it and have you adopt it and upgrade the firmware.

2) Once the firmware update is done, do a factory reset (paperclip useful) on the unit so it forgets it had a wired up link

3) Unplug the unit and go back to the UniFi interface. Go to the device configuration and select "Forget this device"
If you don't do that, UniFi puts you in a death loop of connecting and disconnecting endlessly after you have moved the unit to, say, the top of a water tank. Sigh.

4) Deploy the unit where you will (wired or wireless) and UniFi will rediscover it. Then you can adopt it into the network. Wireless adoption takes some time - like 5 minutes. Wired is faster.

5) Then make any other config changes you want

If you skip the "forget the device" step, you will not be able to connect the device the network, nor do any configuration. Note that in order to get to the "forget device" menu item, the device needs to be unplugged from the network. If it is still in the death loop trying to connect, the "forget device" option is not available.

This is not an unusual use model and Ubiquiti should make this much easier. I returned a unit before I figured this all out. I assumed because it wouldn't connect wired or wireless after a factory reset that it was broken.

title: Good Soundbar for Bedroom
text:
After mounting TV, the sound from the TV speakers seemed underpowered. This sound bar did the trick. Sound quality is good. Connectivity is good, Bluetooth, hdmi, and optical options included required wires.

Wallmount installation was simple. It came with a foolproof paper cutout you tape to the wall, use a level, make your marks, and drill holes. Slides right in to slots that are screwed to the wall. It is not heavy and does not need to be drilled into studs. Of course you could just set it down instead, as it has rubber "feet" on the bottom.

I currently have it connected via Bluetooth. I wish there was a way my Hisense TV remote would power on the TV and soundbar at the same time. Right now I have to turn each device on with their individual remotes, then use the TV remote to adjust sound. If I use HDMI the TV remote will *sometimes* turn on both, but I have to go into the TV settings and enable the soundbar hdmi output each time I turn on the TV.

Works, nonetheless, for a bedroom. Doesn't shake walls or anything. This provides much better sound than a TV alone. I would recommend something more powerful for a living room entertainment system. Value for money is definitely good. Doesn't seem cheap.

title: Attractive, robust, chunky short-trip backpack
text:
It is a seemingly robust, decently sized day or couple day pack. It has chest and stomach clipping straps, and almost enough strap adjustability to achieve optimal comfort. The ergonomic design has nothing on a true hiking or backpacking pack, and I suspect it would begin to be uncomfortable on a long walking or hiking trip. It is perfect for public or personal transit to pack ones equipment out to a specific shooting location, or for a short hike.

There is enough room in the "laptop pocket" on the back of the bag for a water pack! The tube takes some work to get it to lie flat, and an extra elastic or velcro band might help it look better, but this pack CAN be converted into a water backpack.

I purchased this model for the side-access camera pocket, hoping that it would allow me to quickly access my camera without removing the pack while on a hike (something I can currently do with my old side bag). It is possible to get the camera out without taking the bag off, though it is a little awkward, and very difficult to get the pocket zipped back up all the way after. If the zippers are not in the right position to start, it is pretty much impossible to get the pocket open with the pack on, too.

The final comment is the bag does seem chunky and bulky when it is worn, which could be a desired aesthetic or could be a negative, depending on what you're looking for! Otherwise a very attractive bag

title: 5 stars - A good sound value.
text:
These are about the best wireless buds that I have used. They sound great and the Jabra App is good with features too.
I like the comfort fit (4 out of 5) in the ear and the really good sound isolation which offers sound passing through (hear thru) to allow out side noises. You can raise and lower volume on the buds, you press a button to activate on the bud. You can use just one bud (will be mono, but that's okay). Bass is good and I actually heard "new" instruments and sounds in songs that I have listened to before.
A lot of good sounds and well thought out Bang for the Buck. Well worth $125, but at $79 a real bargain for the quality sound value and feature.
Note: I have the standard Medium sized buds and while walking the ear fit is so sealed that I can actually hear the sensation of sound/pressure from my footsteps. This was unusual and distracting. The volume was on lower even outdoors as the sound isolation due to the well sealed fit did not require high volume. I raised the volume a little more and notice less of the sensation but it was still there. This type of occurrence could actually happen with other brands and models of well sealed or fitted ear plugs. I may switch to the smaller sized ear gel plug to see and hear any improvement as this may alleviate the seal and pressure (but hope they don't fall out of ear either). However the sound and features are so amazing and great that I believe I would still keep these and would definitely use them, due to the comfort sound and features. I have two pairs of the original air pods with an over the ear cover that helps the pods for on your ear without falling out, and those still are the most comfortable and have lasted long. The sound and features of the Elite 3 is much better (granted they are almost three years in design ahead of the air pods). I dig the Navy Color on the Jabra and they stayed in my ears and did not fall or slip out (this fit could vary with the shape and size of your ears). I am using these on my Androids: Samsung Note 10 plus and also Sony Xperia 1 Mark 3. I have used Amazon Music, Tidal, and Spotify (which the Elite 3 allows you to hot button to connect to Spotify by two taps on the left ear). Sound phone quality is really good. It is a winner and a excellent value. I would say these may probably sell out before Christmas and may even have a price bump like the new Soundcores (that turned me off). If you register in the app the warranty bumps to two years. So for half the price of others you will probaby find this to be a literal good sounding value.
PS Update, I have experienced that these ear buds require you to run the Jabra App to listen from the smartphone you are listening too (it seems to get all the features running, not ecstatic about that, but still a good product. I will use my original air pods to listen to Apple, Android, and other bluetooth devices that do not requite an app to listen, for that)

title: Big price for small gain but, hey, a great picture IS worth 1,000 words
text:
Call me greedy but my RF 100-500 comes up a tad short sometimes. Missed shots because, even with cropping, I'm just a tad short. While I love my R5, native lens options are still in their infancy, so what's a guy to do? The only option is either suffer, buy a non-native lens and adapter, or live with the 1.4x or 2.0x RF extenders. I chose the latter.

Before I go further, please know the RF extenders only work in a handful of RF lens, The RF 600, 800, and 100-500. They won't work in any other lens out right now (July 2021). So if that's not you, you can stop reading here.

Before I bought the RF 1.4x I rented the 2.0x, because, hey for $100 more I could get 1000mm reach instead of 700mm. The 2.0x is really nice, but it didn't suit my style of run and gun photography. I see a picture I take it, I don't sit in a blind for hours waiting for something to happen. Because the RF extenders are an odd-duck on the 100-500 and must be attached with the lens at 300mm (which will become 2.0x) I can't get a good handle on my surroundings at 600mm. I need to zoom out a little and then zoom back in. So that was out.

The 1.4x, for me, is easer to handle on the move. It converts my 100-500 lens to a 420-700mm lens which is great for shooting birds in flight or even perched birds or bison, or bears where, again 500mm is just a tad short because of the distance between you and the animal. But I've also used it at zoos and it makes for great animal portraits. Their is really no perceptable loss of sharpness, something I can't say when you put on some junky filters or even old school extenders. But there is a penalty to be paid (other than $). You lose a stop of light, which is a lot for an already slow-ish lens. Focusing is **almost** 100% of the len's capability. It's just a hair slower -- something you noticed but doesn't really affect the outcome.

So my dislikes about the RF 1.4x extender, which I knew going in: 1) on the RF100-500 you are robbed of "wider" angles since it's locked into the 300mm length. So you lose some of the lenses versatility there. And because of how extender is installed in the lens, it's a bit of work to remove it, and not something you'll want do do in the field unless you have a clean, stable platform to do so. So, for me, once it's on, it's on for that shoot. That means you have to really know before you go on a shoot what you intend to be shooting.

2) At $400, it's a lot of money for a 200mm gain. It had me doing a lot of thinking when I could sacrifice some MPs and crop to simulate. But ultmately, I wanted the full 45mp details of that actual tight shot of the proud eagle, lunch in talons. That's worth $400 divided by all the cool pics I hope to get with it.

The unexpected problem with it, or at least the sample of one I purchased, is that the sound quality of music files is noticeably better with the 860 EVO. When I first noticed the difference, maybe after 125 hours of SSD use, I wondered if it was a matter of burn in (maybe SSD's are like everything else from a sound standpoint). I'm giving it three stars instead of four in case my review catches the attention of someone planning to use the 870 for the same purpose.

title: Another winner from Neewer
text:
Neewer has become my go-to source for lighting. I just spent a year teaching online using some of their lights for my teaching "studio", and they have never failed me.

This light set with built-in rechargeable batteries is another winner:
* First and foremost: those rechargeable batteries! I love not having to worry about purchasing separate batteries and a charger. The lights arrived fully charged and ready to go. When not in use, the batteries do a good job of holding their charge. After a month of storage, there is no noticeable loss of power.

* I can charge the batteries and use the lights at the same time. When I'm near a power supply, I'll plug in the included adapater (actually, 2 adapters are included in the 2-light set). That lets me use the light while the battery charges.

* Separate brightness and color temperature dials. I've gotten used to lights that have a single dial for adjusting the brightness and the temperature (turn the dial to adjust brightness, press the dial, turn it again to adjust temperature). But I really appreciate Neewer making these two separate dials. It's just a bit simpler for me to control the light output to suit my needs.

* Extra included hardware. It's nice that the package includes not only the lights and chargers, but tripods and adjustable cold-shoe mounts as well. And it all fits nicely in the included case.

One small complaint, but I knew this before I ordered the lights: There's no obvious way to attach some kind of barn doors to the lights. The Neewer lights I'd been using for the last year included barn doors which gave me more control over the direction of the lights. Not only were no doors included in this package, but I don't see a good way to connect some after the fact. If anyone has successfully done this, I'd love to know!

All in all, I'm really so happy with this portable light solution. How nice to have batteries built in. I hope that becomes a trend!

title: Don't buy - 5 solid reasons below
text:
The specs for the cost on this computer are okay, but there are just a few nagging problems I had with it that led to me returning it.

1. When you turn the computer on, it plays, at full volume, a cringe-inducing "gamer start up" noise - it will also play this when the computer restarts to update at 3am. Presumably it can be turned off in the bios, but who's idea was this? Who does it appeal to?

2. I can't speak for all units, but my computer constantly struggled with switching to the speakers sound input if the computer was using another audio device as output. Using a monitor, USB headset, or otherwise? I had to restart the computer every time or get errors whenever I tried playing media.

3. Computer has a "turbo" mode, which seems to apply some OCs or something along those lines. It also puts the fans up to 100 percent, which is deafening. In my experience, the turbo button just stopped working like 2 weeks in to using the laptop, which is a shame, because sometimes I would use it during gaming to level out the fan curve, which is audibly jittery as it tries to figure out if it should sit at 80, or 50, or 80, or 50, etc etc etc. The constant throttling is almost more annoying than keeping the fan at 100.

4. This is a problem I had years ago theast time I had a gaming laptop, and this seems no different: a lot of games, AAA, indie, you name it, will not run off of the dedicated GPU by default, and will instead (poorly) run on the integrated Intel GPU. To fix this you need to change the program's defaults from within the NVidia Control Panel.

5. This thing runs HOT. Running a game like Phasmophobia, which isnt exactly "next gen" makes the keyboard so hot that it hurts to use the B key to talk on global comms after a while, because there's clearly a major heat sink underneath it, possibly for the GPU or CPU.

If youre looking at this for a gaming computer, consider running a desktop. If you must go with a laptop, I'd look elsewhere, as questionable design decisions and downright bad ones make the experience here frustrating at best and broken at worst.

title: Best Buy for the Calculator Guy
text:
Ok so some of you probably know a weirdo like me who collects calculators. I know I'm not normal, I long y calculators. I don't even really use them for work but I never got over how useful they were.

Anyway growing up I used my Dad's HP 11C which my brother ultimately lost. So about a decade ago I went and bought my own used HP 15 C and one for Dad as it was superior to the 11C. I loved it. But the calculator was showing it's age.

I used my Dad's 11 C in calculus in highschool and ultimately upgraded to a Ti 89, and an HP 48 G series.

One thing I loved about the HPs was RPN. Anyway I deployed to Iraq and while overseas I missed the opportunity to buy the HP 15 C limited edition. These days you can buy them but because of how few are out there you need to purchase a second hand item at prices upward of $1000.

When I discovered the Swiss Micro DM 15L I couldn't pass it up. It arrived in a timely manner, especially considering it shipped from Europe. But more importantly this machine rocks.

I don't have a 15C limited to test it against, but it certainly is faster than my older model. This calculator uses the exact same voyager layout as the 15C, the feet are sturdier, has a USB port, uses RPN, and is without a doubt my new favorite calculator.

If you know someone who collects calculators this is definitely one to give them. I absolutely love everything about it. The keys, the machine work that went into the casing. This calculator is great.

title: Great economy headphones
text:
I've had these headphones a few weeks now and have used them several times. Connectivity to my three-year-old Samsung Galaxy S10e cell phone was easy, although still haven't been able to connect them to my 2018 Amazon Fire7 or 2014 Dell desktop computer. :(

Sound and range: While not noise cancelling, volume moderation makes listening reasonably focused with minimal external noise detection. Sound quality is very good for the price and range is impressive. I have clear, uninterrupted connectivity/sound throughout my home, inside and out. I walked half a block outside before sound started cutting out.

Battery: Battery life is exceptional. I used the device for several hours then turned it off to store them. Several days later they still had 100% charge and functioned for another few hours. I just rebooted the headphones after a week in a drawer and the battery reading is still 100%!

Comfort: The headphones are adjustable. That said, one reviewer mentioned getting a headache after a short time. I've worn these headphones for hours at a time and only felt a dull ache after those hours. A simple adjustment of the over-head band solved this. The band is padded underneath (next to the head) and comfortable. Also, the padded over-ear phones are comfortable for hours of use. Even while wearing studded earrings.

Recommended for quality and value at this price point. Thank you.

If Apple had some other way of charging the Pencil this would be minor to me but Apple is going to Apple and not provide alternatives.

I have contacted Spigen support about this and hopefully this gets fixed in newer batches of this product. Until then Pencil owners should look elsewhere. I ultimately returned this case due to the Pencil issue.
