title: Very durable saves me from buying new cables
text:
The main selling point of these cables is that you can interchange the USB connector types which are magnetically attached to the cable itself . So you don't have to purchase different types of USB cables just to get different type USB connectors. For example if you have a family that uses both Android and iPhone devices they can use the same cables by just changing the connector tips.

But another big selling point for me is the durability of these cables. I use my phone a LOT and sometimes I have to use it while it's recharging. I would prop bottom against my chest and eventually the USB connector would get bent and no longer connect securely or the cable would fray when bent forcing me to purchase new cables.

With these cables you don't have that bending and fraying problem because of the rotator joint thus solving a major headache for me and saving me money on new cables. Also because the USB connector tip itself is magnetically connected to the cable you don't have to worry about the connector becoming bent or broken it will simply detach if too much pressure is applied.

The LED light at the end of the cable is also very useful because it helps you find it in the dark and it indicates if it has become disconnected from the AC outlet. It also helps you orient the rotator joint in the position you want.

My only complaint is magnet strength which is not strong enough to pull the connector tip from my phone.? The previous generation of magnetic cables (that did not have the rotator joint) had magnets strong enough to pull the connector tip from the phone socket by pulling the cable. You can't do that with these cables because magnet not strong enough. So to remove the connector tip I always have to use the tool included or something like an ink pen. This is a hassle and you could potentially drop and lose the tiny connector tip. That's why I prefer to use an ink pen because it will magneticly stick to the metal tip of the ink pen. The tool they give you is plastic.

The other alternative to fishing out the connector tip is to just leave it in phone. My phone has a case with a flap that folds over it's so I don't have to worry about something touching it and possibly causing a short circuit. So if you move around the office or the house and you have multiples of this cable you can just connect using the same tip already on your phone. But be careful using cables like this from different manufacturers because the tip ends do look different and I don't know if they are compatible? That's why I bought this four pack of cables.

title: Day 15, Still Extremely Happy! Great choice
text:
I originally purchased from Best Buy an iBuyPower gaming computer for about $1,200, and I'm not sure if that thing was just defective or what, but day one, I had problem after problem so I had to return it. (I will say their customer service through iBuyPower was excellent, but it doesn't matter if the computer still doesn't work!).

After doing a lot of researching and even making a spreadsheet comparing 6 other computers, I decided this one would fit my needs the best, even if it was about $300 more than I wanted to spend.

PROS:
- All hardware is recognized without any issues
- Upgraded to Windows 11 and it's very easy to learn, it's pretty much just a cleaned-up version of 10.
- All Windows updates and driver updates went smoothly, no problems with any of that.
- Very quiet even when there's a game running
- Haven't had any problems with lag in any games outside of my crappy internet provider
- Appearance: very nice!!! Not super gimicky like most gaming computers with a million different lights spinning and flashing. This one has the 2x2" diamond on the front and the ring in the front, the inside is fully lit but not obnoxious.

CONS: (1)
- Only one issue I've noticed that isn't a 100% consistent problem but has happened many times so far. When the computer goes to sleep (not when the screen goes black but actually goes to sleep), it takes a REALLY long time to wake up. Like, as long as I do on a Monday morning. Sometimes it wakes up right away, other times it may take longer than a min and a half and hitting the enter key like 20 times. I'm wondering what to do. Currently I just turned the sleep settings to 2 hours, and when I need to wake it up. Sometimes I have to turn off the power completely and turn it back on. Very annoying!! There is no power switch on the computer and if I hold the power button when its stuck in sleep mode, it doesn't power down no matter how long I hold it in. I have to turn off the power from my surge protector.

I currently use it to run Assassin's Creed Origins on the maxed out settings and there's no issues and it still runs quietly. That's the newest game I've tried so far, but it runs my old stuff on Steam perfectly too like Sims 4. Seriously, no problems whatsoever other than that sleep mode wake up issue.
If I remember later when I figure out how to fix the sleep problem, I will post an update. Overall, I'm very happy with this computer and would recommend.

title: I've bought Fintie covers before, for a good reason.
text:
I recently replaced by Kindle, upgrading to the new Paperwhite. I had a similar looking Fintie case for my old one, and loved it. I had no reason not to think this one would be great, as well. I wasn't disappointed. The quality of the construction, and the beauty of it's design, are top notch. When I look at it, closed, and when I open it use, it "sparks joy" for me, as Marie Kondo would say. The magnets old it securely and evenly, closed or open and folded behind. When closed, it puts the Kindle into sleep mode, automatically, saving power. It fits in my hand comfortably and, given the new screen size and thinner borders, I don't know how I would be able to hold the Kindle Paperwhite without it.

So why not five stars? I'm not 100% thrilled with the style of the bits that actually hold my kindle in place. I would have preferred a plastic clip that didn't completely cover the front plastic edge, as this style does. But it functions perfectly, and I've had no problems with it so, that's a matter of personal taste. I also have reservations about the hand strap in the back, however. It's nice, but I worry that, over time, the elastic will stretch and will become loose. Also, the strap doesn't really work for me under most reading conditions. Normally, I hold my Kindle with the bottom corner resting in my palm, gripping the device at an angle. When I hold it this way, the strap can barely secure my first two fingers, and even then it's more or less useless. It's only when I grip the device directly in the middle of the "spine," that the strap becomes useful for me. Again, its a matter of personal preference.

Would I buy another Fintie cover in the future? 100% yes! They make, by far, the best covers for electronic devices I have ever used.

title: Wanted to love this camera, but should have went Go Pro...
text:
I purchased this camera right when it came out. Admittedly I was torn between the One X and the One R. I specifically wanted a 360 camera that supported live streaming. To my surprise, the One X supported live streaming but not the One R. Sadly I found that out AFTER my return period. Good news is Insta 360 finally updated the firmware to allow live streaming, but that happened after the event for which I purchased the camera. Why am I upset about this? The camera was marketed as being able to support live streaming, but the initial firmware release didn't support it. Connecting the camera and setting up a live stream through lets say zoom wasn't possible and the support around live streaming was non-existent.

I'd love to say this camera was one of the best purchases I could have made, however at this point for the cost it's basically a glorified paperweight.

** Pros **

The picture quality is fairly good, and the editing process is super easy, so its easy for beginners.
Modularity of the camera (swap lens), allows you make the camera what you need for various circumstances

** Cons **

Pretty much everything else. The software application is slow and clunky to work with. Editing is fairly easy once in a video, but its extremely annoying navigating the app at all times because the connection between phone and camera is slow (connected using iPhone 11 Pro, Samsung 8+, Samsung 9+, Samsung Note 10+). The camera cost just over $500 at the time I purchased it, so needless to say, I expected a much better experience. Because of the lack of functionality for live streaming I ended up not using the camera at all. Purchased a protective case and tucked the camera away. Now months later, I take the camera out of the protective case and proceeded to try and use it. That buggy app I told you about...yeah its back in full affect. Honestly, I figured the app had to improved after months of waiting for the software to catch up to the what I thought was good hardware, but nope. Same ol crappy app. After multiple app updates and updating to the latest firmware, I finally connected my phone (currently iPhone 11 Pro), and realized immediately I can no longer preview photos or cameras from my cell phone while connected to the camera. That's basically the entire point of of some of these devices. Interesting enough I can still initiate a photo/video from my phone. Adding more insult to injury I noticed the camera don't always take the photo (even though it plays the shutter sound so I know the connection between phone and camera is fine). If you think that's bad, it gets even worse...after realizing the camera wasn't taking my photos consistently, I turned the camera around to inspect the camera and imagine my surprise when I read the following error message "The Lend Mode is disconnected. Please check the connection between the core and Lens Mod, and restart to try again". After multiple restarts, clearing cache, resets, and all of the above, I'm sure this camera is pretty much done for after maybe 10 uses and that's being generous. Pretty much a glorified paperweight. On top of that, the support has been pretty terrible. I wish I would have kept the messages about the lack of support regarding live streaming.

Waste of $500. Should have went Go Pro.

In short, if your reading this...hopefully I can save you the shame of dropping basically a small fortune on a camera that likely won't hold up (barely used mine). I essentially took a baby stack of money and lit a fire to it. Implore you to look elsewhere for better quality and better support for the money! I would love to comment on other things like stability control or anything else, but sadly my camera is done, never hit the ground, never wet, nothing...pretty much lived and died in its case. As you can probably gather SUPER upset.

title: Awful reliability, pretty bad customer service.
text:
These are phenomenal earbuds. I have tested so so many. Basically I bought about 5 pairs, kept 2, bought 4 more, kept 1, and bought 2 more, keeping neither - endlessly searching for the best set. All of them had issues of some sort, but that's not to claim they are at fault for them. My ears are, to put it the best way I know how, cavernous. There is that disclaimer that I need the LARGEST earbud tip possible as well as the largest earlobe wedge wing thingy to hold em in. Some of the others did not provide large enough tips to form a seal, so this excludes me from testing about 40% of earbuds. These barely did the trick. I would like a slightly larger one, but with some adjusting, I can get a good seal. I am a gym-goer and it's my favorite part of every day. I treat the entire process as an experience and I want to enjoy it to the fullest extent before I go back to what is disappointingly the rest of my life. I'll spend what I need to in order to do this, and let me tell you that I dropped over 250 dollars on some Sennheisers momentum TWS2, the latest and greatest from Sony (1000XM3), Lypertek Tevi's and a few other China sets. I really enjoyed the MPOW BH437A with the huge charging case because I literally forgot they EVER need charging. 3 months after owning them, they stopped working and I was like "oh yeah... I have to charge them sometimes" The sound quality is great on those and they are an incredible value for what you get. The Lyperteks were utterly amazing in the clarity department. Some of the highest quality sound I've ever heard from TWS's, but they miss the mark on oomf. I use my earbuds at the gym and nowhere else. As such, my music tastes are industrial, heavy, loud, bassy. Is "gutted" too mean? If you sit in your home and listen to earbuds hoping for a flat EQ with every detail painted like a picture, buy them. They are incredible. And they are CHEAP. However, given what I needed them to do, they just couldn't. The Soundcore Liberty 2 Pro's are great. I admit I do prefer a V-EQ meaning I like it when you tick the "Loudness" checkbox in your car stereo, then continue to crank the treble and bass. I do not know what manner of PFM aka pixie dust China sprinkled on these earbuds but they are absolutely exactly what I want to hear. I absolutely could not tell a difference between them and the Sennys after I maxed out the "V" in my phone's internal EQ to just a tick under where it started clipping to make the Sennys what I wanted them to be. They didn't go as loud being so heavily doctored but I was not disappointed because the ballpark these are all are playing in is as good as TWS sound gets. They were 250 dollars though which isn't chicken scratch, and their battery life was pretty bad honestly. I get it though, Sennheiser isn't really in the battery business. They are in the speak business, and they did a great job. They didn't fit me quite as well though, and kept falling out. The SCL2Ps easily surpassed the cheaper Sennheiser TWS sets though. The Sonys stood up hard on the bass side, but the clarity just wasn't there and they also were finnicky for no reason, one earbud cutting out when I put the phone in my pocket. Frankly just not worth the trouble. The choice was clear at 100 bucks for the soundcores. FF to 8 months down the road, after I had forgotten all about earbuds having spent all my gym days spoiled by the soundcores. The left bud stopped connecting and eventually died all together. I was disappointed and called Anker. Within 5 minutes of placing the call, I had another set in the mail with no obligation to return the others or prove I wasn't just trying to score a second set of 100 dollar earbuds for free. They even restarted my warranty to go with the new set. In this day and age of dying customer service, this was really refreshing and I cannot recommend you buy these any harder. There is almost no compromise with these. They fit a huge variety of ears, sound 9.5 out of 10 good, have good software with a surprisingly powerful EQ that is NATIVE-FIRMWARE (meaning the actual earbuds themselves adjust the sound instead of making your phone do it), insane range, good battery life, gobs of concise bass yet accurate, non-aggressive treble. The Lyperteks were the clearest earbuds I've ever heard. Seriously incredible on par with 500-dollar over the ears. But gym gains are all about dat bass. Finally, the Ankers underwent and largely tolerated 7 months of crazy abuse cooking in 150* Arizona-registered cars, being banged around in gym bags, getting sweat all over them and dropped on the floor, stepped on, rained on, etc. Sensitive electronics just shouldn't be expected to tolerate this, and Anker seems to know this. I wouldn't recommend using their website for warranty claims. It wouldn't recognize my amazon order number anyway, but the phone call was relatively quick and painless. If I could find one fault w/ these, it's that the MIC is not great. It's perfectly passable, but lets in any and all outside noise. You can use them in a quiet room, but it will really get fatiguing to the listeners if you're in the car trying to talk to them on the phone. Seriously, get these. They are better than headphones listed 2x as much.

UPDATE:
UNTIL.... a few months down the road, and I'm 3 replacements deep into this. Why? The left earbud keeps dying. Also when you have multiple product failures and have to deal with their mediocre customer service many times, they punish YOU. You have to send your dead ones back before they will send you different ones. I'd say new ones, but they aren't new. They're used returns sent back by other customers. The first used ones I received had ear wax on them and were missing all the tips. They require the box and packing material to process subsequent replacements. The subsequent replacements take longer and longer to receive. They make damn certain you do not want to deal with them so that you'll just let it go and deal with a better company.

Really shame on you Anker. You need to treat people better or make products that are good enough to where you don't have to treat people well.

title: Solid Bluetooth Speaker - 4.5 Stars (Rounded Up 0.5 because I love Aiwa)
text:
Before buying the Aiwa Exos-3, my collection of portable standalone bluetooth speakers included a Diamondboxx XL2, an Aiwa Exos-9, a JBL Charge 3, and a UE Wonderboom 2. Each serves a purpose and has its pros and cons. I received notification from Aiwa about a promotion on the Exos-3. I love my Aiwa Exos-9, so it felt like a no brainer to buy Exos-3 with a promotion, which I was hoping to fill the gap (in terms of portability and loudness [particularly in terms of bass]) somewhere between the Exos-9 and JBL Charge 3. (My JBL Charge 3 is still going strong after a number of years and, in my opinion, is still an excellent speaker).

Sound: I predominantly tested the unit with hip hop and dancehall reggae streaming from Spotify (High Quality Stream selected). The Exos-3 has excellent sound quality, and it can get very loud with minimal distortion. No, not Exos-9 or Diamondboxx XL2 loud, but more than loud enough to be the life of a moderately sized party indoors and, at full volume, might cause a neighboring apartment to complain (I haven't tested it outdoors yet). I did a sound comparison between it and the JBL Charge 3, and the Exos-3 gets louder, has more bass, and seems to have less distortion when you approach volumes of 80%-100%. That said, the bass is very good at high levels, but not ground-shaking (which I suppose can't be really expected for a unit this size) - at higher volumes, the Exos-3 gave more than enough to make me say "OK, that's some decent bass," but from the company that made the Exos-9 (which, IMO, really kicks for it's size), I was hoping for something more substantial in terms of bass. The lack of ridiculous bass is not a deal breaker for me - the Aiwa Exos-3 is still a fantastic portable bluetooth speaker in terms of sound and indeed seems to fill the gap between a JBL Charge 3 and Aiwa Exos-9, but closer the Charge 3 than Exos-9.

Other features: The Exos-3 is a bit bigger than the JBL Charge 3, but holding the Exos-3, you'll instantly notice how well built it is. It's built like a tank and has some weight to it - certainly not enough weight to make me feel like it's too heavy, but heavy enough to give me impression that this is not a flimsy piece of equipment. As a NYC resident who is always on the go, the strap is a great feature. Also awesome that it has Bluetooth 5.0 and can act as a charger for my phone. I'm definitely keeping this unit, but Aiwa's 90 day risk free trial and 3 year warranty is fantastic and gives me a some assurance that if this thing malfunctions, it will be supported.

title: Worked great. For less then three uses.
text:
My wife bought some string lights she thought were AC powered. Turns out they were 9volt battery powered. I look on amazon, and boom, a 9volt power plug to replace battery powered devices. "Buy now" and they were on the way. When they arrived, I opened the boxes and was pleasantly surprised. They even had the 9volt adapter on the end! I was getting excited now.

To say I was happy as I unboxed these would be an understatement. No more wasting batteries. She bought two strands of string lights, so I bought two of these adapters. It was kismet.

The first adapter worked twice. The night I installed them, and once after that. Then the string wouldn't light at all. Troubleshooting the strand or the power pack, I tested with batteries... which still powered them. Okay... well one out of two isn't bad. I guess we're still saving batteries.

The next night we plugged in the remaining set, and it powered the string barely to illumination. Again, on battery the light string worked fine.

Neither of these AC adapters worked more than three times. I'm certainly no certified electrician, but I've done enough work around my house installing switches/running new circuits/etc that I feel I gave these a fair troubleshooting run down (even finally verifying with my voltmeter there was nothing across the prongs). The lights were plugged in and used for maybe 2 hours during the evening and unplugged again. I am returning these.

Great idea, terrible execution.

title: Very nice, good value.
text:
I got this to record track days and autocross for my ND2 Miata RF.

First impressions of the mount are good. The magnets seem very strong and the pads are soft but thin. The thin pads are probably needed to allow the magnets to get close enough to the metal for a good hold. The pads are rubber and grippy. The metal “bridge” between the magnets is perfect for prying the mount off.

The ball head mount for the GoPro is a bit cheap. Though it doesn’t need to be a massively strong piece as it only has to hold a few ounces of camera. I suspect it would hold a small point and shoot camera that can do video but mounting a DSLR or even a Mirrorless is out of the question as the ball head mount is just too small for that kind of application. Plus the tightening screws are not in very good locations and you can’t get the main one very tight. The secondary screw you need to use the smaller of the two supplied alan keys. That one you can can, obviously, get nice and secure.

The two supplied GoPro mounts are perfect fits but not sure why you would want to use the plastic one when the metal one is so much stronger.

The tether is a nice touch and if you can secure one end to something solid, I’m sure it would hold the mount and GoPro if the magnets should lose their grip. I do not want to actually test this.

The mount works great. Solid and secure and with the tether it should meet nearly all regulatory requirements for track days and autocross.

text: Very similar to the other wansview cams. There is no web gui configurator. Only very limited configuration settings can be adjusted in the android app. These wansview cams seem to be setup for people interested in a subscription cloud service, and are not really optimized for people who want to run their own rtsp cam server software. It will connect and work with rtsp but these wansview cams are pretty flaky on rtsp and lack basic configuration settings. The power supply setup is not optimal at all for an outdoor cam. The power solution chosen is a wall wart usb cell phone charger at 5vdc and 1 amp with a long direct attached non-removable usb cable extending from the camera. That makes this model incompatible with the majority of camera power supplies that run 12vdc with barrel connectors. The usb connectors are not ideal for an outdoor setting. It's almost like this cam is too good for indoor use because of the PTZ, but not really up to the task of constant outdoor use. title: Modern, robust phone runs Android 11
text:
Had to switch phones due to my ZTE Majesty "standard 4G" soon to be discontinued. This phone is a giant leap forward, like going from Windows XP to Windows 11. It runs Android 11, so the OS is current, robust, and secure, albeit more automatic updating. Here's the pros and cons to expect:

+ FAST! Boots up and installs apps 5x to 10x quicker than my old phone.
+ Battery sipper. Even with all the initial setting up, I'm still using the original battery charge 7 days later!
+ Loud volume for notifications and phone ringing. I like not missing my calls and texts.
+ This version of Android includes shutting off ALL notifications of any app. So, for example, Google Maps hounds you to leave reviews everywhere you visit, you can just switch it off!
+ The 3 main control buttons DO remain showing at the bottom of the screen, so you can easily navigate back or show all open apps if needed.
+ Headphone jack!

- BLOAT! Once you get your Gmail/Google account signed up, click the gear icon and scroll down the screen to apps. Go through the entire list and uninstall anything you don't need. It has several games, 3 casino apps, and even an adult app! I know many people have their addictions, but it SHOULD NOT COME PREINSTALLED ON THE PHONE! And, heed this warning if planning on giving this to your kid!
- Android system updates. Be forewarned: These DOWNLOAD automatically, and no way to set it to "only when WiFi is available." These will devour your data!!! You can let it INSTALL during the night, but it has already downloaded and gobbled your data!
- Bigger phone means a bigger brick in the pocket. It's both wider and longer than my previous phone.
- The preinstalled keyboard on my last phone (which I liked better than Google's) isn't here. Just Google's Gboard.
- I bought this phone with 1 year service included with 1500 mins talk, 1500 texts, and 1500MB data (good), but all of my existing texts remaining vanished! Tracfone's customer service just kept arguing and I finally gave up. Tracfone's customer service is notoriously bad and this is a perfect example. Thankfully I don't text a bunch, but it doesn't make this excusable.

Overall, a great phone once you get everything set up correctly.

title: Hands down, THE BEST Laptop Cooler design on the market (18 month review)
text:
I have had numerous laptop cooling pads for my laptops, most of which were for a Desktop setup (not in your lap). I have done massive amounts of research (stupid amounts) on what is available and even older models that aren't made anymore. This is THE BEST option for laptop cooling out there, conceptually, and in execution, so long as you have air INLETS in the bottom of your laptop (most gaming laptops do).
For others looking for functional requirements:
- Air INLET is in the rear; so air goes through the filter before entering your laptop
- Air passes through the inlet chamber post-filters which is shared between the fans/inlets (good to prevent one fan weakening/air flow differentials)
- It then hits the turbine style fans and passes through the small outlet into the bottom of the laptop, speeding it up
- Air EXHAUST is through your laptop's exhaust fan vents
- KEY FEATURE not mentioned: in the box there are two semi-stiff plastic flaps with glue on one side. These flaps go on the cooler facing backwards to separate hot exhaust air from the inlets direction below and behind your laptop's rear fan exhaust vents
- The rubber seal is well constructed and works perfectly to seal the bottom of the laptop so only air coming through the cooler fans and filters is ingested
- Noise & Vibration: minimal noise and vibration from the fans. Speed 1 = almost inaudible; Speed 2 = audible but quieter than your laptop's fan at full power; Speed 3 = As loud as your laptop's fan at full power (my fans are loud though)

Three Neutral/Negative points:
- Because of the design, running your laptop with the cooler OFF is not a good idea for anything more than idling. Your laptop's fans will have to work harder than designed to pull in air and that isn't good for long term reliability
- The rear stand legs are not wide at all. This is good in some applications, but means you have 2, 1" square points supporting the laptop
- The side width of the cooler is more than necessary. It's only an inch or so on each side beyond my 15" laptop, but it takes up more space than it has to

I have been using this for almost 18 months now and it is still going strong.

I just did a full cleaning (standard filter washed monthly) and was shocked how much dust I was able to blow out of the fans with compressed air. The fan noise is now AT LEAST half of what it was before cleaning, so I recommend cleaning the fans out with highly compressed air every 3-6 months.

I couldn't recommend this more IF you have the proper fan/vent/inlet setup. Most performance laptops do. It's amazing it took this long for someone to come up with this design as it is vastly superior to all other options on the market if your goal is max external cooling for long-term reliability

title: Needs Work, Not Enough Ports, Damages External HD Drives
text:
This product was well reviewed on blogs and Youtube and was a bit cheaper than CalDigit's TS3 Hub so I purchased it.

I've had this device for a week and these are my initial impressions:

1) Just a bit shy on USB-C ports and USB-A ports. I do a lot of backups and drive duplication on a weekly basis, so would appreciate a hub that has 2 USB-A ports or 2 USB-B ports to allow for A/B backups. As it is I'm having to use additional dongles and hubs to facilitate volume duplication.

2) The SoHo hub has difficulty mounting external hard disk drives. I recently had a 4TB WD drive become damaged after connecting it to the SoHo and it failed to mount on my MacBook Pro. Luckily I have a backup of that damaged drive but the incident doesn't inspire confidence.

3) The main I/O USB-C port is located on the right side of hub. If you have a setup where the laptop is on the left side of the desk and your monitor is on the right side it creates an awkward situation where the cable doubles back on itself. Might work better if it was located in the back to make it more agnostic.

I was hoping for this product to replace my Satechi Type-C slim hub in my backpack but I don't trust the CalDigit Soho anymore for that.

My hope is that the V2 of this product offers 2 USB-A ports, 2 USB-C ports, better placement of the main I/O port and more reliable mounting of external HD drives. Thunderbolt 3 compatibility would be appreciated as well.

Until then I think a $60 slim hub USB-C adapter works much better for most people.

Update (August 2021)
I use this device weekly for photo and video shoots to offload media cards to duo SSDs (Primary and backup). It powers SSD drives very easily, I don't connect HDD drives to it anymore however, will connect it to the laptop itself.

I originally paid $100 when it was first released, I thought it was overpriced then after using the device for a while but the lowered price of $70 makes it a good value in terms of USB-C hubs.

I would love to see a Thunderbolt 3 hub in this form factor.

title: It performs at its price. Not so great as a headset.
text:
The rating should be 4 stars in terms of value: one gets what one pays, which is relatively low price. However, 3-star rating is selected to warn others who might have high expectation of it as a noise cancelling (NC) headset, as opposed to headphones.

A headset consists of two functions: headphones for hearing, and microphones for recording the sound. The headphones function is only for hearing.

Headphones technology is simple. Anyone can make it, and high-performance headphones (wired or wireless) can be had for as low as $25-ish. This one works quite well as headphones.

For a noise cancelling (NC) headset however, the technology is challenging, because it must make a distinction between the voice that comes from the user's mouth and the ambiance sound. It should cancel the ambiance while recording the voice with as high fidelity as possible.

This technology is complex and costly, which is why there are such a wide range of products and prices. I have tried a few under $70, and none of them work well as a headset, although all are quite good as headphones. I have a Sony WH-XB900N (~$150-$250) which delivers excellent sounds in both headset and headphones modes, which is why it costs much more.

This Anker model Q20 is highly rated, and I purchased it as a gift for a relative, who uses a 15-yr old headset (no noise canceling) to talk with family/friends, and also to do karaoke while doing household chores. I thought the noise cancelling feature would make this headset an improvement.

Unfortunately, after a few days of trying it, the relative lost interest because of its poor performance as a headset. As headphones, the noise cancelling is just OK; but for the headset function, the noise canceling is so bad that one cannot listen to the background music with any quality while hearing one's own voice mixed in to perform karaoke. I thought that turning NC off would have made better, but it didn't. It was just a tad better. And the relative even told me to return it even as it was a gift. So, I can't recommend it as a headset.

Nevertheless, if one has no need for high-fidelity communications like Zoom or similar, this one is worth the price.

title: Good and Bad
text:
As anyone who works with M2's knows, they can generate a boatload of heat. When you use them with a portable enclosure you dont have the computer's internal fans, which makes it even more important that they are able to get rid of the heat. On the good side, this is one of the best I have worked with for doing that. The enclosure is single-piece aluminum, and is very robust--no plastic other than the end caps. I did a 30 minute file transfer, and at the end it was rather warm, but still able to be touched easily.

Now the not so good stuff, and why I had gave it three stars instead of five. Thank goodness for Amazon's return policy, because I had to go through four of these units to get two that consistently worked throughout the transfer process. One arrived DOA...it just would not boot up, and another kept going offline. That suggests to me that maybe their quality control for the USB boards could stand an improvement.

Amended--The fourth unit referred to above went bad, but the good news is that a fifth one seems to be working ok. What I have learned not to do is to have them plugged in at start-up. Instead, plug them in after everything is G2G.

My suggestion is that if you can deal with the frustrations and delays, then this is worth the effort, because the fact of the matter is that these enclosures have the most robust heat dissipation capabilities of their type on the market.

title: $1300 set up but SeaLife doesn't include lens cap
text:
I've had a SeaLife DC series for years. It's been a great device, but I thought it was time to upgrade. So, I bought this package. I haven't gotten it in the water yet, but I've got a few issues with SeaLife on this model already:

1. They don't include a lens cap. It's a big miss. This is entry-level product management. If you scratch your lens, you basically ruin a $1300 setup because the OEM didn't want to include a $3 lens cap. Oh, I asked, and they will sell you one separately. [Update: I contacted the seller (not SeaLife, but a store) and they sent me a lens cap that fits, which is pictured nearby. I had to rig up a way to attach it to the camera
with 550 cord].

2. There's no native way to dummy cord your camera or the light carriage to your gear. No hooks, loops, nothing. Again, entry-level product management miss. I've fashioned one of my own out of 550 cord and a combination of bowline and (half) figure 8 knot (pictured).

3. The arms for the lights don't move. You have to buy an additional (and separate) flexi arm for ~$60. I bought one and offset the camera to one side. Why is this important? Because you need the lights behind or to the side to avoid backscatter. This is a packaging miss on SeaLife's part.

4. There's no digital Zoom on this model. Maybe that's a function of the "mini" but the camera isn't all that much smaller than my 10-year old DCS model.

5. The camera itself is waterproof. This has benefits and drawbacks. One big one is you can't add a removable memory card, or swap a card out on a trip.

6. The directions for the lighting have gold connections. The directions say you must wipe these with alcohol EVERY SINGLE TIME you charge the batteries. a) it's hard to reach without something like a q-tip and b) this is a huge pain on a trip. I don't mind maintaining my gear, but this is *high* maintenance.

Generally, I don't think SeaLife has met up to the standards of their own reputation. I'm absolutely fuming about the lens cap thing.

Update: I have tested the camera in the water over 8 dives recently and am pleased with the photos.

- It's simple to use in the water - good for a non-pro-photographer.
- I like the extra settings on the white balance which gives you some flexibility to experiment with.
- I set my white balance to the "quick button" which is a nice feature underwater.
- On their website, SeaLife has a pro photographer (Brent Durand) do a ~20 minute summary on how to use the camera which I thought was very helpfu. You can also find that video on his YouTube channel. Basically, you watch that video and you know everything you need to use the camera.

There's a photo above with a remora attached to a parrot fish that I took with this camera (the other two were taken with a phone).

title: WATCH OUT! this is an AC97 front panel, NOT HD!
text:
There are 2 kinds of front panel cables/connectors. One is the old AC97 standard, the other is the newer (Intel) HD standard. If you buy a nice new Sound Blaster Audigy FX card, and plug this cable into it, it will go into front panel mode, and never come out, until you unplug this cable from the SB card.
The newer Intel (HD) cable / connectors have wires that come back to the Sound Blaster to tell it when you plug in a microphone or headphones. If you have an older computer, this will work, but NOT with a newer sound card.

title: Phenomenal - bass/fitment issue resolved.
text:
I was not familiar with the sound of Beyerdynamic until recently after acquiring their Lagoon Premium ANC headphones, and most recently the Amiron Wireless Copper. About my background - I am a musical aficionado, aka "an audiophile". I am a professional musician, concert and recording artist and sound and music is my life. My latest interest was in a truly great wireless set of cans for listening at home in the late evenings when I can't use my big audio system. I've went through BW PX (which I own), PX7, Shure Aeonic 50, Lagoons, Sony MX3, Dali IO6, probably a few others. Before I get to the Amirons, Ilet me just say that my priority for my type of listening with wireless headphones is SOUND QUALITY, ANC comes second and is not that important for me. Also, I am fully aware that a Bluetooth headphone can't and shouldn't be compared with a wired one. With that out of the way, as far as Bluetooth cans go, the Amirons are the closest example that comes to "musical perfection". They posses incredible detail from the lowest to the highest ends of the sound spectrum, in a perfectly blended and balanced way for a "liquid musical nirvana". I want to address an important issue with regards to the bass. Many people and reviewers have weak/insufficient bass due to poor fit. This is true, however, but easily correctable - the fit must be perfect around the ears with a proper seal in order to hear the bass of the Amirons - and they do have it in spares. If you press the cups towards you ears, you should immediately hear and feel all the bass. Now, if this happens, what you can do to increase the clamping force and make a good seal is gently bend the metal extensions just before the Y split - see my photo where I am pointing to the exact spot. These are meant to be adjusted. I have done that, and boy, did it resolve any bass issue. I have a perfect seal, and while the comfort is just as good, the bass is now all there and the sound balance is absolutely stunning!
A few words about the sound - lows are deep, and I mean deep. If you have a bass rich song, you will hear it and feel the impact. Please, don't mistake the well balanced sound signature for a "bass heavy" cans, these are not! The lows are extremely clear, clean, tight, weighty and defined. Bass is not bloated, nor does it bleed into the lower mids. It's there and it reveals what's in the music, if the music has it.
Low mids are full, textured, and perfectly blended in the mix. Higher mids are extremely nautral in timbre - male and female voiced sound "centered". Instruments in the mid register sound very realistic with plenty of micro texture. Strings, piano, harpsichord, human voices...
Higher register is extremely extended, clean, transparent and never shrieking or over detailed to the point of being distracted.
Overall, the whole tuning of Amiron creates a sense of an expansive soundstage (quite impressive for a closed back design!) with the sound surrounding you. You are in the center of the stage, and there is plenty of air and separation of instruments. Never a sense of congestion. Beyerdymanic has really achieved something special here and these may well be the most musical and "best" wireless headphones available. Of course, they are on the neutral-natural spektrum of tuning, as all HiFi grade 'phones should be. There are other headphones with much different tunings, that may appeal to different personal tastes. However, I can say the Amirons are absolutely a Hi-Fi "audiophile grade" cans in a wireless package. There is just a liquid musical magic oozing out the them with virtually any genre of music that I threw at them. Comfort is great, even with the increased clamping adjustment which was critical for hearing all the bass, and they remain extremely comfortable on my head after 2-3 hours of listening. Hope this helps!

title: Best on all aspects
text:
Update July 15rd, 2022:

The original pair I ordered from Amazon was defective. One side would constantly lose volume in under an hour of use until it was left to recharge for at least 5 hours (even though battery was 90%). And the mic on that pair did not work at all. I sent an email to FIIL and they sent me an extra pair free of charge which I appreciate but the volume issue still happened. Moreover, it's sometimes a hassle to sync the 2 buds with each other. In many instances I had to the unsynced bud back in the case, close it, wait 2 seconds, and then pop it out again, and if that didn't work I had to unpair and and re-pair it with the device, and sometimes it took multiple rounds of attempts for syncing to work (this happened with different devices). Ultimately, these were still worth the $44 I spent on them, because I just got the Sony WF-1000XM4 (suggested on nearly every review website as the best sounding TWS available today) and the FIIL T1XS SIGNIFICANTLY exceeds the Sonys' clarity of audio and bass quality.
Given this perspective, and for the price I got them, the FILL T1XS are a mighty 4.7/5, and I'll be returning the Sonys.
------------------------------------------------

OLD REVIEW BELOW:

I'll start by saying that I'm not an audiophile but neither do I not care about my music sounding well. I like a good seal, noise-isolation, and in-ear stability during activities. Because of that I usually limited myself to a $10-$20 range.

I've had about 4-5 pairs of earphones over the last ten years some of which I re-ordered several times because I liked them even though they broke several times. They all had over-the-ear hooks because I used them for treadmill running. They were all marketed as "noise-isolating" earphones, and some as "bass-boosted".

Now, my latest were KZ-ZST and after a loyal 1.5 years the cable connection broke on one side. So I decided to try out a TWS pair because for one I was getting tired of messing with cables and secondly I wanted to transcend the $10-$20 range on earphones. There is one exception in my earphones history and that was a $90 pair which I will talk about in a bit below.

I read multiple reviews on the T1X from various websites, including reddit, and a site I discovered along my research: Scarbir.com.
All were praising the T1X, but then I noticed the T1XS which was newer, only $5 more (on sale) than the T1X and has even better reviews. I was skeptical as I always am about anything but decided to give these a try.

They arrived, I put them on and played some of my favorite tunes.

Man, let me tell you, I felt like I wasted a decade of quality enjoyment from music.
With the T1XS I am literally rediscovering each tune in my music library with clarity I never heard before.
When connected to the phone, with the FIIL+ app you can set equalizer presets that make a big difference in the way things sound. My all-around favorite is the Home Theater preset because that's exactly how it makes the bass sound. Similarly when I'm on a computer, I make sure to have "Bass boost" enabled on Windows' sound settings and that makes everything sound better.

I thought I knew what good bass sounds like but the these proved me wrong. I thought I could hear details in my music but again... I was wrong. I thought I knew what good in-ear stability was and I was wrong. I bought a pair of $90 Klipsch IMAGE S4 as an experiment in 2011 and still remember how they sounded to this day. The bass was thumpy, dull, and the highs were overbearing. I could never get a good seal and they just wouldn't stay in my ears comfortably. This is not to say Klipsch are bad, but to show that price is not necessarily an indicator of quality. The T1XS are half the price but score more than double in sound quality and comfort.

Pros:
- Amazing sound, pronounced details, bass sounds like you're sitting in a car with top of the line subwoofers or in a movie theater.
- Good fit, stay snug in ear during exercise.
- Variety of earbud sizes.
- Optional wingtips in 2 sizes offer more stability.
- Good battery life fast charging speed.
- Small elegant case.

Cons:
- Sometimes one side won't work upon Bluetooth connection or when switching connection between devices (i.e. phone to computer), but that is easily resolved by restarting the earphones or by a long-press on the earphone that doesn't work.
- FIIL+ app doesn't close unless force-stopped on Android. It occasionally crashes too.
- No way to turn off touch controls. This becomes a problem when you have a beanie on that makes contact with the touch-surface and makes unintended pauses, switches to the next song, or even shuts down the earphones. This is my main gripe for outdoors winter running.
- Taking the earphones out of the case is inconvenient. They're prone to slipping.

In conclusion, these are a popular option, and one of the most positively reviewed earphones. If sound and fit is what matters most and you don't care for eye-catching style designs then for the price (I bought them for under $45 on sale) it's a no-brainer.

title: Convenient way to put those unused bare drives to use
text:
This dense little appliance is a great way to make spare SATA hard drives earn their keep. It's dirt-simple to use: Connect power and USB cables, install one or more drives, flip the power switch in the back, and press the power buttons for the drives you want to use.

Having a separate power button for each drive is seriously convenient. You can stop a drive, power it down, and remove it without disturbing the other drives. You can also leave a drive switched off until you actually need it. (The unit is pretty good about spinning down drives when they're not being used.)

The only wrinkle I found involves installing a drive: Don't force a drive all the way into a bay. (Forcing it in bends the little ejection lever at the rear of the bay.) Instead, slide the drive in as far as it easily goes. Then close the door, letting the internal mechanism seat the drive. Double-check that the door is actually latched.

title: Valuable alternative
text:
I have been a mofi user for decades, both for business and personal. Mofi's are extremely rugged (attics, trucks in winter and summer, train cars) and the access to advanced configs is pretty insane at that price point. For basic, simple use, in my opinion, that is also their downfall. The UI is not that intuitive and the lack of 5G (wifi) in 2021 is an issue. Sure, you can just use it as a gateway and add a more modern WiFi router behind it, but that is just another piece of hardware to purchase, manage, and secure after shelling out 300 bones for the router.

Enter the X750. While it doesn't feel as rugged, the WiFi antennas are internal, and the SIM slot isn't as convenient, I have zero complaints given it is half the price of a mofi. The UI is refreshing, not to mention it supports modern browsers, and so far I haven't discovered many features that are lacking compared to the mofi. I would recommend that you purchase the mofi enhanced LTE antennas ($20) to slap on this bad boy (or something comparable) given the stock antennas can't compete (the mofi enhanced antennas double my 4G LTE speed on the X750). Also, I did have to place a WiFi router behind this as it could not handle the 40+ WiFi devices in my house, but at half the price of a mofi, it feels more acceptable to use it as just a gateway.

I highly recommend the GL-X750.

title: High powered and economical modified sine wave UPS for your PC
text:
Uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) are very important for certain electronics in maintaining operations during unstable grid power. For brief outages, such as accidentally tripping the breaker because I forgot to turn off the AC before cooking something on my electric stove, the UPS will ensure the important work on my computer continues in the 5 minutes it takes to reset the breaker. For longer outages, UPS will allow you to save your work and safely hibernate the device so work can resume when power is restored.
This UPS offers quite a high power rating, 900W is far more than what most PCs consume. This is good because it means that it will continue to function even if you upgrade to a more powerful computer, or if you use a lower powered computer it will last much longer, giving you more opportunity to shut down the device.
Longevity is quite good: I have another UPS from the same brand and it still works after several months.
A significant downside is this UPS uses a modified sine wave (simulated sine wave, square wave) inverter that is fine for computers and laptops, but may be problematic in other devices, such as appliances with AC motors. If you’re plugging in something other than a computer or laptop, make sure the device is safe to use with square wave, otherwise you risk damage.
It is a relatively small size but still quite heavy due to use of sealed lead acid batteries. The small size makes it easier to transport and carry so you could even use this for portable power in a pinch. Lead acid batteries have low energy density and don’t offer much of a price per kwh advantage these days, however they excel at providing a high power output at low cost. Lithium batteries at the same power output would cost twice as much as lead acid, while providing quadruple the capacity and having better longevity/ service life.
Due to the smaller battery size. You can also only expect a shorter window of time to safely shut down the computer before the battery is depleted. The specs say 24V 9A (216wh). In my tests measuring the usable power, the total usable capacity was measured at around 110wh, which checks out as 50% usable is normal for lead acid batteries. You can potentially run a 900W device but you will only have 8 minutes to shut it down.
The power draw when charging is a steady 40W. The LCD screen is backlit and offers a broad overview of the status, including a 4-bar representation of battery status (I would prefer a more precise reading). Interestingly, even with nothing connected the bottom of the case is warm at 100F in an 80F environment. This temperature does not increase while outputting power.
The beeps are of moderate volume. There’s repeated beeps providing a 1 minute warning for depleted battery that cannot be disabled. Beeps during initial power loss can be disabled. To disable, you have to first disconnect power and then press the power button to toggle it off. The next time you lose power it will stay quiet. However there is no internal storage of the settings so if the UPS shuts down due to lack of power, the beeps will default to enabled status.
In summary, this is a square wave UPS that is an economical way to add redundancy to your computer during power outages.

title: Disappointed
text:
Very disappointed with this product as it repeatedly fails the set-up procedure. I returned the first unit, received a second one, and it also failed. The set-up routine will not activate the phone camera function that is required for scanning the QR code. It eventually times out with a "failed to connect to the network" message. Just to confirm I have made every effort, here are the steps I have tried:

1. Successfully set-up two other EUFY camera models (indoor pan & tilt types) using the same EUFY app, same procedure, same 2.4 network, and same Smartphone. That all went well so would indicate my network and phone are not the issues
2. Reloaded the EUFY App to current version
3. Tried two different E40 Solo Pro cameras
4. Tried two different Android Smartphone's (LG & ZTE)
5. Spoke with EUFY customer support and verified the procedure was correct and should work. They suggested turning off mobile data. getting closer to the router, and trying a different phone. Tried all three suggestions.

One other reviewer of a similar model (E20) has also encountered the problem. Both the E20 & E40 are new models but use the same set-up app as the other EUFY products. Obviously there is some sort of mismatch involved but I'm at a loss as to what it is. I suspect it has something to do with the new model app code (or camera firmware) & certain phone models. Too bad because the E20/E40 appear to be affordable well-built products with a number of nice features. I gave the product 3 stars on the assumption that it is probably a good product since others have activated it so it "may be" a mismatch on my end. Still, the company needs to investigate and hopefully fix the problem.

title: I liked the Topping EX5 so much, I bought the company!
text:
I didn't buy the company, but I did buy a 2nd Topping EX5 for my main stereo. I decided to go the balanced connector route for all my components in the living room stereo. This time I got a black one.

So far so great using the EX5 with the Apogee Acoustics Stages. Living the good life for sure! Great DAC. A bargain even if you aren't using it to power headphones.

PS: Someone from Japan passed on some misinformation about the EX5's balanced IO (XLR) not really being balanced. As anyone can clearly see in picture #2, those are balanced XLR cables which go to the balanced input of the power amp. If there's an electrical engineer with schematics that is willing to discuss the matter, please alert me. For now, I'll go with the empirical results in my living room.

[Original Review with Silver EX5]
I listened to several songs encoded at 192khz@24bit. Indeed there is more to be had from digital music than CDs. Really stunning in terms of quiet background and extended high frequencies.

I've seen a few disparaging remarks about the Topping EX5. I don't have an FFT analyzer or even an oscillioscope at this point in my life. However I am somewhat of a jazz musician and my ears have miraculously survived somehow.

Using a Hifiman Sundara phones with New Fantasia balanced cables. Highly recommended all! Unless you can afford anything you want.

title: Use MCUFRIEND_kbv library
text:
Display looks nice, installs neatly on top of Mega board, but blocks the rest of the pins. With right-angle pins, you should be able to get around that if necessary, or use cables to connect it instead.

Install the library MCUFRIEND_kbv to use this board. There's a github repository with source and directions, prenticedavid / MCUFRIEND_kbv.

You also need to install the Adafruit GFX Library - install the BusIO dependency if it asks.

When you install the library, there are some example sketches installed as well, try the GLUE_DEMO_480x320 just to check if everything works. Uses 29,724 bytes.

I haven't checked for anything that uses the microSD slot , but it should be easy to find.

title: Great Router
text:
Replaced an old +10 yr old router that was only getting 15Mbps (out of the 100Mbps we pay for.) Now we are getting 40-45Mbps, higher if closer to the router. Old router was also dropping signal several times a day (very annoying.) Zero drops with the new router after about a week. Quite happy with the Nighthawk purchase so far.

This router sends out 2 Wi-Fi networks: a 5G network and a normal one. The 5G sends out a faster speed but to a smaller area, so if you are having trouble with slow speeds or disconnects, check to see if you are on the regular network (which covers a larger area.) Netgear also asks you to use a mobile device to install the router, but there is an option to install the router if you don't have one available. Setup was not difficult. So far, so good. Thanks!

title: Great Little Adapter--Needs HEIC Converter Program
text:
UPDATE: Downgraded to three stars as it only lasted a year before the iphone stopped connecting to it. It might be worth it for a year of use, but I'm not getting another one.

Nicely made unit. Seems of good quality. Easy to use.

You find it on your phone after you plug in the flash drive by going to the file folder app and to the little blue browse file icon on the bottom right (can read ntfs as well as exfat and fat32). Some say if you want to transfer from iphone to flash drive make sure the flash drive is formatted with exfat or fat32 as you can lose data with ntfs. Your flash drive should be the list of "Locations" after "On My iPhone" (scroll down) you should see either your flash drive name (e.g., Kingston) or Untitled. Tap it and it will open to view files. Long tap on the file you want to play/view and short tap to play.

To download photos from iphone to flash drive, go to your photos app files and select the photos/movies you want to download. Tap on the upload icon (bottom left) and scroll down to "Save to Files" and tap that. Scroll down to your flash drive icon and click on the folder you want to copy to. Then click on "Save" (upper right) and wait for the loading to finish (it will go back to the original photos screen that you selected the photos/movies to upload from when it's finished.

Movies play fine, but photo files are all in heic format which none of my photo programs can read and maybe yours can't either. So, go to the Microsoft store and get an app to convert the photos to jpg or another format you want. I found converters that have a limit on photos per day without buying the upgraded version, but one free one that seems to have no limit is the Real HEIC Converter (its store title is "HEIC to JPEG, HEIC to PNG, HEIC to JPG, HEIC to BMP,..."). When you choose files to convert, make sure you choose the second grouping that starts with IMG. There is a first grouping that starts with ._IMG which are not the actual photo files.

It's a great little adapter, but needs help by adding an HEIC converter program which is why I give 4 stars. I do wonder why the flash drives made for apple transfer have that already done. Apparently their apps do the conversion.

title: Wish it had more audio juice
text:
Overall I am quite happy with this projector, I am shooting straight to a wall that is 25ft away and the quality of images is truly impeccable! The amazing feature of the digital zoom in or out allows you to shrink or widen the boarders of projection basically down to the order of inches, it is remarkable.
The remote control is super handy even if at times you really have to point it at but it is a minor problem.
The only thing I wish it would be different is this: there are 2 ways you can connect it to (in my case) a quite powerful sound bar and it is via bluetooth or via AUX cable. I have it hooked on both, why? Because the bluetooth has a very slight lag between video and audio (half a second at most) and of course the Aux doesn't!
Now the makers of this great toy would just have to turn the volume output signal a bit more because, even with the main volume almost at 100%, the signal isn't enough to appreciate the potential sound of a sound bar (in my case even hooked to an exterior sub-woofer) because there isn't enough juice coming out of the source (the projector) in the first place. When you are on Bluetooth you have more range hence louder sound but you get lag, when you are on AUX, you get no lag but basically very little volume. I have both projector and sound bar turned all the way up and I still have to pay attention to sounds and words in order to catch them.
Turn the inner volume signal up Fangor! That is all you are missing really!
Antonio

title: Fantastic Theater in a Box
text:
I have been jonesing for one of these - along with Optoma, Vava etc, for a year or more - and so it's probably the most research I ever did on a single device - as well as now knowing far too much about the overall scene. I did lust after the triple laser version, but the price difference was too steep a cliff for me.

It's oddly hard to see one of these in person - Best Buy is useless and I couldn't find one set up anywhere, although it's easy enough to buy. I had realistic expectations about the brightness relative to a normal daylight living room, but once I got it out of the box and set up I was sort of surprised to see that it wasn't just "watchable" in daylight, but crisp, distinct and pleasant to watch. At two PM on a fairly sunny day, in a south facing room with huge windows.

With our blinds down - or after dark, it's a staggering difference. I use OLED screens at work - but my home TVs are a QLED and a Sony micro-LED - blacks obviously don't meet the OLED bar - but I was also wary that this was more expensive than even a 65 inch 2021 OLED, and that picture quality would not be as good. But the trade-off - absolutely massive, so far faultless 4k real estate and a more-than-adequate built-in soundbar - is well worth it.

I'm currently using on an older white projection screen - and it looks fantastic - so next step will be an ambient light rejecting/cinegrey screen - but I haven't figured out what the "no-brainer" <$200 model is - feel free to recommend... I'd like something with a stand or a frame, but even if the picture improvement is marginal- I'll be delighted.

Games work fine - was nervous about latency being dramatic - but even twitchier FPS game modes are fine - or at least my ability to detect or be bothered by the latency is aging out along with the rest of me. I already won a few rounds of SWAT on Halo, which is my go-to for testing latency vs input. They also look spectacular - and driving games look incredible - as does Flight Simulator on Xbox Series X.

Audio is a big deal because I want as plug n play solution for movie nights - I HAVE better stuff here - two Atmos systems and a true audiophile bar, but I don't want to fuss with it - and want my family to be able to handle without me there, so it was important it have fidelity, oomph and at least enough bass to sell action movies - and it's great. In fact the projector itself is close enough to silent so even at low volumes, the built-in speaker works perfectly.

Samsung's array of Apps is available - matching my QLED setup right down to how buggy HBO Max is... and it copied all my apps and settings from that set during initial setup - (although it doesn't copy individual HDMI settings, so you may still have to go turn off motion smoothing, tweak for games etc) so all I really had to do was log into the streaming apps - and for me at least, no need for a Fire stick - some of the Chinese boxes are missing either Netflix or Prime and thus require a stick or STB. Full disclosure, I will probably use a mix of built in and Xbox Series X apps depending on the bitrate/audio support of each application.

I could have gotten a cheaper box with similar tech. I could have gotten a triple laser for a similar price, but there was no sense of risk or worry about reliability here and I know Samsung will do at least moderately good support for new apps and updates for buggy ones. I'm still befuddled that I don't have to tinker with focus or moire effect or pincushion or geometry or any of that normal projector stuff - plugged it in, turned it on and bingo! It worked.

I will be adjusting it to tune it to my preferred granular look and feel - but even if those options weren't available, I'd still be delighted by this thing.

title: A waste of my money ultimately.
text:
I bought this as a replacement for a similar HP printer that I had had for several years of faithful service. I skimmed over reviews and discredited, unfortunately, the comment about how flimsy the parts were and a few other negatives. It would be my 3rd HP printer over more than 20 years and I was sure it would perform.
Sadly, the reports of flimsy parts and construction weren't understated. The paper trays, guides etc. all were light plastic and tended to catch and needed careful adjustment to function. Nevertheless, the first prints were excellent and with gentle use all was well.
However, problems started after the starter ink supply ran out. Purchasing new ink from HP, was a trial of paying close attention to the model--because they don't standardize the cassettes. The inks for this printer a tiny--Take note! Next, the ink dries out very quickly and jams up. After the first ink ran out, the cyan never printed properly again--despite all efforts to correct the problem. Useless for photos, I continued to use it as a printer for documents while I worked from home.
I was then stunned to discover that the scanner only scans into GIF format. That is, no PDF, RTF, JPG or any other format are supported. Okay for that quick scan of a single item, but pretty useless for documents. And questionable why they'd bother putting in a document feeder.
The last straw came when the paper tray ceased pulling paper correctly would jam inside if more than 10 sheets were in the tray.
I finally bit the bullet and paid the extra cost of an Epson printer/scanner, which has the stability of product I expected and has functioned flawlessly.
I can only emphasize my dissatisfaction and won't ever buy an HP again.

title: Improvements Over Similar Mini Projectors
text:
Pros:

Comes with a tripod! This is a huge bonus. The tripod locks in place and is easily adjustable.
Rear facing speakers have improved sound over previous models. Decent sound for the size.
WiFi connection and screen mirroring is great. I've only tried Android, but it works flawlessly.
Easy source selection now from a home screen.
Remote control is small and simple to use.
Picture quality is decent at this price point. Plenty bright in a dark room.

Cons:

These mini projectors are indeed mini. So are the cooling fans. Which must spin quickly and create some noise. I found it minimal and not too distracting with audio at a reasonable volume. I feel like the cooling fan is more quiet than previous models.
There is Keystone adjustment. But too much Keystone makes it difficult to focus all areas of the screen. The fix? Be sure the projector is throwing an image as level as possible to limit the need for Keystone adjustment.
I found the picture to wash out quite a bit in a room full of daylight. But, let's be honest, nearly all projectors do this in a well lit room. I am projecting onto a wall and normal painted surface not intended for image projection. This may be completely different on an actual projection screen with gain.

Tested with Nvidia Shield Pro @ 1080p via HDMI.

Get this unit on sale or even with an available coupon and it is really hard to beat. It's very portable and easy to setup when moved. I definitely notice hardware improvements from previous model years. If I encounter any quality issues, I will update my review. As of now, I have no issue recommending this unit for casual projecting.

I go through corded headphones about one per year. I had this for at least three years, possibly four. BTW, the reason I bought it was because my phone's headphone jack was damaged at the gym. My phone was otherwise fine, so I grabbed these BT headphones.

I remember being too cheap top buy the awesome bass from hell $80 version and settling for $50. It had less bass in the store, but when I got home, I no longer thought that. It was perfect. It works well for music and calls. It worked well with my phone and computer, and the BT button was great for moving between devices when my devices got too dumb to know what I was using.

I'm bald. I don't know if it's a problem for people with hair, but I can't look down while wearing these headphones. To drop something and to pick it up means the headphones will slide and roll forward, unfold and fall off your head.

I also noticed that the sound cancelling tech or whatever it w3as was totally annoying. I heard EVERY FOOTSTEP on the treadmill like Frankenstein footsteps. I will admit that I can't remember any of the instructions that came with it. If this was a flaw in noise cancellation tech, and if there was a way to defeat it, I'm obvious.

Other than that, for sitting at my computer and listening/composing music, it was great. I heard subtle parts of songs that I had never noticed in 40 years.

title: Died after a couple of hours. Worst Customer Service from Samsung.
text:
So I decided I was going to go all in with Samsung and get rid of my iPad Pro. I ordered a 512GB Tab S7+ directly from Samsung. I wanted one with cellular, but Samsung doesn't offer one in the 512GB config which was frustrating. I still decide to order it along with a keyboard case. Samsung throws in a gaming controller (which I have no use for, but it's free so okay) I receive the tablet and the case on Friday 1/29/2021. I transfer apps from my Note 10 to it, get it all set up. It seemed like an awesome tablet. I charged it overnight and the next day I used it for a couple of hours. Then the screen just goes black and when I press the power button, I get a flash of blue, but nothing else. I know it is charged, but I go ahead and place it back on the charger. A few hours later I try again and still nothing but a quick flash of blue light.
I called Samsung, they have me press the power and the down volume buttons (which I had already tried) it still does nothing but the flash of blue light. I was told that since I just got the tablet I would need to return it but the department that handles that is close and I need to call the following morning Sunday 1/21/2021. So the next day (today) I call and speak with Rose Veluz at Samsung. I am told that the only option is for Samsung to send me a return label and once they get the device back from me they will refund my money and reorder the tablet. This means I will have to wait until the funds are credited which I imagine will take a while as that will not even happen until after I get this shipped off and they receive it, or I reorder now and have doubled the funds tied up until they credit me. To top it off since the controller that they included (without me asking) has not been delivered yet I would not get a full refund until I receive and return the controller.

I stressed how inconvenient this is and my dissatisfaction with the whole process since I purchased an expensive tablet that lasted one day and now I am being inconvenienced both in my time and money. Basically I’m told that’s just the way it is and there are no other options. I asked if it would be possible for me to return the item to a local Best Buy and pick up another one there and I was told no. I again stress that this is not acceptable and I am then told that for my inconvenience she will credit me 10% off the item if I reorder it. 10% is not amazing, but in addition to the keyboard case I ordered from Samsung I had already ordered and received a regular case from Amazon for the tablet. This means I will have this other case which I have to return to Amazon or it will serve no use. I also did like the tablet for the few hours that it was working so I think maybe I will go ahead and give it another try even though it will mean tying up funds on my card until Samsung credits me for the first order.

I asked how I will go about reordering the item in receiving the 10% and I am told that I can place the order online and after it ships I can re-contact Samsung and ask that they credit me 10%. I explained to her that when I ordered it online there were some promotions and I don’t know that they are still in effect and I ask if there’s just the way for her or somebody at Samsung to order it while I’m on the phone at the price I previously paid -10% and I am told no.

I understand that sometimes electronic items fail and that normally happens shortly after it is used. The issue here is the poor customer service of Samsung by having no options for replacing the tablet and not charge my card unless they don’t receive the previous one back, or at minimum have a way of expediting in order at the price I paid -10% without me having to jump through a bunch of hoops.

title: Disappointing
text:
I own a Nikon Monarch 7 10x42, a Nikon Prostaff 7S 8x30, and I wanted another pocket one for use in residential areas, so I thought I'll just get these Aculon 10x25 since they were on sale at about $43. I have some kid's 12x25 binoculars that cost $20 as well but those look like toys. (the green one in my uploaded review photos)

I feel like buying the Aculon was a mistake. The kid's binoculars actually perform better, wider FOV, and believe it or not, actually brighter. The Aculon is narrower and darker.

Size-wise, the Aculon is actually as tall as the 8x30 Prostaff, and just as wide when unfolded completely. It's hard to call the Aculon "pocket sized". It's definitely not pants pocket sized, but if you holster it, you can hide the holster.

It is easier for adult sized hands to operate than the kid's ones.

The Aculon isn't bad in comparison to the store-shelf brands and no-name brands, but it's actually getting beat by kid's binoculars. I would shop around a bit more. Definitely do not pay full price for these. I think this product is detrimental to Nikon's reputation, because Nikon Prostaff and Nikon Monarch are absolutely amazing.

The physical construction is pretty beefcake, the hinge is definitely an appropriate stiffness. (one of the negative reviews here said it was too loose, I don't think it's too loose at all).

The accessories that are included feels like an afterthought, an afterthought with Nikon branding all over them.

title: Official Salcomp Apple charger.
text:
So.. Apple has 2-3 manufacturers making the 18-20w model of chargers @ 9v2A and 9v 2.22A. I received 2 SALCOMP made 20w chargers that seem to be official and well made.

Not sure why people are getting "fakes" but I can confirm the ones I received are legit.

Build wise, its quite nice. Charges 16.x~w on a 13 mini. 19.x~w on a 13 Pro MAX under 50%. Value wise? Well.. It's an apple accessory so it's "overpriced", but not too overpriced either.. Mixed feelings.

Anker's C TUV US certified chargers cost around $14 bucks so $5 more for an official UL listed certified charger isn't the worse thing in the world.

Apple claims they're going "green" by not including this charger in the box, but they're indirectly causing a bigger carbon foot print with alternative charger packaging and 3rd party shipping. The reality? They want more money and other companies are playing follow the leader.

As a stand alone product? 4 stars. The value would be better if this was closer to the $10-15 bracket of mini GaN units. (This apple charger runs cooler).

As a necessity for a newer phone? 1-2 stars. Complete non sense.

title: A good music player for swimmers
text:
I bought this as a music player for swimming. I had been having trouble with earbuds. They were uncomfortable or didn't fit or fell out constantly. So I thought I'd give bone conduction a try. I've really liked them so far.

Disclaimer: If you use these under water, you have to use MP3 mode. Bluetooth waves cannot travel through water.

Pros: They sound better under the water than they do in the air. The sound quality is pretty good and the volume can go high enough to drown out my splashing. They are pretty easy to use by touch alone. The memory space is decent as well. I have 500 songs on mine and that takes up less than half of the total memory.

Cons: They aren't adjustable. If I wear them as intended while swimming, the connecting loop was constantly rubbing against my shoulders with every stroke. It got annoying fast. However, I figured out a work around. Putting the loop higher on my head and using a swim cap to hold the device tight against my head works well. The conduction still works even when placed higher on my cheek bones. There is no shuffle feature either. So unless you hand shuffle your mp3 library, the songs will play in the order they were downloaded.

I have not had the device very long, so I cannot attest to its long term durability. For the price, it's a good option for swimmers that don't like earbuds.
