title: Revised review after 4 mth use
text:
Revised review (1 star) while the watch seemed to track heart rate accurately initially (and still does if I'm just walking) I have had major issues with the heart rate tracking during mixed cardio activities. The BPM figures seemed excessively high compared to actual, which I validated by intermittent manual heart rate checks. I also did several mixed cardio workouts wearing the Vivoactive on one wrist and my Forerunner45s on the other, and saw differences of as much as 50BPM between the data on the two watches, with the Vivoactive measuring high. I contacted Garmin support and after multiple submissions of data, they picked two samples (1 walking, 1 cardio) out of many and said that the results were within reason. Never mind that there were many others that were not within reason! I cannot use this watch to track my cardio activity, Garmin says there's nothing wrong with it, and I'm stuck. Do not buy this product. In fact, I don't recommend buying ANY Garmin product - their warranty and support are useless.

Original review (3 star) This watch replaced my Forerunner 45s, which I liked until the sockets that held the band broke and could not be fixed. I selected the Vivoactive 4s because it was closest in size to my previous small watch, and had all the features of the old watch plus additional features of interest. The 4s seems to be accurate in tracking steps, distance, time, and heart rate. Cosmetically, the watch I received has a light gold case but silver buckle on its dusty pink band, which doesn't look great but is probably not noticeable to others. The watch faces included by Garmin have sparse feature content, and I do not like the fake analog hands; however, I was able to download a very good digital watch face free from Garmin Connect.

The major drawback of this watch is the miserable performance on counting stair climbs and descents. The results are extremely inconsistent - sometimes high, sometimes low. I have read Garmin's suggestions on correcting this, which tell you to swing your arms while going up and down (maybe outdoors if you're on a hill, but what kind if nutcase swings their arms going up and down stairs?) If this is Garmin's solution for excluding altitude changes such as riding in an elevator, surely there is a better method. I am resigned to accepting the lousy performance of this feature and just not tracking stair climbing, but I could have purchased a cheaper watch without the stairs climbed feature.

title: They are functional but not ideal
text:
I tested both of them against a multi-meter. They read slightly different from each other but pretty close. The first thing you have to know is, when is a battery dead? Of course its when it wont power anything but what that "thing" is makes a difference. My Dish remote and my Xbox controller start complaining about low battery before the battery is dead, and will eventually stop working if I dont replace them. But I can take those batteries and power LED light strips in my pantry, etc. and they may work for weeks to months depending on the activity at the LED location.

Searching online, batteries are "dead" at about 1.2 volts, but those batteries will work in those LED lights for a while as I said. I had the opportunity to test truly dead batteries that died in those LED lights, batteries that will power those lights but make remotes indicate low battery, and brand new batteries (usually test at 1.5 to 1.6 volts). These testers gave repeatable results, but I now know that the yellow "replace" area of the meter really means "low" and pretty much anything below the yellow "replace" area are dead. Anything in the green area is in great shape.

This only matters for devices that use more than one battery. You can waste a lot of money throwing away all 4 batteries, for instance, instead of seeing if they are all actually dead. When those LED strips go dim, its not unusual to find that only one or two batteries are actually dead. One dead cell can make a device not work.

I dont really like these testers but there isn't much out there these days to choose from, oddly enough. It's a bit cumbersome to hold the battery in place (I've only tested AA batteries) and close the clamp, and its weird that you have to insert the battery, what common sense tells me it positive "up"...positive "down" Its just strange and backwards; but then again I dont understand twist ties twisted counter-clockwise either. Americans know its "righty-tighty-lefty-loosy" but in other countries, apparently its the opposite.

I gave 4 stars, but only three stars on the overall function. it's a three star product I gave an extra star for being so danged cheap. I'd rather pay more and get abetter product though. These will suffice now that I know how they read batteries.

title: This is an excellent disc player; don't expect anything else.
text:
I never thought I would be buying a $500 Blu-Ray player, but here we are. Physical media is dying and rightfully so as streaming quality becomes more and more passable, but right now, it's not up to my standards. If you have an OLED TV, 4k projector, or proper surround sound, then you are really not getting the most out of your gear by only watching streaming media. Through streaming, video and especially audio are still getting compressed, even when you think you're getting a 4k stream with Dolby Atmos. It just doesn't compare to the quality you get from a physical disc. I was really surprised how even 1080p Blu-Rays look from this player compared to streaming. They actually look a lot better than 4k content over streaming.

It's a little maddening that we have all these capable 4k TVs and receivers capable of 7.2.4 channel Dolby Atmos and then most of the content that people are playing on these devices is compressed /lossy / ruined. The people that make this content put so much effort into producing it at the highest quality and then consumers are generally only viewing it in this sub-par state. Anyway, getting a good Blu-ray player like this one is the best solution to viewing content in the way it was intended.

After doing some research, it seems there are lots of crappy 4k UHD / Blu-ray players out there and I just did not want to struggle with a device that does not do what it's supposed to do. So far, this player has performed perfectly; no skipping or discs not working. No issues with content being transmitted in the proper format to my receiver- I'm getting 4k, HDR, and Dolby Atmos without any problems.

All of the bad reviews I've seen on this player seem to be because the additional features aren't working great (playing video from USB, Netflix app, etc). My advice: buy the right tool for the job. This tool plays 4k UHD / Blu-Ray discs. Wouldn't bother trying to play anything else on this device. Get a different device for streaming like Roku Ultra, Apple Tv, or Nvidia Shield. Those won't let you down.

My only criticism for the Panasonic is that the remote sucks. 1) It's not backlit and 2) the Netflix button is too close to the pause/play buttons and when you accidently hit the Netflix button, your movie stops and the Netflix app opens up; very annoying- have to be careful. Any higher end home theater-use remote should be backlit. I use this in the dark with a projector so it's kind of stupid to have to struggle to see the buttons. My receiver also has a non-backlit remote so I'm used to this problem.

Anyways, if you want a 4k UHD Blu-ray player that plays discs without failing, get this one. Don't expect any of the extra features to work and you'll be satisfied.

title: Good quality dash cam with lots of features, gets too hot and no buffered parking mode anymore
text:
I have tested and reviewed many dash cams and this is one of the very good ones in the market right now.
It uses the STARVIS sensor which belongs to Sony and you can never go wrong with Sony. The quality is really really good.
The 2inch LCD is not that big but it does help in having a feeling of what you're recording, for better preview, I'd recommend using your phone and the App which I explained below.
The advantage of the plus duo system is that you can add the 2nd camera to get a dual channel system. The front can go up to 2k QHD at 60fps and the rear can go as far as 1080P 30fps. There was an issue a couple of month back where you couldn't maximize the quality and fps on both front and rear camera but I've heard Viofo has fixed that by a new firmware so I strongly recommend updating your firmware to be able to get the maximum quality.
If you want a 4K you got to go to the A129 Pro but this one in my opinion is more than enough, since it gives you 2K at 60fps, you never miss a license plate or a face on your footage which is exactly what you need from a dashcam.
The field of view is pretty good at 140 degrees, I've seen a few cameras at 150 and 160 which is better obviously but 140 degrees is still pretty good imo
One advantage is that this new model allows you to record H.265 video codec which can save you a lot of space on your mirco SD when recording videos as it decreases the files sizes drastically. Remember to utilize this option for sure by stopping recording first, holding the mic button and changing the setting on the SD card icon.
The GPS works like a charm, very accurate and the time and locations stamps and the speed that it records are all very accurate.
One of the nicest features that it has is the fact that it has a 5GHz WiFi, as you know most newer devices have 5GHz while old ones are still running on 2.4GHz. The 5GHz makes it really easy to quickly download files to your phone without using any cables. btw there's no cloud service with Viofo, only you and your micro SD cards.
The Viofo App is designed pretty good, it allows you to get your travel data from it and you can see a preview of what the camera is and will be recording on your cell phone.
One disadvantage in my opinion is that Viofo for some reason removed the buffered parking mode option from this model. Not sure if it's back yet but last time I checked the firmware, it wasn't there. It does have the option of motion and impact being triggers when parked at a parking but the buffered option is not there. Apparently limited to A129 Pro only now.
Another minor this advantage which is not really a big deal but important to some people is that it gets really hot. Specially when it's processing and recording at higher qualities and frame per second rates. Nothing harmful but I've never seen a dash cam get this hot. So something weird going on there.
Overall, this is a very good quality camera with a Sony sensor H.265 codec option, front camera at 2K 60fps and rear at 1080P and 30fps with lots of options and features on the App. I do recommend this camera if you are looking for a decent priced reliable 2K camera that does offer 60fps. I just hope they bring back the buffer parking mode option.

title: Artist Review - Digital Illustration & Design
text:
- Gorgeous Bright Screen
- Fantastic Pen with a rubbery nib that gives you nice resistance on the screen's glass surface
- Surprisingly Good Speakers
- Expandable Micro SD Storage
- Holds Its Battery When Not In Use
- No Slowdown When Doing Art
- Handy Front-facing Camera

------------
------------
OWNED FOR 5 MONTHS:

FIRST and FOREMOST, I purchased this tablet to use as a pen display for my Windows PC. Tab S7+ connects to your PC in a number of ways, both wireless and wired. You can either mirror your tablet screen to your PC or your PC screen to your tablet. But these baked-in features, though good in certain ways, are not robust enough to give you a premium digital pen display experience.

To use Tab S7 as a high quality pen display with your desktop art apps, I recommend Superdisplay - a $15 app that you'd download onto your tablet through Google Play store. Superdisplay only works on Windows OS currently. Additionally, you might want to buy a 6 feet (usb-c male to usb-a male) cable because you'll want a nice wired connection to eliminate lag while avoiding the frustration of a short plug chaining you too close to your PC tower. I also purchased a Parblo PR 100 tablet stand so that my Tab S7 would be angled up rather than lying completely flat. A small mini bluetooth keyboard rounds out my pen display setup.

When using this as a pen display (through the Superdisplay app), I use Photoshop, Illustrator, ArtRage, After Effects - basically everything I use on my PC can be interacted with on my Tab S7+. The S Pen itself is nearly perfect in my opinion, and you get all your pressure sensitivity inside your art apps. And you can extend your PC screen to your Tab in either portrait or landscape. It only takes a small time to get used to the setup, but once you do, it becomes an easy plug-and-play. Connect your usb-c cord when you want a pen display; remove the cord when you just want to use it as a standalone tablet.

------------
------------

Small Gripes:
- As a 12.4 inch tablet, using desktop apps in portrait mode takes some getting used to within the narrow space. I can see the advantage of the extra space of iPad Pro's 12.9 inch screen, BUT this small issue isn't big enough to make me opt for an iPad. I value the openness of the Android OS.

- Battery life is great when using the Tab for regular tablet stuff. But when it comes to doing serious art, the battery life can drop from about 10hrs to about 4hrs. Rarely am I far away from a power source longer than 4hrs though.

- As a HEAVY user of the S Pen, I'm rounding down the pen nib. Tab S7 does not come with replacement nibs. I spoke with Samsung about this and they decided to send me another S Pen, but the pen that came with the unit is not worn away completely. I still use it.

- Android art apps are not as numerous as on Apple's platform, but among the selection available on Android are high quality and professional level apps. Noteworthy for my illustration work are Clip Studio and Infinite Painter. Sketchbook Pro and ArtRage are good ones too.

------------
------------

Drawing on this Tab S7+ as a pen display or just a tablet has been heavenly.

title: An OK options in a limited field
text:
I have actually purchased two of these sets. Each set lasted 3-4 years, at which point one of the receiver/amplifiers died, rendering the entire system basically useless. (A single surround speaker can mess with your head after a while.)

Unfortunately, there doesn't seem to be much of a market for making surround speakers wireless. Given the rise of soundbars with remote subwoofers and surround satellite speakers, this makes sense. But if you prefer the sound of your old-school speakers from a traditional amplifier, your options are limited.

There is a better option toward the bottom of this review.

PROS:
- Decent sound
- Avoids the need for an awkward wire run either through a crawlspace/attic or across a room
- Separate receiver/amplifiers further reduce the need to run wires to two speakers from a single device.

CONS:
- EXPENSIVE (I managed to purchase my last one for $80, but the normal cost is $200)
- Some static/noise when not using the system
- Receivers seem to have a limited lifespan
- Can mess with 2.4 GHz deviced, including Bluetooth, wireless phones, and WiFi
- Doesn't take much to disrupt the signal even a mere 20' away. It claims to extend to 300'. You have been warned.
- Replacement parts are not readily available. (Trust me, I've tried.)

I also use a RocketFish system (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B000VEP3XO) which performs the same function, but has a single receiver that powers both speakers. I hear no ambient static, and the system has not failed me in over 6 years. Costs $120, but you can get it as low as $80. Unfortunately, I can't find a way to actually purchase it on Amazon, so search for "rocketfish wireless rear speaker kit" in your favorite search engine, and you'll find it quickly.

Geekria Case received today. It's nice. Much nicer than I thought it would be. The headphone ear-cup divider has an integrated magnet that, like Apple's Smart Case, puts the headphones into deep sleep mode. Pretty sweet.

The internal hanger, the divider/magnet and the storage pocket are all velcro'd into the case and can be placed to your spec. The case is a very nice fit to the headphones and has an overall nice fit/finish. The exterior has a soft/durable material that feels nice to hold. The case provides strong outer protection.

The case's headphone cup divider has a velcro strip that I needed to affix to the bottom of the divider - the velcro strip was loose in the case. I see another review here where the buyer complains the velcro strip is missing - you can see it in his pictures - it's just adhered to the case (peel it off and stick it to the divider). Once I placed the velcro on the divider it stuck firmly/permanently. Once I put the divider in place, it's rock solid - perfect.

Only one small nit: Charging the AirPods Max in the case is possible BUT the cable's exit point at the bottom of the ear cup is slightly tight with the clamshell style case closed - however, the dual zippers work well to accommodate the power cable's exit when closed.

title: Great screen, but a few problems
text:
The screen is big and vivid. It's hard to imagine better. Three problems, however:
1. Someone thought it would be really cool to locate nearly all the ports on the bottom where they cannot be seen. Plugging in a cable requires removing at least half of what's on a desk and then performing neck gymnastics to see underneath. If you wear glasses, recruit someone else to do this because you and your glasses might not fit. Every time you do this, you'll will wonder whether someone on the design team dislikes people who use monitors.
2. The manual is not written for people who read manuals. It tells you that some ports are upstream and others are downstream without telling you what those terms mean and why they matter. It took me a half hour googling them to find out. The manual is similarly mysterious about other things a user might want to know such as whether the monitor should be left on 24/7 or turned off when not in use.
3. The USB-C-to-USB-C connection was nice because it carried two-way traffic -- images from my laptop to the screen and electricity in the other direction so the monitor charged my laptop battery. After a year it became a one-way street, the electricity flowing but the images no longer appearing on the screen. I bought three cables highly rated on Amazon. When I plugged each of them in, the monitor sternly warned that the cable was unauthorized and dire events would happen if I used it. I gave up and now use an HDMI cable to get images to the screen. Other reviewers have complained about the cables that came with the monitor, so I assume that was the problem here. I also suspect that the dire warnings are insincere.

title: Zeos Knows What's Up
text:
I already loved my DT 770 Pro 80 ohms with the stock pads, but after watching Z Reviews' lil pad swap adventure with the Beyerdynamic lineup, I can see why he recommended these leather ones the most. It increased a lot of the soundstage and instrument separation, making my already favorite, daily drivers even more my favorite.

Of course there was also a slight emphasis on bass treble, with a little scoop in the mids, but it didn't make them super recessed like their graph based on the DT 1990 would lead you to believe. Thankfully the treble emphasis isn't too much, depending on how well mixed your music is. Personally, I found some Deftones tracks a bit harder to listen to now since it now sort of emphasizes the sibilance from Chino's vocals. But that's probably more him interacting with the mic and how the sound engineer treated it since I never experienced any problems otherwise.

The leather is super soft and having actual memory foam really made these so much more comfortable to wear. There was a small period of a day or so where the clamp force was a lot, but after breaking it in, it got a lot better to wear.

Surprisingly, despite the leather creating a deeper seal than the stock velour pads, I haven't had much in the way of heat around my ears.

Overall, great pads, definitely recommend these if you have any closed back Beyerdynamic headphones.

title: Amazing for a Highly Sensitive Person
text:

The sixth level is very clear for dialogue. I don't have hearing loss, but am very sensitive to noise and hate loud background music/effects. The music alone plays nicely. When talking starts, it fades into the background without blocking the talking.

My only complaint is that the volume adjustment could be a bit finer...one click turns it up just a bit too much but not much to complain about given how well it works. Perhaps the higher versions would have a more sensitive volume control. regardless....I HIGHLY recommend this for everyone.

Your neighbors won't have to listen to the roaring noise because the voices aren't discernable in most modern cinema/tv. Plus, if you are sensitive to noise, as I am, this is a saving grace speaker.

Buy it! and if you can afford the higher grade, buy that. I may save up for one of those. But this is really a great buy!

title: Bulky and Dim. Overall Terrible
text:
Preface: I don't take my time to write reviews all that often, so please understand that what I am saying below is completely objective and based on a real product comparison I made to another product (Lian Li Strimer). I'm upset not only that this is such a sad excuse for a product but also because of the amount of time I spent TRYING to make this work and it simply would not. I have no relation to Lian Li or anything, I just bought their set after installing this and seeing how terrible it was and I would like to save others from this hellfire.

If you like to shake your soda or beer can before opening it to make sure all of the carbonation is out, you will love this product. Just like drinking a warm and flat beer, this cable solution provides happiness only to a select few. I bought it because it was a little cheaper at the time but what a terrible mistake that was.

First of all, as you can see in the comparison photos, the XPG is EXTREMELY dim. Mind you this is at maximum brightness using its included controller and the same thing happens when connected to a razer chroma ARGB hub. Oh, and good luck getting all of the LEDs to work at once. Sometimes they do and sometimes they don't. To be fair, this could be the Chroma Software I am using but the point remains that Lian Li doesn't have this problem.

The ARGB 3 pin 5v connections are horribly designed and the pins are flimsy yet the connector housing is bulky and can't plug into any hubs or controllers without being shaved down (including its own included controller lol).

They are extremely stiff and you can't straighten them out anymore than is shown in the second video because the actual cables are much shorter than the light bars. Trying to bend it presents a bigger issue because it then puts SO MUCH torque on the connectors I felt uncomfortable as soon as making the connection.

The ends of the lighted strip are so large that if you, like me, have a board with the front panel USB header immediately next to the 24-pin ATX connector, you will need to either forgo the USB or shave down the connector housing of you front panel link to make room for this monstrosity. It also makes for one heck of a cable management issue if you don't have a stellar case to accommodate the connectors in the back.

Also, specific to the 8-pin GPU connectors, they are split into two cables which makes it hard to make them visually appealing (see the first picture where the Lian Li Strimer is a solid run) and you also cannot flip them over to accommodate different GPU power sockets so depending on your card, you're stuck in one configuration.

title: Nice upgrade
text:
Because video cards are so expensive this year, I could only update the RAM and CPU on my rig this year. I have an ASUS Z370-A motherboard and it’s listed as compatible, but when I installed the new CPU the computer didn’t boot. Troubleshooting said to update the BIOS which made sense because the BIOS I had was from 2018 before 9th gen Intel CPUs. Swapped the CPUs and updated the BIOS with the old CPU and then reinstalled the new CPU and it booted perfectly.

- Be sure to update your BIOS before you install the new CPU
- Only replace one thing at a time. I know it’s more work to boot up in between, but if you replace RAM, too, you won’t know what’s not working if the boot fails.
- Keep your old chip handy in case something goes wrong and you need to swap it out
- Don’t put too much conductive paste on the back. One instruction video said a drop about the size of a grain of rice. That seems right. Too much and it gets everywhere.

Overall, installation was pretty easy. It took me a couple of tries to get the orientation correct, but it only fits on one way. The hardest part, really was finding and downloading the BIOS on the ASUS website and attaching the Coolermaster radiator and fan over the top.

One note: This CPU comes with video but the HDMI out on the motherboard stopped working, It’s not an issue because I use the HDMI and DVI out from a 1070 video card.

Bottom line: it was a good upgrade. My games run moderately faster with better frame rate and nothing seems to be running hotter. I’d recommend.

title: Great media storage
text:
This new Samsung Pro Plus micro SD card is a good step forward from the previous generation one with better read and write speeds (160mb/s and 130mb/s) and slightly changed look, plus there is a nice USB reader included in the package.
There are definitely some good positives and a few minor negatives about it, or more like nitpicking or wishful thinking, but before that a few quick words about the packing and presentation. The card comes in a ultra compact packaging that is outlining all the necessary specs of it, like capacity and rated speed, also you can clearly see the product through the transparent cover, in addition there are some recommendations about what devices it can be used with.

Positives:

- It Samsung - throughout the years the company became an example of a quality when it comes to storage, so far I have never had a failed storage device from Samsung, SD cards, SSD drives or Nvme drives.
- The USB-A to micro SD card adapter is a very good quality one, sturdy and can sustain some user abuse over time, plus it can eliminate the need of a built in reader and can be used with every computer that has an available USB port.
- Respectable read and write speeds
- It can be used with most modern devices that support SD and micro SD slots - personally I am using it with my Sony a6400 camera.

Negatives:

- Not as fast as advertised - I know that there are fester models out there and I personally could not achieve the advertised up to 160Mb/s reed speeds, but regardless of that my camera was able to record 4K videos at 30FPS and 60FPS, without complaining about the storage speed not being enough.
- A bit on the pricey end - I wish that all the brands including this one lower the price by 20% at least, that just my wishful thinking.
- No card holder/protector included - other brands are including the plastic case protector for their memory cards, but Samsung are insisting on not providing those.

Overall, I like this great little micro SD card that is reliable and can be used across many modern electronic devices.

The only problem is that a drawing on this page shows a stand on the back. There is a clip on the back, which doesn't seem useful, but no stand. At my desk, I can prop it up on something, but the stand would have been better.

The fan is very light. Hanging around my neck, I wouldn't be able to tell it's there except for the breeze in my face.

A small display shows what speed it's on when you push the power button, but since I can tell that, from the sound. But when not changing the fan speed, it displays the battery charge left as a percentage.

When charging the fan, it displays the % charged which is very handy.

When charged to 100% and then used on battery at low speed, it instantly drops to 60%. I was afraid this would mean that it wouldn't run the 6 hours on low speed as promised, but it does seem to get around that time span.

When I use it at my desk, I leave it plugged in all the time.

text:
This is the second time I order this one–this time by accident (thanks so much, Amazon suggestions!)– and the second time I have the same problem. I had forgotten that last time I ordered this (again, thanks for the suggestion, Amazon!) all my Apple devices rejected it immediately. You know, that “device not compatible” message thing that starts popping up when it’s that time of the year to charging cord, except the cords were brand new. It’s not just that, though; I have to be careful how I set my devices down and not to touch them, otherwise they start screaming at me because the connection gets interrupted. Anyway, I don’t make a fuss and just order a different one because it was just $10.

Well, it’s that time of the year again, and I, again, ordered the top choice without giving it much thought. All I really care about is that I want a long cord, and $10, again, seemed like a good deal for two of them. After I ordered it I had a deja vu moment, but didn’t really give it much thought. I also have to be careful when I set my devices down and not touch them... anyway, you know how the story went from there, and my rear end is now ordering a different cord, AGAIN!

Do I have anything positive to say about this cord? Sure, I really like how long it is, and the material it’s made of is both flexible and feels well reinforced so I’m not worried it gets nicked easily. I can get that from other cords that don’t turn my phone into a parrot you just offended.

Once more, I don’t really care to get a refund or anything. It was just $10. However, I would really appreciate it if Amazon stopped putting this listing first thing in front of me when I search for a long lightning charging cord. Mark my words, numb-nuts right here will be doing the exact same thing a year from now otherwise, wasting another $10.

title: $25 battery powered portable TV?
text:
I'm old enough to remember when battery-powered TVs ran on disposable batteries, and if a hurricane was coming and you would likely lose power for days, you could continue to watch the TV coverage for however long your stockpile of batteries lasted.

But since TV went digital in the USA, now all the battery-powered TVs have non-removable lithium ion batteries that hold about 4 hours of charge, max, and once that runs out you are stuck with your disposable-battery- or crank-rechargeable- radio until the AC comes back on, probably getting more Sean Hannity than local storm coverage.

A couple of months ago I got a new Motorola Moto G Power phone, primarily because of the positive reviews of its multi-day battery life, and I thought to myself, "Self, I wonder if anyone makes an Android TV tuner, and would that, and maybe one or two lithium ion 'power bank' phone rechargers be enough to get me through a long hurricane power outage?" The google led me here to this $25 dongle.

I bought the PT682C model with the USB-C interface, and I am happy to report that this little thing is pretty neat. It comes with two antennas: (1) a pocket-friendly wire loop that receives a handful of channels, and (2) a comically-small rabbit ears antenna that receives about 90 channels, including all 4 major network affiliates that I might want to watch during a weather emergency (I am in Houston, the West Gray area, in a 2nd floor apartment).

But anyway, in addition to the tuner, you need to install the free PadTV HD app from the Google Play store, and my experience was smooth. I installed the software first, then plugged in the tuner, and the app woke up and asked me to associate it with the tuner, pick my country, scan for channels, and boom, I'm watching live TV on my phone.

Now, as to whether this $25 dongle, my phone, and some power banks can get me through a prolonged power outage? I think probably so! For testing purposes, I put my 2021 Moto G Power phone into airplane mode, dimmed the display, and started the tuner. With those settings it drains the battery at a rate of about 10% an hour. So with my brand-new, beefy-battery phone, fully-charged and doing nothing but running the TV tuner, it looks like I could get about 10 hours of usage. I also bought an adapter so I could use it with my older phones that are otherwise just sitting in a drawer (search for "USB-C to micro-USB adapter", and, IMPORTANT! it also needs to be "OTG" compatible). With my 2018-ish Moto E5 Cruise, airplane mode and dimmed display, it ran for 3 hours. With my 2013-ish Nexus 5 - 1.5 hours.

Finally, the description up yonder says "Rewind & Fast Forward Live TV Shows w/Time-Shift Recording" but I haven't found that functionality in the app. There is a "record" button, but I have not been able to successfully record and playback whatever program I am watching on my phone. So if you are hoping to turn your phone or tablet into a DVR, I can't report any success in doing that. But if you just want the ability to watch live over-the-air TV on your Android device, this tuner, app, and comically-small rabbit ears antenna has exceeded my expectations.

Edit 3/15/2022 -- The comically-small rabbit ears antenna that comes with this tuner has now replaced the big, clunky death-ray antenna that was previously the only antenna I had found that would receive all the local broadcast channels on my TV in an inner-loop Houston apartment. (Here's my glowing review of that antenna from a couple of years ago: https://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/R3IKFYZRYS7XZW?ref=pf_ov_at_pdctrvw_srp) ... the comically-small antenna requires TWO, yes, TWO adapters before it can mate it to my TV's antenna input (approx $11 bucks), but it's totally worth it.

title: Breaking the Rules
text:
[[VIDEOID:cf8b8e68de00e0f735b503cbbe2ea5dd]] I had been using a powerful stereo system to amplify my flat screen TV sound and about a year ago it died. I decided to replace it with a sound bar. Because I am a senior citizen, I am on a fixed budget and am somewhat hearing impaired. Everything I read said I needed a lot of power for the 700 sq. ft. room I was putting it in. So I tried several different brands from Amazon and finally kept a 100w sound bar, that put out 105db, with DSP technology (for my hearing) for under $80. It was much better than my TV speakers but I did need to make it fairly loud to hear it clearly.

This Bestisan sound bar was a good price with a coupon and I decided to try it for my bedroom TV. First I tested it with music. It easily connected with Bluetooth and the music sounded fine. Then I connected it to my main TV to compare it with the sound bar I already had and I was blown away. The DSP technology made the spoken words crisp and chrystal clear even when there was music playing in the background on the show. I can even understand the words when the actors are whispering and I sit 16 feet from the TV. Even though the Bestisan sound bar puts out 95db and is half the size of my old sound bar, it is far better. I don't need to blast it to hear the dialog. Needless to say, I have replaced my old sound bar with the Bestisan on my main TV.

title: Not bad, but...
text:
So the product title is "AINOYA 4 Pack Screen Protector for Apple AirTag with 2 Pack Case, Soft TPU Cases Holder with Keychain and Compatible with AirTag". I scooped it up thinking what a deal for 4 cases! Well, it's 4 screen protector and 2 cases, right there in the title and I felt like a complete moron for misreading it, even worse, when I opened the package I spend a good minute looking to see if 2 of the cases fell out some place. I'm not reducing my rating based on this because it is clearly user error, but some retooling of the title might be in order.
The product isn't bad. It feels solid. The material is a stiff plastic/TPU feel and fits the AirTag perfectly. It does not feel like it will fall out. I bought them because they look neater/nicer than the cases that cover 1 side, in my opinion. My only issue is that even with the many wonderful tools provided in the package to help apply the surface protector (why are you calling it screen protector?), it still doesn't really apply cleanly, but that may be on me. I expect it to fall off rather quickly and for the device to get scratches, but I don't care too much, as long as it continues to work the way it should. The other downside is that this kind of material tends to break eventually so we'll see how much life I get out of it. Assuming none of that happens short term, initial impressions are good so far and I would recommend this product.

title: No q-flash. Bios don't work with Ryzen 5000 series out of the box. Headache

It HEAVILY implies that this motherboard has q-flash when it doesn't, why else on god's earth would someone put that in the description for buying this. I knew it was a problem when i bought it and i simply thought that the motherboard had the solution built in with a q-flash feature, WHY ELSE WOULD IT BE IN THE DESCRIPTION OF THE PRODUCT???. I cannot believe i now have to wait for AMD to reply and supply them with loads of information just to have to wait days for their CPU to arrive, have to disassemble my whole PC, update it, reassemble, and then ship the CPU back just because of one little piece of misinformation. I would have never bought the board if i had the slightest idea that it would ever have been this hard.

If you are building a PC from scratch and don't have a 3000 series or less AM4 socket chips laying around (like most people) then stay VERY far away from this board.

First off, the construction is SOLID. I'm used to spending $200+ on something of this caliber years ago. Now a days we can sturdy tripods for "throwaway" prices. But I will not be throwing this one away any time soon! It has some weight to it, enough to make it stand straight for long hours but not enough to make it heavy on my back while I move around.

This is also my first tripod monopod COMBO. Before I would collapse the tripod legs down enough to mimic a monopod OR I'd have a separate pole. Having this 2 in 1 has eliminated yet another piece of gear to carry around. I'm able to "swap" to monopod mode within a minute and move with good flexibility. The bolts and screws are strong.

I have done a dozen or so outdoor photo sessions, each taking a few hours. This tripod has treated me well and has been beyond versatile for my needs and the best thing I've added to my gear recently.

If you're in the market for a new tripod with the added benefit of being a monopod too, this one gets my vote and I'm glad I chose wisely!

title: Bluetooth Constantly Loses Connection
text:
UPDATE: I changed my review to one star because the left ear speaker has stopped working less than two months after I purchased them and the seller won’t take returns after one month. This product is a huge dud! DO NOT BUY!

I can’t sleep with total silence. My wife can’t sleep with noise. So a compromise is a comfortable pair of Bluetooth headphones for me at night. I’ve owned many pair and they always eventually break after a year of use. So during my most recent hunt for Bluetooth headphones that are comfortable enough to sleep in (especially on my side with my ear to my pillow) I found this product. A secondary need was battery life long enough to last through the night. This product ended up meeting both needs. The bud that goes into my ears is very soft. And the battery seems to last for several days between charging. That’s very good.

However, these earphones disconnect from my Apple TV very frequently. If I just pause for a second they disconnect. If I move my head around they disconnect. Sometimes I do nothing at all and the disconnect the instant they connect. I’ve never had a problem before with staying connected with other brands of Bluetooth headphones. So it’s definitely this model. And that really sucks. Because I do want to like them.

Also, just recently I noticed the battery pack has separated from the metal wire that goes around my neck and is just hanging with wires exposed. I just got them about a month ago. So the design is a bit flimsy.

Overall I think these are very comfortable and they have great battery life. But the constant disconnections and the flimsy construction means I cannot recommend them to anyone. And my search for a decent pair of Bluetooth headphones continues.

title: Expected BETTER....
text:
Ok...What to say? I took the plunge on these not being well versed in ear buds. Here are my thoughts.
1) SOUND-I do like the sound from them. It's definitely by far the best from the ear buds I have personally tried. Music, talk sound good and to my liking. For me, it all sounds bold and crisp.
2) I have not delved deep into them so far. I'll add more at a later date, but it seems as if there are adjustments I can make for my personal taste. Adjustments are nice.
3) NOISE CANCELLATION-The ANC....I feel like there is something going on. It doesn't sound much different than when I turn it off. I don't have much experience. But in fairness, I don't hear back round distraction noise as much....so obviously something is happening with a positive effect.
4) FIT- They fit in my ears great....after changing the cups/ear pieces. I wish more were included. I'm nervous about needing more in the future. I hope other ones fit. Amazon, are you going to have them available for us?
5) CASE- LAME. The lid on mine is loose feeling. Too easy to open. So much so that I don't feel good about it in my pants pocket. Putting the ear buds in is not intuitive. Not natural at all. Trying to get them out is AWFUL for me. Like literally trying to pull them out with your fingers isn't easy. They are slick to grab and there isn't space to firmly grab them with your fingers. Poorly done. Case size is just ok. The texture is slick... definitely too easy to drop.
6) BATTERY- I'm baffled by this. The case takes forever to charge in my mind. The ear buds NEVER get to 100% charged for me. Both hover around 97 to 98. Why? Also, the right ear bud is always 10% lower in charge after extended wear. Why? Just give me a reason. After 2.5 hours if yard work, the left is at 67 and the right is 55....WHY?
7) THE ALEXA PART- So far , it's amusing. I don't do Alexa products. My use of it with these is ok. It's kinda cool. A little helpful. I'll have to experiment more with it.
OVERALL- A perfectly fine item that I enjoy and also dislike. Good sound combined with a bad case and odd power usage. Features that kinda work and some that I don't care about. Yes....I think these are the best buds I have personally tried. But I'm not happy in general. I think I'll keep them because I think they are ok as a value for the introductory price I got them at...$99. I wouldn't pay any more for them. If I want to spend more, I'll definitely move on from these. You did OK Amazon. I expected better.

Following, what I thought to be, extensive research I purchased the SIMOLIO head phones for the wife. Right on schedule they arrived and I immediately realized my extensive research wasn't worth a damn - I had overlooked the fact that they were NOT blutooth. Setting that aside, I opened the box to find a very well constructed head set that fit over, not on the ear. Everything was in the box, no missing parts!! I installed the system, based on easy to follow instructions, without the slightest problem (my TV is a 2019 SAMSUNG). So far I couldn't ask for more but remember these were my last resort for providing my wife some TV watching enjoyment. She tried on the head set as I waited with baited breath and to my surprise a large smile came over her face - NO DISCOMFORT from the head set. Following some quick simple instructions from me on operation she now really enjoys watching TV and possibly even better  I too can as well with volume at 25/30 not the hearing destroying 100 levels. My last word on this, if you are in the same situation I was,  give it a try - nothing to lose with Amazon's easy return policy.

title: Simply Incredible for the money
text:
I've owned IEMs for years. I was a DJ back when people actually ran radio stations (I'm talking late 90s, In college), a sound engineer, recording engineer, and I've been a serious audiophile since I first laid ears on a Carver Silver 9t screaming through some Snell Bs in the early 90s....

These. Things. Are. Incredible.

I'm running them though a Bryston BHA-1 on my main system, a Woo/AE-9 on my PC, and a Sony 507 when I'm on the move. They legitimately tear apart everything up to the Sony Z1Rs. They're comfier than the Z1Rs, too. And, honestly, add in the drone of a jet engine, my furnace running, my dog walking around, a breeze, anything, and I think that $1,500 delta feels better in my pocket than the exceptionally slight difference in sound quality. Plus, if you're on said plane, and accidentally drop/leave them, it's not the end of the world.

Really. If you're in the market for anything less than $1k, buy these first. Take the rest of the money, and do anything else with it. There is very little to no color (perhaps a very slight mid-bass bloom, very, very slight), they're detailed, crisp, clear and really well built. The cord is the weakest part, and honestly, it's still nicer than what comes with UEs (Pre-logitech, like everything else Logi touches, they killed UEs.)

Buy them. You won't regret it.

title: Good Support -- Nice Little Panel with Cloud Support
text:
I mostly can report on this as end user, as I did not install nor manage this at the top level on a routine basis. The panel is nice in appearance, has a touchscreen that works well, and allows both key fob access and entering a PIN number to unlock the door.

A nice feature is you can issue PIN unlock numbers to individuals that are time locked/bound, say for a visiting relative, or somewhat permanent, for a UPS or Postal worker to gain access to the common area of your building and leave packages in a secure area rather than outside. Each individual has their own PIN code.

The mobile application, which needs a little work in its UI but is completely functional, allows you to issue the PINs I described to your guests, has a long of all transactions that have occurred under your account, and additionally allows a two-way video chat with whoever has rung your unit number using the touch screen.

Because it is cloud-integrated, you can perform all of these functions while on the go, including the video chat or just unlocking the door remotely if you don't want to go the PIN route. This is also handy to let yourself in if you've gone out and forgotten your keys.

From a building manager perspective, which is above my pay grade, you can assign a subset of panel functions like PIN generation down to each tenant with access lists, allowing you to remove or add accounts as folks come and go in the rentals and give them access to the doors managed that are appropriate for their needs.

Integrates with a standard key access door release mechanism. Also has a proximity RFID reader for the aforementioned key fobs or RFID cards.

I have had on a few occasions reason to contact support, and they have been very responsive and helpful, and have not put helping me behind a wall of support entitlement paperwork before they speak to me, which is uncommon these days and very much appreciated, which is why I give the unit such high regards in my review.

title: Great audio, useless noise cancellation, not compatible with iOS.
text:
So, I got these earbuds after watching a review where the reviewer shared the mic quality of the earbuds. people talked about the audio quality and such, and they were cheap. When I received them, they worked great with my aging android phone and Windows PC. The noise cancellation is virtually useless, but that wasn't a major issue for me.

My main issue was that when I upgraded to an iPhone, the absolute lowest volume level started around 60-65db. Which was uncomfortable for me. Apparently it is a bug that became a feature of iOS. Cause of Apple tax. There were no apps that helped lower the volume. There is no official app for the earbuds, just one from some sketchy guy.
I'm determined to keep trying iOS, but miss the openness of Android. I wanted people to be aware of this issue. Apple intentionally sabotages the usefulness of other manufacturer's products so that people will buy their over priced products.

Bottom line, what do I think of these earbuds? Honestly, I think that they are better than some earbuds that cost much more. The audio quality is really good. I haven't tested the mic myself, but I assume it is as good as the one the reviewer shared. The noise cancelling doesn't seem to do much, though maybe I didn't use the right sized ear pieces. Despite that, I think these are good earbuds for what you pay for them.
They don't have wireless charging or pairing through NFC, but that isn't really a major issue. I didn't really expect it. These are quality, low cost earbuds. Unfortunately, they don't work well with my new phone and the best option is more than I can afford right now.

I rated the earbuds lower than I consider them in the hope that someone could avoid the issue that I ran into. If you want to use these with your Android device or Windows PC then I'd consider these 4.5 star wireless earbuds. For iOS, save up for something owned by Apple or just avoid Apple all together. They just don't care about anything not owned by Apple.
I hope that the company develops an app to fix this issue, but I don't expect it. Anyways, I hope this review is helpful.

Update 1/8/22:
I bought a Beats Flex set for around $50, which works well with my iPhone. The brand is owned by Apple, so it makes sense. If you’re looking for something low cost that works with an iPhone then Beats is a good, low cost option.
They don’t really have as many features as several of the other earbuds, but they work. Just don’t get them wet since they aren’t resistant to liquids, unlike many of the third party earbuds in that price range. Apparently Apple can only compete by hobbling third party manufacturers.

I stand by my earlier assessment of the SoundPEATS earbuds. They are an excellent option for everyone else. Their audio quality is on par with the Beats earbuds. So, if you are looking for budget wireless earbuds, look no further.
That said, if you can afford it, go up around $20 and get something with some amount of water resistance.

title: What an android tablet should be.
text:
I purchased this unit to replace a Galaxy Tab S6. Believe me, it is worth the upgrade. The size is helpful. Samsung is putting the effort into making a tablet that is a pleasure to use. I have the keyboard case. The improvements in the keyboard are noticable. The keyboard is a true keyboard. I also use DeX exclusively. Samsung is doing a good job with this addition to the android O/S. One of the main unpleasant ordeals - there are many differences with a Tab S6. Most of them relate to the keyboard improvements as well as the larger screen. This screen is a spoiler. It will spoil you. Sharp, Clear, Bright, and Fast. To say nothing of the size. All in all this is the greatest Android device out there.

Just to update - I have now used this device for daily email, calendar, SMS, as well as other daily tasks for a couple months. I want to make a couple comments re: where does the Android Tablet find a place in todays marketplace. With phones becoming the answer to all needs, is there a need for a tablet? I think so. But for specific applications - I use a Samsung Galaxy S10 Plus for a phone. I use it as a hotspot for the S7+. Works for me. When I say tablets fit a particular place in the marketplace. If you want a one device does it all, the S7+ would be difficult to justify. The phone is too small for me to use as a one size fits all situation. However, the S7+ is capable of doing all my daily tasks. There are limitations, I have a Lenovo LTop which I have to drag out on occasions. This brings up the major issue with Android. With so many devices and Manufacturers and each mfgr responsible for updates to operating system, the lack of cross device compatibility is a problem. I need the Lenovo to print to my P-Touch printer. Brother says "Buy a new printer". Not a real answer. Just another part of the Android issue. In typing this review, another issue with Android - Cut and Paste works different depending on what app you are using. This is not a Tablet problem. It is a Google Problem. I think Samsung is doing what they can to make a great Android Tablet and a Great Operating System as well.

I am quite upset. I have purchased dozens of computers including Chromebooks without any problems. I ordered this based on reviews. The Chromebook looks beautiful and the screen is indeed fantastic. However, the first one I ordered had a broken camera. I suppose this can happen but I have not heard of this before. So, I packaged it up and returned it to exchange for exactly the same model since I liked the form factor. Amazon is extremely good at returns and I had a new replacement 3 days later.

I just unpacked the new one, turned it on and tried to log into Google. As I typed in my password the field truncated, turned red, and said I had the wrong password. I tried again. The field always failed. By trial and error I found that the "i" key on the keyboard would send a set of 5 characters instead of an "i" and the log in would fail.

Two brand new Chromebooks right out of the box with quality control issues and failed components.

I do not trust getting another and Lenovo is now on my blacklist. I have always had solid Lenovo products in the past. This Chromebook, however, has a great design but poor quality control at the assembly plant. I do not recommend that you purchase this model.

text:

Bose microphone is tad better for phone calls.

Bose offers a full body protection case. Supports 2.5mm / 3.5mm.

Bose has USB-C which is ubiquitous.

Bose works with both Apple and Android ecosystems without losing any functionality.

Bose is lighter.

Bose is about $250 cheaper!

Where Apple AirPods Max shine - fit for larger ears is better than Bose. Overall build quality is more premium.

I’ll say that if AirPods Max frequency response curve were more like Bose’s, I’d have definitely kept them as my second pair for Apple ecosystem and used Bose on the go. But the mid high dip is very noticeable.

title: Slim, works well
text:
I bought this for my Surface GO tablet, as the original Micro*oft keyboard died way too early-- likely from a failure of the ribbon cable feeding the keyboard/mouse. Since my primary use for the GO is to read Ebooks? I really missed using the right-arrow key to advance to the next page. Since the Kindle app is so twitchy, and poorly written user interface? Using the keyboard is a must. I was going to get a 3rd party replacement keyboard cover, but I saw this little inexpensive bluetooth keypad instead. I have a nice heavy canvas carry cover for the GO anyway. I had tested a USB keypad, and it worked beautifully to advance pages: hit the 6 key to go forward, the 4 key to go back, and so on. Some folk may not realize, that a numeric keypad can double as a cursor array, including page up, page down, end, home and the 4 arrow directional keys too. The Kindle app recognized the 6 as being forward, which frankly surprised me (as I said, the app is horrible for PC... if I did not have 1000+ kindle books already?)

Anyway, this little bluetooth arrived, and paring took seconds-- a nice blue light indicated it was paired. I like not having a bulky USB cord+adapter (the GO only has usb C). Furthermore? It is both rechargeable and has an on/off switch to power down during transport. I've not recharged it since the initial charge, and it is going strong. Flip the power switch to on, the blue light blinks, the goes steady, then goes out-- connected. Hit the 6 key to advance pages in Kindle app.

My only complaint, is that all the keys are identical in feel: so I put a small drop of simple glue in the center of the 6 key, for a tactile location for my fingers. Fixed.

I'd buy another in a minute, if I lose this one, especially it's less than $20.

title: Mobile app 2/10, Hardware 8/10, Fun with Buddies 10/10
text:
Patience. Once you set the headset up, the features and sound quality of the 50R make it a pretty nice experience to have when riding.

The audio quality is excellent, for music and mesh connected riders, BUT - Setting it up is a pain if you’re exclusively using the mobile app... (the ratings in the Apple store are pretty accurate in this regard). My recommendation is to download the desktop application. Using the mobile app and the included wifi adapter is not an intuitive process. I work with technology and tried watching the online video and app instructions first, and the desktop app is MUCH easier. After you download the desktop app, start by attaching the earphones so that you can hear the audible indicators as you work through the setup. After you attach the earphones, power the unit on and attach it to your computer with the included USB cable. The first task will be to update to the latest version of the system software for the SENA unit. While the update is taking place, go ahead and install the app on your mobile phone. You will need to use it to control the units features and functions. Do NOT try to pair with your phone until after the software update for the unit completes.

Installation of the unit on the helmet is easy enough. I opted to use the included clip and Velcro tape which secures the device very firmly in place.

Finding the different buttons while gloved can be challenging at times, especially with thicker gloves on, but I expect it to get easier with practice. I have not yet purposely tried to use the voice commands but have inadvertently started calling people I had no intention of contacting when voice commands activated by mistake.

title: Check the pins that hold the legs
Needs to be flush with monitor screen
text: I bought this product to apply to an HP All-in-One desktop to reduce glare. It has virtually no bezel and I was hesitant about putting tape directly on the screen, so I tried Method 2 first. I found that this method left the filter about a millimeter or so away from the surface of the monitor, and this was enough to cause some distortion of text.  It was quite uncomfortable to read. So, I removed all the clear plastic holders and tried Method 1. This enabled the filter to fit flush with the screen and text reading was much improved, though there was still some slight distortion. I was able to compensate for that by enlarging the font. Method 1 would probably have worked if I'd applied the tape completely on the screen rather than partially on the bevel. Fortunately, enough tape is supplied to make it possible to experiment, and it comes off easily enough. I didn't need the privacy function, but it does work amazingly well for that purpose. All in all, it's a good, well-made product that is easy to install. Four stars only because of the text distortion, but perhaps that's unavoidable.

title: Works! Can deliver 0.75 A @ 12V, but only if your 5V supply is adequate
text: Not every power supply lives up to the spec, but this one does. I tested at 0.75 A load and it delivered 12.03 V at 0.75 A, from an input of 5.0 V at 2.29 A.  This was using a bench power supply.  Since not every USB port can deliver that much current, it is reasonable to specify 0.7 A as the output limit.  It can actually go up to 1.0 A output while drawing 2.69 A from 5V, but the output voltage sagged to 10.3 V and it started getting hot.  It is 82% efficient at 0.5 A output.  However, at a light load of 70 mA (12.49 V out) it still draws 0.25 A from 5V, so it has 69% efficiency at that load current.

This morning one of the extension tubes simply slipped out of the leg. I tried to reassemble the tube, but found that the locking mechanism no longer worked and it now slides freely in and out. I've tried flipping locking sleeve in several different directions, but it makes no difference. At this point I have to assume that some other part slipped out with the leg and is lost. At this point, this brand-new tripod is useless.

I've spent more time fooling with problems with this tripod that I have actually using it. I'll be contacting support and very likely returning the tripod. I do not recommend it.

Update: the manufacturer has contacted me and offered to compensate me for the defective tripod. I appreciate this, so once this is complete I will update my comment and my rating.

title: IT WORKS!!!  OMG IT WORKS!!!
text:
This is EXACTLY what I needed and it works perfectly and was super easy to set up. My old laptop, a 15 inch retina MacBook Pro that I bought in July 2012 finally died last week. I was watching a YouTube video and the screen just went black and it wouldn't turn back on. I tried everything within my power (well, with google and YouTube at my disposal of course) like booting in Safe Mode, in Recovery Mode, in Transfer File mode or whatever it's called, and nothing worked. I'm way out of the Apple Care warranty, and a local Mac repair shop wanted $70 just to look at it, then anything else they did would be extra. As far as I can tell it's not a software issue but a hardware one, and even a used logic board is like $260 and I'd have to do the install myself. I'm long overdue for an upgrade, but I kept using this computer because it just kept going, but it's not worth putting a bunch of money into it at this point. There were a few gigs of stuff I wanted from the hard drive though (most stuff is backed up to an external drive and the cloud but not everything), so I wondered if there was a way to turn a laptop hard drive into an external drive that I could extract data from, like a USB stick or something. And it turns out you can! And this adapter is exactly what I needed. (By the way the website/YouTube channel Apple Dollars was super helpful to me in this process, check it out!). I already had one of the special screwdrivers to get the hard drive out, which was actually really easy. And once this was delivered it took like 2 minutes to plug the drive into this adapter, then plug the adapter into my Mac mini desktop, and I got all the data I needed! This adapter has 2 usb plugs, I gather you have to plug both in for the extra power to actually get your old hard drive to wake up or whatever. Anyway, I'm not a computer expert but I'm not afraid to open up the laptop and try stuff, and this worked perfectly. And for like $19 it's totally worth it. There are a ton of adapters like this one depending on the type and year of your laptop, so if this isn't exactly the one you need keep searching! Totally worth it and now I have a 256GB external drive to play around with.

The actual adapter was mislabeled, it says 8 + 18 pin on it (you can see that in the pic) and before I plugged in my hard drive it said "For MacBook Air only" on it. But I have a MacBook Pro, not air. But it must have been incorrectly labeled or something because it totally worked for my MBP, which is a proprietary 7+17 pin type (or 24 pin). Anyway, I almost went to Amazon immediately to request a return, but then I put the hard drive on top of the adapter and it looked like it would fit, and I tried and voila! It worked! So just be careful. The outside packaging is labeled right, just not the actual adapter, but I don't care. This saved me a ton of money and I got all my data so I'm 100% happy.

And I don't get anything for writing this review by the way. I bought this for full price because I needed it and I'm thrilled that such a product exists and worked so easily. I'm just trying to be helpful and use my decent reviewer number to try and provide reliable, honest reviews.

Again, check out apple dollars (dot com), click on Troubleshooting and then Data Recovery. No, I don't work for them lol. That site/YouTube video was just totally instrumental in my process so I thought I'd pass it along.

title: Great TV - when not bugging out and needing restarted
text:
I finally upgraded a 10 year old 1080p TV to get into the 4K game, using this primarily for TV viewing with some causal PS5 gaming mixed in.
The picture is great, cannot complain about that aspect at all. Looks great on 4k content on Netflix, Amazon, or even over the air sports. I'm a pretty casual gamer so not sure i'd even notice the 'lag' or whatever people are on about when it comes to gaming TVs, seems to be perfectly responsive enough for me. Sound seems decent, I've debated hooking it up to my stereo system but so far it hasn't even been necessary. Surround sound isn't really all that important to me.
The reason this TV is not getting a higher rating is because i've had several buggy issues with it, almost since the first week of use. On a couple of occasions Netflix 4K or Dolby atmos shows just would not load, no matter what you did and yes, with a perfectly fast internet connection. Apparently it's some sort of memory issue with this TV that required it to be unplugged and restarted - which fixed the issue. I had also been using the NBA league pass app on the Roku menu and that would crash and restart the TV over 50% of the time trying to watch a game. Not sure if that is the fault of TCL, Roku or the NBA app (probably NBA app in this case because it's absolute crap on nearly every platform i've ever used it on.
Other bugs that have occurred include a totally black screen but with sound if you're using the remote, so the picture is just out. Like the previous problem, this is also fixed by unplugging the TV for a few seconds and then plugging it back in. Just recently I had an issue where the sound was totally out of whack. While 12-15 is the normal volume that I would listen at, it was just barely audible at that point and needed cranked all the way up. Obviously a glitch, I unplugged and restarted the TV and it was corrected. I probably need to unplug and restart this TV about once every week or two to address one of the above mentioned issues. Not sure if these are Roku or TCL issues, but they seem to be deflecting the blame when you try to contact them about the issues. If restarts were required any more frequently than currently I would probably return it, but when it's working it's a great picture and value for the price. J

title: Great product if you have some experience buildinging.
text: So..if you aren't use to big boy coolers and your case cannot handle this, it is probably not for you.  This is my 12th computer build, and the second build into my corsair 900 obsidian series case (although after this build I would probably go to a 680 or something, there are some serious annoyances to the 900 that I didn't realize at the last build).  Comparing this to noctua d15, there some things that make it better (width), but overall I preferred the Noctua. The biggest flaw of all in the design is that the heat pipes *are* the interface for the die cap heat spreader.  These are infamously not flat...I was unsure what to believe, but I didn't want to fry my processor so I lapped the surface sequentially from 800-7000 grit and boy was I shocked how uneven that interface is, see the pictures, if it were flat the whole contact would be copper.  However, after doing this and seating with pk-3...my 3950 is running 39-45 idle to load, which is pretty much what my 1800 was running with the Noctua.  Very pleased with this product, but I drop a star because this is not fire and forget, plug and play, or whatever you want to call it.  I think it will be quite a good product for experienced users.  Other thoughts, the width of this is a couple mm narrower than with the Noctua which forced me to use this with the asus board, since the cpu placement is rather close to the first pciex16 slot.  Keep this in mind if you are building and want a boss hog cooler on your CPU, you may need to drop your gpu down to the second slot.  Usually not as much of an issue any more because high end boards come with several pcie16 and no one is crossfiring anymore legitimately I would hope (since it isn't efficient). I had to use the first slot because I wanted to use a heat sink on my NVMe drive.  These aren't deal breakers, but nevertheless something to plan for.

title: Ignore the bad reviews it works great.
text:
I've been interested in astronomy for a long long time. I have owned about 30 telescopes, but currently a 10" and 16" dobsonian, and an SN6 . I've always wanted a decent little cheap planetarium. In the past I painted glow in the dark dots on the ceiling, different sizes for magnitude differences, using a huge paper template to get the star positions correct. It works fine but it's a lot of work, and the sky doesn't change.

Then I saw this Homestar, and did some comparisons between this version and the new version. In every review I felt the new version was TOO bright. It does not accurately represent what a night sky looks like. For this reason I purchased the original version. The original version is also a bit too bright, but acceptable. Another reviewer mentioned that the stars do not revolve around the pole star (Polaris) but that is wrong. The sky does indeed rotate around polaris. This is neat because on my ceiling polaris is (correctly) in the same place all the time, just off to the edge of the ceiling. This means that the sky completely changes over the course of 30 minutes or so.

I still feel this device is extremely overpriced for what it is, but I suppose that has to do with the limited demand, and cost of manufacturing the laser disks.

The shooting star effect is pretty good even though it's always in the same place. It's spaced out timing wise, and the sky has rotated a bit by then so it does not get repetetive.

Overall I am really happy with this. My wife lost her mom about a week ago due to covid. I was going out to a friend's house for awhile and knew she would go to bed early.

I had just received the homestar and secretly set it up for her but left the room lights on so she couldn't notice. When she turned off the lights to go to bed she was rewarded with a star lit sky. I received a text which only said "thank you <3"

In the morning she told me she was so delighted that it made her cry.

Now we run it every night when we go to bed.

BTW, even if you do not set the timer, it turns itself off after a few hours. I'm not sure how long that is yet because I'm usually asleep when that happens.

BTW the other night I played "space music" really faint to add to the theme. I had already fallen asleep when my wife came to bed. She woke me up and said she keeps hearing UFOs taking off outside. Apparently she had been looking out the window for awhile before waking me.

That was pretty funny! I just love her

title: Almost perfect, but….
text:
[[VIDEOID:63d4ac0184ea2edd47907208b794948a]] This bag is almost perfect.

First, the good. It’s very well made. There’s no loose stitching on the “leather”, the metal feels high quality, the zippers feel sturdy, and the outside material is soft. I love the clasps. They feel very secure.

Now the bad, The first complaint is that the straps are way too long. I understand they did this so you can carry it as a messenger bag too, but they really should’ve just included one long strap and two shorter ones. On the smallest hole these were 32 inches long. I had to poke new holes, and now I have extra strap hanging down that I don’t really know what to do about.

The second problem is the D-ring you attach the straps to so you can wear as a backpack. When you add the length of the ring plus the clips it makes the bag sit at an odd angle while on the back. It creates this huge gap and looks like you’re wearing a messenger bag on the back. I notice now they only show one picture of the bag on the back, and not even in the original listing. In the picture she has her hand on the strap, and I assume she’s holding it up. However, attaching the clips to the briefcase handle completely fixed this problem.

It seems a lot smaller than they show in the video on the listing. This isn’t really an issue for me personally, but I just thought others might want to know. My laptop is significantly more slim than the one in the video. I also put in a book that’s thinner than that one in the video and a small kindle paper white. I’m already almost out of room. After I put in my laptop charger and a spiral notebook that’ll be it. I bought the (15.6 inch size). Also, it’s a hair difficult to get my laptop in. It is a 15.6 inch, and I have to really make sure I’m putting it straight down and flat against the back of the bag. The sides are curved inwards towards the bag, and that’s the only way it’ll fit. However, the front pocket fits my large happy planner no problem.

Once the laptop is in the padded compartment it’s near impossible to put anything in or get anything out of the zipper pocket as the material of the bag doesn’t stretch. I attached a video of me showing what I mean by this, as well as showing how much room I have left. (I have very small hands, so not much room at all) As you can see in the video I have to undo the Velcro of the padded compartment to access the zipper and I can barely get my hand in and out. If you put the laptop in the big compartment you can’t utilize the pen compartment or fabric pockets, so you really just have to pick which one you can’t use.

All in all though, it isn’t a horrible product. It’s great for my needs, but if you need to carry more things like a Bluetooth mouse or headphones be aware those things might not fit. If you don’t need as much space it’s a pretty small modification to make the straps work out. Just a quick poke with an awl or even a small screwdriver. I might add some little gold feet as well so it doesn’t sit directly on the floor during class.

EDIT: This bag is SO HEAVY. My back is hurting so bad, and I only have a laptop in there now. As far as laptops go mine is fairly lightweight. Even without anything in it the bag is a heavy weight material.

The stitching around the D-ring is coming undone. I had to put the straps back on it because with the straps on the handle the D-ring rubbed on my spine in a really uncomfortable way.

I’ve used the bag for about 2 weeks, and now there are indents in the bag from leaning against my desk, and they won’t come out. This bag definitely isn’t going to hold up, and I’m so disappointed.

I want to love this bag. It is so cute. But it’s already coming apart, and the weight makes it impractical for everyday use.

title: Used this monoscope for firing range and distance work... needs a well weighted tripod
text:
ITEM: Lincredible 12x50 Monocular Telescope

SUMMARY:
With the upgraded optics of BAK4 , this small spotting scope, as I’ve found, is a really nice add-on to my field optics gear. As a spotting scope at the range, it provides a fixed and steady image of the target. And that’s helpful as from a distance, I can’t always see the fine line placement of my shot. I also used this for our recent July 4th fireworks, viewed from our Uncle’s balcony over-looking the valley area below their property. The 12x power view was enough to clarify locations for the various celebrations below.

I’ve not been a fan of either the smartphone optics adapter for recording, nor the very light weight tripod. When I do use this scope for spotting or viewing, I use either my larger mobile tripod I keep in my vehicle, or one of my few high-quality and weight mini-tripods. I found stability in the tripod was essential for a steady view either on the range or when trying to find something in the distance. Steady pan controls are also essential. And both my large and Hi-Q mini-tripods are weighted and dampened in their pan and tilt. That makes this a worthwhile monoscope.

I bought this projector (Xgimi Horizon Pro 4k) because it was supposed to have 3D support with the new firmware. It shows two images when you try to play a 3D DVD. Edit--3D works great just have to figure out the menu to use.
There is light beyond the picture which is projected to the ceiling which may be fixable if you could get some support. Edit--The light is not a concern once the Keystone adjustment is done. Tried the online chat thing and that wasn't working. Called the phone and no answer.
Seems like they are selling a ton of these, but haven't gotten the support thing figured out yet.
On the bright side, I am projecting on a dark red wall and the picture is quite good, I will be painting a screen on the wall when the screen paint arrives. The contrast is also good, at least on a red wall. Hopefully a bright white wall will make it even better.
All the connections are working, BT, Wifi, HDMI, haven't tried the USB yet.
Sound is great. Fan is fairly quiet.
If they can get the support going this thing will dominate it's price point.
XGIMI I want you to succeed, please get some customer support. You have to do something other than just answer AMAZON reviews occasionally.
Update
Still no support.
Painted a 180 inch screen on my basement (man-cave) wall. Big improvement on color and picture quality. Contrast does seem a bit low compared to my LED Samsung, but that is to be expected I guess.
Everything runs great on Android TV. The BT seems a bit glitchy, audio not as smooth as every other BT audio device I use.
Every time I turn it on I have to adjust keystone setting, I just turned off the auto keystone and never have to adjust it again.
The speakers are really good.
Plugged into my home Cat6 network fixed the BT problem, so have a good connection for smooth BT.
Found lots of info on the Xgimi Tech FB page. Good alternative to XGIMI Support.
