title: This projector is incredible
text:
I bought this during quarantine because I missed going to the movie theater and it was the best decision I've ever made!

The picture quality and brightness are amazing. I have an older projector of similar lumens and it's completely drowned out by a single light. This thing I can use with multiple lights on (Hue lights in a warm setting at around 40-50% brightness) and it still looks incredible. This more has to do with the contrast ration, I assume, because this projector has super dark blacks and bright vivid color.

The sound was okay, but unusable at lower volumes because of the loudness of the fan. I don't find the fan particularly loud or distracting, it sounds like any other projector. It can definitely heat up a small room, but it's a lot less hot than some other projectors I've had.

I opted to up my experience by getting Bose soundbar and luckily, instead of having to deal with hiding cords, this thing works great with Bluetooth. I have little to no latency issues. The latency issue is almost always on Netflix and I haven't had too much trouble with any other streaming service. It's fixed pretty easily by just pausing, rewinding a second or two and then pressing play.

The Android TV is awesome, but configuring your home screen is a little less awesome. It's a bit complicated and clunky to download each streaming service and upon start up, it takes about 15-20 seconds to recognize that I'm pressing buttons on the remote to get to my streaming service of choice. I had a ton of issues with Wifi connection that plagued me for the first month and still comes up sometimes. It just won't connect to my Wifi. I have a Velop mesh network, any and every other product I've had has never had connection issues. It says there was an error connecting, but I have super fast Wifi and I have a Velop in the same room as the projector. I have to try again and again for 10 minutes, sometimes it connects, other times I have to turn it off, wait for it turn back on, then deal with it not connecting another 1-3 times. I haven't had that issue as of late, but it happens every now and then. Also, don't even bother downloading the Hulu app, it won't work. It has a crazy amount of lag and nothing can fix it. The only way I can watch Hulu is through casting it from my phone. The Chromecast function works great and I love it.

I don't know how to put into words how much of a godsend the zoom feature is. It is the best thing ever.

TLDR: This is probably the best bang for your buck on lower budget home cinema projectors. (I say lower budget because this thing is still incredible expensive, but it is so worth it if you can't afford one of those $6000 cinema projectors). Get your own sound system, the built-in speakers are okay and unusable at low volume. The features are kickass but as with all technology, there are some flaws, like Wifi connectivity issues, occasional latency issues, slow start-up, and the Hulu app being unusable, but it more for makes up for it with the amount of features it has and the quality of the picture. The zoom feature is the best thing ever.

title: Do NOT buy if you use eARC / Soundbar!
text:
I will update this review if anything changes:

11/8/2021:
The TV looks great, however, I have HUGE issues with using my Soundbar with the TV. First, on default settings, I can't hear anything but clicking sounds -- my Soundbar acts as if the TV is constantly sending new types of audio out (like stereo, Dolby Digital, 5.1, etc) so it keeps resetting.

I was able to fix this by changing my Audio Settings "Digital output format" on the TV from "Auto" to "Passthrough" -- however, now if I try to play anything from a connected HDMI port, the audio has a significant LAG from what is being seen. (Test with Xbox One on HDMI 3, Soundbar on eARC HDMI) Not the end of the world, as I only need one input, so I now run that HDMI through the Soundbar directly and no issues there - however, this shouldn't even be an issue, and TCL needs to fix this.

Now, I've got other random issues when using the built-in Roku -- while the TV is in Passthrough, Netflix won't play any audio in 5.1 (I have to manually select the regular Stereo audio in order to hear anything, 5.1 is silent -- tested with She-Rah). Amazon Prime Video won't play any sound at all (Tested with House). Disney+ I can hear the menu scrolling sounds, but no audio on the actual videos (tested with Avengers End Game). Oddly, HBO & AppleTV work fine (tested with Dune & Foundation). Pandora also works (presumably b/c it only outputs stereo?).

NOTE: My prior TV, which had NONE of these issues, was TCL 55" S405 (2018). The TV I purchased is a TCL 55" R635. This should have been an upgrade, I don't understand why I'm having issues on the MORE EXPENSIVE, PREMIUM VERSION of the TV.

title: USB power feeds back to SDR, potentially destroying it
text:
If powered via USB, that power is fed back into the SDR unless you hack your own DC-blocking capacitor solution. I wondered why my SDRPlay's main graph kept jumping around, I believe it was tripping the ESR diode repeatedly. I hope it's not permanently damaged! Found an article online that noted this problem, and that you can fix it with a "high quality capacitor" on the RF line back to the SDR, but I haven't tried that yet (I'm not seasoned enough to know what capacitor would be appropriate, and can't find any info about it).

Note also that this requries too much power for the SDRPlay to provide it via bias t, so you MUST use the USB connection with that SDR. Very disappointed...

title: Doesn't work in cold weather
text:
I just contacted Ring Customer Support and was told that their products do not work in cold weather. I live in Minnesota and my doorbell completely died during the winter. This spring I brought it back into the house recharged it, did a hard reset, and nothing. THe good news is that they are sending me a new doorbell. The bad news is that I was told I would have the same problem next winter. Seeing as they don't have a disclaimer saying, "Does not work in cold weather climates" I asked for a refund. They declined. So in essence, if you live in a climate where the gets below freezing outside, their doorbells and cameras will not work. And this is according the Ring tech support.

UPDATED} I'm changing my review to one star instead of 2. A week ago I sent a detailed email to the Ring Support staff in the hopes of getting this to work. I have heard nothing back.

I've set up my three Echo Show 5's to immediately show my doorbell video when it detects any motion. But it very rarely works. Most of the time the Echo devices say "OK" and then it tries to connect and then says "something went wrong". And by the time it starts recording (which does not show up on the Echo Show) the person is already walking away from my door.

The doorbell is hardwired, is about 15 feet from a Wifi mesh point, and shows a signal strength of RSSI -44. The Doorbell's firmware is the latest version. My Internet package is measured at just pver 100Mbps.

Trying to set this doorbell up with an Echo show is about an 8 step process of creating and configuring 2 routines, "Start Recording on Motion" and "Stop Recording after x minutes" when there should just be an app for the Echo Show with a button letting you to turn "Start Recording on Motion Detection" on or off. But what you have to do is configure two "routines" for each Echo Show you want to connect. For me that was six 8-step routines.

Maybe some future updates will simplify this process and make it reliable but since Amazon owns Ring you would think that this would been one of the first things they setup for Echo Show. I would assume that, like myself, most people would think these two devices were made for each other and that they offer pure and simple compatibility. But not so.

title: I have other Cowon products that are perfect; these sound great but have issues
text:
My Cowon E7 are my go-to out of house headphones, so I was excited for the chance to try out Cowon's newest TWS earbuds.

Frankly, if I was not so enamored with the E7 and not used to the app controls of the two earbuds I typically use, Jabra Elite 85t and Airpod Pros (both more expensive than these) I would probably be more impressed than I am. These sound GREAT for music, very good for phone calls, but the real shortcoming for me is the ANC and the "transparency mode", the controls and the lack of an app to control the headset.

The good:
1. The sound for music is great.
2. The sound for phone calls is very good.
3. The charging case is unique as it has a USB-A output so another device can be charged via the case in an emergency.
4. The case shows the battery level of the case. Unfortunately, it does not display the battery levels of the earbuds.
5. There is good audio feedback to let you know that the Bluetooth is connected, that the ANC is on/off, etc.
6. They are comfortable and stay in with the included tips, the latter of which is odd for me. I use third-party tips with my Jabra and Airpods.
7. The earbuds can each work individually. Unlike many others that either need to pair or have one bud that can work alone, for these, either bud will work individually. If you are stressing on battery life, you can recharge one in the case while talking on the other.

The bad:
1. There is no app and thus no EQ settings at all. There is no way to customize the sound.
2. Everything is controlled by button presses. With a dozen-plus sets of wireless earbuds, I'll never remember what buttons to press, so it will be trial and error.
3. The manual is printed incredibly small. I was able to find a version of the manual on Cowon's website. Here it is http://dn2.cowon.com/data/C09/CK20ANC/CK20ANC_manual_1.0_ENG_web_210121.pdf.
4. The ANC functions poorly. This is a real disappointment.
5. I had trouble figuring out how to use the "transparency mode" and when I did, I learned that I could not distinguish any difference between "transparency mode" and "ANC off".
6. Other than a blue light on the earbuds to indicate they are fully charged, and an audible "battery low" there is no way to know the battery level - and no way to know if "battery low" is 20%, 5% or any other percentage.
7. The instructions claim 17 charges from the battery case; I recharged once and the case dropped from 100% to 70%.

Overall, these sound great for music, but that's with the ability to use my MP3 player's EQ settings; on an iPhone the settings are not as customizable - thus I'd prefer an app that lets me control this.

Cowon products have proven to me to be reliable.

Perhaps I'm grumbling too much at the comparison to devices that cost twice what these do; the sound quality is pretty much on par with all the devices mentioned, the biggest difference being control via app the ANC/pass through sound issues.

I will continue to look forward to and purchase new Cowon products.

Our goal was to play some Region 2 DVDs through our TV, which seemed fairly simple. The price was substantially cheaper than comparable models, so we took a shot. Twice. About 20 movies in, DVDs just stopped playing. You'd start up the player and see grey lines going across the screen. At first, we thought it was the movie. Then, we realized that all Region 1 DVDs continued to play just fine - it was only the Region 2 (AKA the reason we bought the player) ones that stopped. Needless to say, attempting to contact the company for a resolution is just as likely as winning the lottery, and Amazon refuses to help since it's been longer than their standard return window, so I hope that this review at least helps deter other folks in my situation from making the same mistake that I did.

title: Love the company, disappointed in this product
text:
Years ago I bought the Thule MacBook Gauntlet sleeve and loved it. It was slim, sleek, highly durable, and protected my laptop against the inevitable drop. People would ask me where I got it, and I would always refer them to Thule.

When I bought my new MacBook, I decided to upgrade to the Attache. Big disappointment. The design is odd--they try to give you enough space to carry a few items (I carry just a small 4" x 8" notebook), and still make it slim, but in doing so it's neither.

I can't fit my laptop charger comfortably. Part of the appeal of the Sleeve was the ability to open the top and leave my laptop in the case, work, then close and zip when I was done. That process is more awkward with the Attache.

Finally, if there was a flaw in the Sleeve, it would be the long-lasting durability of the elastic straps, meant to keep the case open at 90 degrees when working. Over time the straps work weaken and the top would fall over awkwardly on the people sitting across the workspace from me. Given that the bulk of the Attache is in the part meant to stay upright, I would imagine the straps would weaken much, much quicker than those in the Sleeve.

My advice to anyone considering the Attache would be to save a bit of money and go with the Sleeve, and invest in a separate carrying case to achieve whatever purpose you want the Attache "extras" for.

title: Firmware Update Warning!
text:
Be very careful about firmware updates on this device or else you could lose functionality and your configuration. As far has hardware goes the AC2600 has been good, but a poor decision by Linksys has prompted me to post this review as a warning and to express my disappointment. It is also the reason for the two stars. Prior to this debacle I would have probably given it 4 or 5 stars. Let me explain…

You used to have an option to use Linksys cloud management solution or to configure the access point locally using a built in web interface. The latest firmware update completely removes the option of local management without warning, it also wipes your entire configuration, and removes the ability to use the second Ethernet port entirely. Need/Want to use the LAG feature you paid for, sorry it’s gone. And oh BTW you also now are forced to use their new Cloud Management site.. Don’t like it? That’s too bad because you can NOT revert to the older Firmware… You are stuck. Now they do document these shortcomings on their website… The problem is, you see none of that on the firmware update screen on the device. So if you are like most people and it says a new firmware version is available you are also likely to click OK and then boom you are stuck. The UI provides no warning, nor does it even have a link to any release notes warning of the drastic changes.

This, in my view, was done intentionally to force you into their new platform. What happens when/if they decide to shutdown their cloud management solution? Or force you to pay for the privilege of accessing the management site? Well, unless they reverse course and bring back the local administration option, then you will have some large expensive paper weights.

In the meantime this update actually removes features and capabilities as well as previously mentioned, and as an added bonus it has introduced some stability issues just for fun. I now have it on a nightly reboot schedule to keep things stable. Prior to this “improved” firmware, I could go months without needing a reboot. So you basically get less, for no clear advantage. All of this could be rectified if they corse correct in a future update, but for now be careful with the firmware minefield they have introduced.

Get it together Linksys or I am likely never to purchase anything from you again!

title: Does Not Work w/ Newer Mac Computers - Deceptive Item Description by Apple
text:
I've been using my laptop to play audiobooks and music over the home audio while puttering around lately, and am tired of returning to the machine to mess with the volume or forward/rewind/pause audio. I could really use a remote. I poked around a bit, and saw this.

I read the item description above - It says "Control your Mac, iPod, or iPhone from afar with the sleek aluminum Apple Remote."

So, it'll work with my MacBook Pro, right? Why wouldn't it? I remember how ten years ago these used to come with all Mac machines. I used to have a little collection of them, back in the day.. They worked fine. They paired like a charm. No need to risk trying a third party solution, just go with the quality Apple hardware for the best experience, right?

I didn't notice that this isn't bluetooth. It's an infrared remote. It didn't occur to me to check if my laptop had an infrared receiver. Apple says here that it's compatible with Macs, it must be so, right?

But no. No. Not right. I just got this thing today. And it won't pair. For the very rational reason that my late model Mac doesn't have an infrared sensor installed. The latest Mac computer model with an infrared sensor is the 2014 Mac Mini. Other than that, no Mac products have included a sensor since 2012.

Make sure that your computer has an infrared sensor. For your convenience, here's a list pulled off from Mactracker of older Macs with infrared sensors - I assume it's correct:

Mac Mini - 2014 and earlier
MacBook Pro - non-Retina, Mid 2012 and earlier
MacBook Air - Mid 2009 and earlier
MacBook - Mid 2009 and earlier
iMac - Mid 2011 back to the iMac G5 with iSight (from 2005), with the somewhat surprising lone exception of the 20-inch, Mid 2009 model which apparently has no sensor.

Do your due diligence regarding your own hardware, verify your own specs before you buy.

Note also that Mac computers with infrared sensors can apparently only be used with infrared Apple Remotes, and not with any other infrared devices. Apple just loves to force us to buy only their hardware and peripherals, it's how they make their billions. Apple TV 4th generation devices (and later Apple TV iterations, one hopes and assumes?) are exceptions to this rule. Also - though I could be wrong here - I wouldn't assume that this Apple Remote would work with other non-Mac or Apple infrared devices.

Again, *do your due diligence.* Make sure that what you're getting is compatible with your hardware.

Else you end up annoyed and frustrated like like I am right now.

title: Much better than combination camera-lights
text:
I've got several of those security cameras that are surrounded by a zillion little IR lights; maybe you do, too. The problem is that during frequent moisture conditions at night, invisible swirls of water vapor blow and spin across in front, partially or completely blocking the view. Same during rain and snow events. The problem is that the camera’s built-in lights are immediately adjacent to the lens and light up moisture particles that are normally invisible to us.

The solution is to disable (or tape over) the internal IR lights and instead mount a separate IR floodlight several feet offset from the camera. Before, I would often get “fog stormed” out for an hour or more at a time on many nights, blinding me to what might be happening. Since one of my cameras is on guard duty to watch for bears in my bee apiary, this was unacceptable; my motion alarm would wake me up, but I had no way of seeing if it was a bear or just a passing deer.

This particular Tendelux 200ft IR light works GREAT! It is sturdy, inconspicuous, reasonably priced, and very powerful. It is far brighter than what the camera provided. The bears voted for one star, but I voted for five!

title: Enjoying Them Immensely
text:
The experience of owning these hasn't been flawless, but overall I'm very happy with them. When I first pulled them from the box they seemed heavy, which worried me. However, I find them entirely comfortable on my head. I also was disappointed that they didn't connect automatically to my iPhone. Perhaps that's because I was already running the beta of IOS 15. I tend to use Bluetooth headphones mostly for watching foreign language shows and old movies on TV, so sound quality isn't so important to me, but I did start my experience with music, specifically classical music. The headphones sound great. Obviously, I'm not interested in pumping bass, just normal music. I love the digital crown for adjusting volume and controling playback.

Yes, the case is ridiculous, but on the other hand I never use the nice hard cases on my other headphones, so maybe these are more protected in its silly case than if I just threw them on the sofa. The case also relates to battery life. Without any way of turning off the headphones other than putting them in the case, I also find that battery life runs down even when they're in it. Since I don't expect to listen to them for 20 hours a day, this is not a big defect to me, but perhaps it will be to some.

In reading other reviews, I see that the Air Pods Max are often compared to the Sony WH-1000XM4s. I haven't tried those, but I have the Bowers & Wilkins PXs, not much cheaper than the Air Pods Max now that the later are often available at a discount. I don't think one sounds better than the other, and I think the B&Ws have better battery life. On the other hand, I love the look of the Apples, and I love the digital crown, so if I had to choose one, I'd pick the Air Pods Max. Maybe because of the ridiculous case and price, I should rate them at only four stars, but because I'm so happy with them, I'll give them five.

title: IT WORKS!!!  2018 Honda Accord EX-L, iPhone 12 Pro Max
text:
Update... I ended up returning it. The connect time was a little long meaning you could not immediately start the car and, for example, set a navigation destination. But more important to me, the sound would periodically mute. When muted both the car and phone reported that everything was fine, including the song still playing. The only way I figured out to fix it was to switch the dash sound source to Bluetooth (the car would report no bluetooth available and switch back to CarPlay with the audio now working). I'm am guessing it is just a few more software updates before this problem is solved too, but I did check and I was running the latest version of that day, July 3, 2021).

-----------------------------------------

Why only 4 starts? Well the included USB cable failed in a few hours. Luckily my car's head unit suggested reseating it, which did not help, but hinted try another one. Mating it the first time is simple enough, but don't bother with the tiny printed instructions in poor English. Refer to the Amazon listing for clearer language and a larger font.

Apple CarPlay is a little quirky on its own, but with my phone in pocket, and the dongle tucked deep in a dashboard cubby, there is some screen corruption (link data errors?) that is minor (and easily fixed by switching from and back to Google Maps). I've since moved the dongle and generally take my phone out anyway. So far no problems that way.

The iPhone's own GPS gets a little flakey in my pocket. Occasionally my position is shown maybe a 100 feet off the road. The phone displays the same position if pulled out and checked directly.

As others report I am often down the road a 100 yards before it finishes connecting CarPlay. Sometimes it connects more quickly.

But I must say it is all pretty cool. I have the Honda's dash display to the left of the speedometer configured to the music playing, the main center dash display is CarPlay Google Maps, and the phone is on a MagSafe charging phone holder where a swipe up displays the native iPhone and all its distractions.

On occasion my music stops playing and I am thinking I am fat fingering something when it happens, but I can (usually?) restart it easily enough going to the Music App in CarPlay. I need more time to figure this one out...

Overall a very cool toy.

title: Really nice, easier than I thought it would be.
text:
Seems like a very sturdy monitor arm. Wasn't hard to put together at all. I'm using it with an LG 32GK850F which weighs about 13 lb. without its stand.

I guess because the monitor is fairly light I just left the monitor tilt screw wide open. It won't actually tilt down on its own even on the loosest setting. The arm adjusting screw was another story and I suspect it's something everyone will have to adjust to get the perfect setting. It was pretty easy to fine tune though.

Also, mounting it was very simple. The clamp that's included is great so don't worry about that like I did. It has enough depth to fit most desks I imagine. I think the only exception would be someone who has a custom made desk with incredible thickness and in that case you'd probably have to drill a hole and mount it to the surface.

Only have had it a day and took about 20 minutes start to finish to complete. Most of that time was spent un-mounting my monitor from its original stand and mounting it to the VESA bracket on the arm. So it's really simple, nothing to be intimidated about. I'm really happy with it.

title: Beautiful quality, need a little more height.
text:
Soundance is one of three stands that I tried (two other by BoYata). I'm having a severe neck problem since a month ago, enough to hospitalize me, and a more ergonomic setting for my laptop was urgently recommended. So I tried Soundance's laptop stand (this one), and two height-adjustable stands from BoYata.

Soundance stand's quality is superb, the best of the three. It is NOTICEABLY thicker than BoYata stands and I could feel the difference in heft. It is perfectly leveled and the thick arms hold up my laptop (15-inch Dell XPS) effortlessly. In comparison, one of BoYata stands' base arrived slightly warped and would not level no matter what I tried. The long rubber strip running down the full lengths of both arms was a great touch (BoYata stand has four tiny rubber rectangles in four corners). Some people may dislike the high lips (that curved ledges at the ends of the arms that hold the laptop in place), but personally I liked it because it made me feel more secure about leaving my laptop in its hands. (Folks, please remember your laptops often have tiny feet/supports of their own which actually add a little more thickness when you sit them down on stands!! Short lips on laptop stands are NOT a good thing.) The bottom part was actually perfect in size (and clearance) for me to comfortably stick a wireless keyboard AND a wrist pad under the stand. The risers were completely unobtrusive and gave me plenty of space. No, the angle isn't adjustable, but that isn't a huge problem for me, and if adjustable angle is a feature you're after, there are other stands that offer this feature.

When I say the Soundance stand is beautifully simple, that is a compliment. I strongly believe rather than having a lot of gimmicky features, objects should perform well and consistently in their PRIMARY function. No moving parts, everything static and steady, providing good support - Soundance is perfect in all this.

There is just one teensy problem. I am petite (5' 2") and yet when placed on top of my desk, I found that the 6" of extra height that Soundance stand provides is just a little too SHORT to put the top of the screen at my eye level. 1 & 1/2" too short, to be exact. My neck hurts more if I have to look down, so after a few hours, I decided Soundance stand just wasn't tall enough for me.

But I was loath to give up on Soundance stand, so I tried a few solutions, including sticking something between the laptop and the stand (greatly compromised stability, NO GOOD) and stacking 1"-thick book under the stand (the keyboard sat too high and strained my wrists as I typed, again, no good). It's puzzling to me. My desk isn't low. My elbows hang 1" lower than the top of the desk. So if someone as short as me was finding that this stand isn't tall enough, how are the taller folks getting along??

So sadly, I have to give up on this Soundance stand. Gain another couple inches in height, Soundance, and my XPS and I will happily return to your beautifully thick arms.

title: Scrolling glitches spoil a nicely shaped mouse thing
text:
I bumped this up to 3 stars from 2 stars for a couple of reasons. I think the scrolling issue may be battery related. If the battery is getting low then the scrolling action can get less responsive. Also, Logitech has updated their Mac software. Unfortunately I can't use it because I like MacOS 10.14 too much to upgrade. I'm not willing to give up some of my old programs and iTunes. So I can't tell you if the new Logitech software is better or not. The new version requires MacOS 10.15 or higher. (Catalina?)
__________________________

If you like the Apple Magic Mouse then this thing will feel strange in your hand at first. After a while it will start feeling more comfortable as you realize that (once again) Apple designed the shape of their mouse to be "thin and light" above all else. I like the shape of the Logitech MX better now that I've gotten used to it. But there are some serious problems. Maybe it has something to do with the Logi Options application that you need to install to set up all the mouse options. I don't know why, I just know WHAT.

This mouse often seems to ignore the scroll wheel when you are not also translating (moving) the mouse around on your table. If the mouse is stationary and you want to scroll... well, you need to move the mouse first or the scroll wheel might be ignored. This is very annoying. This seems to happen mostly in other browsers than Safari and maybe in some other apps. I haven't narrowed it down to all the specific ways it fails. The scrolling is the main problem with using the mouse. Sometimes the scroll wheel is ignored depending on where on the page the cursor is. It doesn't seem consistent in why it fails or at least I haven't figured it out. I wouldn't have bought it if I had known this and I often go back to using the Magic Mouse since I get frustrated using the MX. I wish they would fix this glitch because i sort of prefer the shape and quick feeling of the MX over the MM.

The battery seems to last quite a long time, well over a month with many hours of daily use. Most of the buttons are useful but the Gesture Button for the right thumb is awkward. You have to press down on it but it is too far backward and stiff to be useful to me. Maybe my thumb is freakishly long. I don't use it. The Thumb Wheel (right/left scroll) is something you might get used to but I'm not a fan. I still haven't used the Forward/Back buttons very much but they seem OK. They are just below the Thumb Wheel. I like the mouse click buttons and they seem very high quality with a nice light click feel and sound.

Ironically, one of the best things about the mouse is the scroll wheel. You can change it from "notchy" to "smooth" action by clicking on the button just behind the wheel. It also is adjustable in its momentum like -- glide -- setting in the Logi Options app. You can spin the scroll button fast and get to the bottom or top of a page really quickly. There is also a click on the wheel that you can customize to your liking. I use it for the ESC key.

If the scrolling function worked correctly all the time this would be a four star mouse. But the way that it can ignore the scroll wheel if the mouse isn't active is very, very, very annoying. Did I say "very" enough times to get my point across? Otherwise this is a mouse I use sometimes and other times I just can't put up with its quirks and go back to my Apple mouse. Hey, Logitech -- please fix it and make the Gesture Button useful for those of us with a mutant length thumb. How about a firmware upgrade or a Logi Options patch? Please? I'll give you a couple of more stars.

title: EXCELLENT OPTICS!  /  MISERABLE LIGHTING!
text:
This AmScope stereo microscope, like all of their stereo microscopes, has one great, overriding defect. The light source that comes with the microscope, LED, is inadequate at any magnification level. Even at 20 power, the lowest level, it is not sufficient. At 40 power it is a very bad joke. The problem is not with the type of lighting used. LED lighting is excellent. The problem is that this particular stereo microscope has only three LED bulbs shining from above. It should have at least ten, and preferably a dozen.

I bought this microscope because the picture was identical to the AmScope stereo microscope that I had a few
years ago and that was stolen with a lot of other things from my home while I was out of town for a few weeks. The microscope that was delivered to me, however, was not the one in the picture, but rather the new, 'improved' version. In my opinion the lighting on the previous model that I had was definitely better than on this one. As to the lighting from below, I did not manage to use or test it, so I cannot give an opinion as to its merits or demerits.

The improved model of this stereo microscope has a light control that permits the intensity of light to be varied from zero to full intensity. Since, however, even at full intensity at the lowest power the light is on the dim side, this is a feature that is rather useless. When the magnification power of a microscope is increased, two basic things always happen: The field of view becomes smaller, and the image become dimmer. The fact that the image becomes dimmer, however, is not a defect in the microscope, but is simply the way that the laws of optics operate. There is a way, however, to overcome this phenomenon to a degree, and that is by providing a strong
light source sufficient to compensate in part for the inevitable loss of light intensity as magnification is increased.

This particular stereo microscope has a little metal box built around the three LED bulbs that shine from above.
At the bottom of this box is a translucent piece of plastic that is probably intended to provide a somewhat attenuated and even illumination. It also, however, has the effect of dimming down the light source. The microscope would definitely do better without it.

There are light rings available that have either 60 or 144 LED bulbs that can be attached to the turret of a stereo microscope, but not on this model. The reason that this cannot be done is because of the little metal box that is
built around the three LED bulbs. There is space enough in that box for at least eight or ten LED bulbs, but only three are there. Were that metal box not there, a ring light could be mounted on the turret and then likely adequate lighting would be available at the various magnification levels.

The optics on this stereo microscope appear to be quite good, probably adequate for magnification powers up to 100 or even 120 times. But without adequate lighting, increased magnification is quite useless. I did, however, just simply turn the light on the microscope completely off and hold a very bright, high-intensity LED flashlight to light up what I was looking at, and then the picture was sharp and clear. So there are ways to work around the miserable lighting system on the AmScope stereo microscopes. If you wish to go to the trouble to try to dismount the metal box that surrounds the three LED bulbs, then it should be possible to attach a ring light to the turret of the microscope. But with the box in place this cannot be done.

Another thing about this microscope model that was the clincher for me was that you are stuck with the 10x eyepieces, which deliver 20x and 40x magnifications. It is impossible to upgrade this particular stereo microscope with different eyepieces that would permit greater magnifications to be achieved. The model that I had previously and that was stolen did not have this limitation. More powerful eyepieces could be used with it.

The construction of this stereo microscope is quite solid. It is for the most part made out of metal. The various
adjustments possible, whether focusing, etc. are smooth and work very well.

I would give this microscope a good review were it not for the miserably inadequate lighting system. I regrettably had to send it back to Amazon. I would advise anyone looking for a good stereo microscope to steer clear of AmScope products until they wise up and do something about their poor lighting system. Be aware that the AmScope stereo microscopes are identical to many other brands, since they are all made by one and the same manufacturer in China. Virtually all microscopes at present, even very high-quality ones, are made in China.

title: Overall, a GREAT machine with only a couple minor complaints.
text:
Generally, I'm amazed by this computer, and absolutely LOVE it! It is HUGE, and outstanding for gaming. I can play super beefed-up Minecraft modpacks (some with over 200 mods!) with ZERO lag. I also recently purchased GTA V for PC, and this machine runs it flawlessly. It NEVER lags in the least bit when playing, although it does become a bit warm when under a heavy load for extended periods of time. Through the included MSI software, though, you can adjust the fan settings to constantly run faster or softer as best suits your program(s).

I love its appearance as well - it is predominantly black in brushed aluminum, with a plastic base. The corners of the screen housing (lid) are slightly "angled," like a frame. But, it still has a "professional" looking appearance, as it is more-or-less rectangular like your "typical" laptop. And, it just has the simple (but cool) red dragon logo on the lid, plus the red-outlined LED-backlit keyboard. What you won't find the are crazy, flashing RGB lights, childish colors, obscurely-molded (curved) chassis, or any of the ugly "bulges" out the back that many other manufacturers of gaming notebooks include.

Moving on, the keyboard is fantastic. It has good travel, with a reasonably soft, tactile response. I would say it is slightly "bouncy," which is a feature I always look for in ANY notebook keyboard. The touchpad, however, was a bit stiff upon initially receiving. It seems to have improved, though, after "breaking" it in for a while. The screen, while not an IPS, is still very nice-looking. You can see the pixels if you look at it closely, but the color rendering is still excellent, it has an insanely-high resolution (at least coming from what I'm used to) and has teriffic response rates. When gaming, everything looks quite realistic - which I would expect and want from this sort of notebook.

Before moving on to my slight complaints, I did want to mention a few other useful tips. First off, the webcam is DISABLED by default. I ended up having to turn to Google to figure out how to activate the webcam, as the F6 key is used to disable the webcam hardware and even ELIMINATE it from the system devices list. This is great from a security standpoint, but was a horrible nuisance before I found out about it - I tried going to Device Manager and Windows 10 Troubleshooting, but to no avail... If you want to use the camera, you MUST remember to hit Fn-F6 each time. Aside from the camera, the battery life is TERRIBLE. When "maxed-out," you'd be very lucky to get even a full hour off the battery - making it more like a UPS. But, this isn't surprising in the least - it only has a 3 cell battery, and guzzles 120+ watts just from the CPU and GPU themselves when under full load. So, it's better-suited as a desktop replacement (as I'm using it), than your "on the go" notebook both due to its power demands and sheer size.

However, there are a couple minor things that DO slightly annoy me. The first is that it came with one small, stuck blue pixel towards the top-middle section of the screen. At this pricepoint, that type of defect (albeit quite minor) is still NOT something I'd want to see. Even the screens on most $200 and below "cloud" or Chrome notebooks I've seen are 100% flawless, but because it isn't a major issue in normal use and just happens to be a "random" defect, I'm not dinging any stars. Sadly, that type of defect typically falls outside of most quality control processes, and warranty won't cover it.

Finally, there is just a little bit of flex in the keyboard deck and upper chassis around the power button, and the lid does flex somewhat. With these exceptions, though, it feels pretty solid and that it wouldn't simply break under normal use. With my minor gripes aside, I would still recommend this machine in a heartbeat! It is WELL worth the money for its outstanding specs, cool (but functional) design, and extreme performance.

title: Topping & Shenzhenaudio knock it out of the park!
text:
Value for money for the EX5 is amazing. I've used the USB, Optical and Bluetooth inputs and they all sound wonderful. I haven't used the coax input yet, but no reason to suspect it is anything other than great as well.

I can't add much to the other more comprehensive reviews other than to say that I really like this DAC/Headphone Amp/Preamp and have been using it several hours per day for the last week since I got it.

I do have a few points to make that I haven't heard mentioned much by others:

1. The remote control is mandatory for full use of the product
2. The remote control does not come with batteries, you have to supply your own 2xAAA cells, I am using eneloop rechargeable and so far they are working great
3. The EX5 can be a bit picky about USB ports, I was not able to figure out exactly what the problem is. I have it working with both ASMedia and Intel USB ports but there is 1 port on my motherboard that doesn't work with the EX5 even though that port does work with other USB devices.

Suggestions for the next version if it wouldn't raise the cost too much:
1. Enable automatic switching to inputs based on the input starting to play. I would like to see the unit be able to switch from whatever current input is selected to a new port when sound starts playing on another port
2. Adjustable input volume trim would be great. It seems that the Bluetooth input is around 4 or 5 steps quieter on my unit than the USB input and the TOSLINK is 3 or 4 steps quieter than the USB input.
3. Since the headphone amp/preamp function is such high quality, it would be lovely to have one or two analog inputs, perhaps RCA on the back and/or a 3.5mm input on the front, again with adjustable volume trim
4. Long-shot: For the tinkerers out there, some mechanism for IoT control of the unit would be great. WiFi/Zigbee MQTT or i2s interface or a USB API to support on/off/volume adjustment, input selection, output selection, and so on.

text: I had my Roku Express 4+ for 2 months.  It worked like a charm.  Good picture and sound on streaming.  Then one day it started shutting off about every 30 minutes when not streaming.  The streaming was still working.  I called Roku support and they could not resolve it.  I looked for the issue in the Roku documenation online without a solution.  After changing the cables, ports, etc., the issue remained.  I did a system factory reset too.  So I just started checking all the Roku settings and found the power settings.  Under settings/system/power, there is a power saving mode that shuts the Roku down every 20 minutes.  I unchecked it and it resolved the issue.  About the same time the power issue came up, the screen saver also turned off.  I believe the firmware update for 10.5 reset these settings.  Just wanted to share this information if others have the problem since it does not seem to be documented.

title: Stunning Speakers--You Will Be Blown Away
text:
Following Polk's connection recommendations and taking a few extra steps, these speakers will blow you away. I have been a big Definitive Technology fan for years, but not anymore. One of the subwoofer amps in one of my Mythos STS towers failed—which led me to these Polk speakers. I decided not to repair the tower as I was in the market for new speakers anyway. To be blunt, these Polk speakers produce better sound across the frequency gamut (with the exception of the very low range) than the Def Tech towers that I paid $3,000 for. I have coupled the L200's with a Yamaha subwoofer to get into the very low end of frequencies—WOW!

Polk recommends bi-amping these speakers which I totally agree with. Be advised that not all AV receivers support bi-amping, so you need to check your receiver's user manual on this. Fortunately, my Marantz receiver supports it. You will also want to change the ohms value of your receiver from 8 to 4. Again, my Marantz receiver enables me to make this change. I also have a Polk 4-ohm center channel. The rear surround speakers are still 8 ohms, but it not presenting a major problem at this time; I may replace these with 4-ohm ones.

Several of my friends who have heard these Polk L200 speakers are also blown away. The sound quality is beyond my wildest expectations when I ordered these from Amazon. Give these speakers about 2 weeks of fairly average listening to break in.

title: EPIC FAIL - Cools 2-3 degrees at MOST
text:
Impressions -
All of the fans on Amazon are listed as having strong blowing power, but for my MacBook that runs EXTREMELY HOT while gaming I was more concerned with purchasing a product that offered extreme cooling ability rather than something flashy or cosmetically appealing. I didn’t care that it was plain or even if it were bulky, as long as it worked I would have been thrilled. But it doesn’t.

Value-
The price was mid range as I was able to find cooling pads for a lot cheaper, but also some that were much more expensive. I had very real expectations for this product, since it wasn’t the top dollar laptop cooler I wasn’t expecting top dollar results, but the product still falls REALLY short of my expectations. Perhaps my expectation was led to be a bit higher after seeing such amazing reviews?? I purchased this particular model after doing my research online and finding it land in a bunch of Top 5 lists by product reviewers - one of them even listed this as the #1 Cooling Device on the internet. This leads me to believe whoever reviewed and gave such high praise must have been offered a kick back of some sort.

Performance -
Well I’ll start by saying that I’m sorely disappointed in the overall functionality of the product. While the fans do run very quietly- I needed something that was really going to cool my laptop down. Even at the cost of being loud. I gave the noise level 3 stars since the product was advertised as being very quiet, and it is just that.
Since this laptop offers a temperature indicator I’ve been able to accurately test how well the product performs, and let me tell you, it doesn’t.
I’ve included an image of the temperature reading on my MacBook. While running at “Turbo” for 30 whole minutes my laptop only cools to 80 degrees from 82-83 degrees Fahrenheit. The “hot zone” is actually much warmer and is closer to 85 degrees even with the fans running at turbo.
Firstly, the speed of the fans can only be set to one of a whopping (sarcasm) two settings - ON and TURBO.
While set to ON my laptop cools 1-2 degrees, and while using turbo I got my laptop to cool a whole 3 degrees Fahrenheit. My device still runs super hot and the fan makes very little difference.
I would be happy to sacrifice some noise level for a little more cooling power!

Design-
As you can see in the image I marked up the design is somewhat flawed. While this fan advertised being suitable for the size of my laptop - it clearly does not fit the way it should. I’m unable to use the clamps to keep the laptop in place, however, that doesn’t concern me much, my laptop seems to stay in place fine just using the sticky pads on the bottom of the laptop for grip. But you can see that not only are the user controls completely covered while my laptop is on it, but the fans are a very small part of the actual device. In fact, I’ve marked the area on my laptop the seems to produce extra heat - I call this the Hot Zone - and the vents are actually closed off to that part of the laptop so it’s really only blowing at a blocked off underside of my laptop.
One thing I did like about the design was that it features 4 different temperature sensors so it can actually tell you which zones of your laptop are running hotter than others, but with only 2 fans it’s not like this function actually serves a purpose other than for giving you some extra information. The product would be greatly improved if it had 4 small fans (one per each zone) that could turn on to cool a specific zone that needed extra cooling power- rather than just 2 large fans in the center. Of course again this would be even more improved if there were more than 2 settings. I mean...there isn’t even Low, Medium, High......just On and Turbo.
It would be really cool to see any hot zones run the fan at Turbo Speed to cool everything evenly, but it doesn’t do that either.
There’s an Auto/Manual button that do nothing other than change which zone the temp reading comes from. On auto it will scroll through the zones and display each of the 4 zones temperature for a few seconds before displaying the next zone and cycling through them. On manual it only displays one temperature zone - which is the zone of your choosing.

Summary-
I was grossly disappointed with this product. It’s not a good fit for my laptop and most of the features fall very short of even being useful, the ones that are useful are poorly executed and work at a very small capacity of what I had expected them to. The fans aren’t very strong at all, and cooling just 1-2 degrees isn’t going to cut it when I’m trying to game and stream without frying my device. That being said if I had a different laptop this may have worked a bit better, but for my MacBook it just doesn’t cut it. The laptop still has a huge hot spot that doesn’t decrease in temperature at all and when the overall device is only cooling 3 degrees max on the highest setting I’d call this an EPIC FAIL.
I’m still on the hunt for a better product.

title: No performance gain over USB 2 but works in USB 3 Ports
text:
I'm going to keep the two enclosures I bought since they are so cheap
however these are *NOT* high performance enclosures as far as I can
tell (having only one non USB3 enclosure to compare it to.)

I'm using a a tool called hdparm and I'm going to show the "buffered
disk reads" since "cached reads" are very similar even with my M2
drive which is obviously higher performance than all others.

Here is the performance of *this* enclosure with the 1 TB samsung
drive when connected to a non "SS" port.

$ sudo hdparm -Tt /dev/sdb1
Timing buffered disk reads: 120 MB in 3.04 seconds = 39.46 MB/sec

Connected to an SS port, I get very similar performance (while I hoped
it would improve):

$ sudo hdparm -Tt /dev/sdb1
Timing buffered disk reads: 120 MB in 3.04 seconds = 39.47 MB/sec

This doesn't really *prove* that much. Maybe my non SS ports are
actually SS ports. Since some peripherals work in the SS ports and
others don't (how lame) they have *some* difference so I do basically
trust this result already but you should require more proof.

Let's check out what happens when I use the bigger brother 4 TB SSD
drive which is now connected directly to the motherboard using the
SATA port:

$ sudo hdparm -Tt /dev/sda
Timing buffered disk reads: 1596 MB in 3.00 seconds = 531.82 MB/sec

The buffered disk reads has jumped from 39 MB/sec to 531 MB/sec. This
is more in line with what I was hoping for. While 531 MB/sec is
impressive, an SS port is actually rated at 625 MB/sec so the drive
could in theory still be supported at full speed with an SS port and
thus in theory it's little brother drives could also work that fast
with a kick ass enclosure.

Before I deliver the death blow, here is what my 512MB "M2" main drive
plugged into the motherboard delivers:

$ sudo hdparm -Tt /dev/nvme0n1p1
Timing buffered disk reads: 512 MB in 0.42 seconds = 1228.80 MB/sec

This is clearly why if you have a choice, you really want a really big
"M2" style drive. BTW, M2 style drives differ in length -- I had to
return one 2 years ago because it was too long to fit in my tiny ass
motherboard because I opted for a small system (a mistake).

**But here is the death blow.**

I have a *non* SS enclosure I bought a few years ago so let's
benchmark that (it doesn't work in my SS usb ports so only one
number):

$ sudo hdparm -Tt /dev/sdb1
Timing buffered disk reads: 104 MB in 3.01 seconds = 34.52 MB/sec

My conclusion is that the "SABRENT 2.5-Inch SATA to USB 3.0" enclosure
being reviewed by me is only better than by old USB 2 one by 15%
though they do work in any USB port I hook it up to.

The good:

* It appears to work reliably in any USB port including SS ports

* My model of SSD fit perfectly and nothing will wiggle once installed

* Backing up 500 GB will take about 2 hours - not great but OK for
incremental backup with something like time-machine, etc.

* The transparent case option is very, very nice. I can now see what's
inside without taking anything apart. The flashing red LEDs (there
is a always on blue LED too) could be annoying to some but OK for
me. ((Just finished my copy and unmounted, the red LED turned off
though the blue LED is still on. This is good.))

* My slower enclosure was actually a mesh material. After a 2 hour
backup, while there was a slight hotspot, if you're using with an
SSD and not a rotational disk, I don't think you'll have a problem
at all.

* The cost of $10 is very reasonable. I probably will not return for
precisely this reason.

The Bad:

* This enclosure seems to perform only incrementally better than a 2
year old enclosure rated for USB 2 no matter if hooked into an SS or
non SS USB port.

* While it's not hard to slip *in* the SSD drive, it's a bit hard to
remove a drive once inserted (though certainly not impossible to
remove -- I've already done so at least twice). Had they simply left
the "bottom" open (the part with the electronics) it would be really
easy to slide in and out using thumb friction. Then slipping on the
top would have secured everything in just the same manner with no
gaps for dust or anything provided the "top" went all the way down
on the back. It's a very trivial change. I'm not an expert on
injected molded plastic but for crying out loud this can't really
cost that more and five minutes of user testing should have
discovered exactly this.

* Although the correct cable is supplied, the USB Micro-B connector on
the drive side is very weird (outside of the external hard drive
world - perhaps par for the course - two Seagate external drives I
have use this same stupid connector). The mesh USB SATA enclosure
had an almost equally hated Mini USB cable though I actually had a
few of those because I hoard cables and cell phones and Palm pilots
used this briefly in like 2008.

title: Good sound, but too uncomfortable
text:
I have used three other sets of wireless earbuds before this and two pairs of wireless headphones. All my prior wireless sets were in the $50-75 price range so the Melomania were the first set I had gotten hoping for a pair of earbuds with improved audio and usability.

I will lead off by saying that the pair of earbuds I received was found to have some level of defectiveness. The defect that was found was related to the earbud's built-in controls for things like play/pause and volume. The buttons had issues registering commands, but the volume controls through the earbuds only affected the earbud they were linked to (only the left would be affected by volume down and only the right by volume up). Even after following troubleshooting guides from Cambridge Audio, the issues persisted. I had the option to complete a request for a replacement pair, but despite the fact that I did like MOST things about the headphones and even some of the issues I had may be explained by the possibility that the buds were defective, I chose instead to request a refund. Following my refund, I choose to purchase a another pair of earbuds in a comparable price range. While those also have some issues, the concerns I had with the new pair are minor and I'm much more satisfied with them whereas even if the Melomania buds did not have defects, I may still have desired to seek a refund regardless.

So what did i like about the earbuds.

First: the battery life was spectacular. My last couple pairs of earbuds, I would only be able to use for 4-6 hours before requiring additional charging. Which if I timed things well over my day, I might be able to put them back in the case and charge enough to last my whole day. This pair, I didn't need to worry about that. I do wish I had paid more attention to exactly how long they did end up lasting for, but they are listed as having 9 hours and it very well may have been in that range.

Second: the carrying/charging case. It was pretty sleek. Fairly small profile, fit in the pocket and the palm well, had a tiny little nub that made it obvious what side to use and made opening and closing easy. Inside, the buds held very firmly by magnets so they couldn't fall out accidentally and they would also snap into place when inserting so it was easy to place them back in. They were also not difficult to remove from the case. I didn't have it long enough to see how it might be affected by scratches like if you had them in the pocket with your keys or something, but the material it was made of didn't seem like it would have any issues with material peeling or scratching too easily/badly. Charging was through a USB-C cable and did appear to charge well and quickly. There was an easy to read light system to show how much charge remained in the case as well.

Third: The earbud controls operated through a physical button. The tactile feedback of pressing a button just feels so much better than a sensor. The fact that the button took up the entire end of the earbud did cause some issues for me, but only when trying to put them in and I'll get to that later. But that's an entirely different problem regardless of the button type, just with how much of the end of the earbud was taken up by the button.

Fourth: Sound quality and customization. In general, the earbuds did sound good. The app that integrates with the earbuds also allowed for many preset EQ settings as well as allowing customization settings. As someone who isn't an audiophile, I don't know anything about how to customize these settings, but I could at least understand the presets and while I would normally keep it on a more balanced setting, I did try some of the others if I was listening to more speaking based audio like podcasts or certain genre of music.

So why did I choose to return them and not seek a replacement.

My main issue with the earbuds was that they were very uncomfortable for me. I tried using both the foam and the silicone tips. The foam tips seemed like they should have provided cushioning to make things more comfortable, but even the smaller foam tips I had difficulty putting in my ear. The foam of those tips did not compress well such that it would then expand to conform to the inside of my ear like I've had with other earbuds in the past and earplugs in general. The most comfortable tips I tried for these were the medium silicone tips. While I was able to keep them in for several hours only minimally needing to take them out due to the irritation, from the moment that I put them in it I could feel the edge of the earbud digging into my inner ear. Even after removing, my ear would still feel irritated for quite a while. And then the following day when I would put them in again, it compounded the irritation from yesterday. This may be entirely an issue with MY ears, other people may not experience this whatsoever. And maybe with continued use and giving my ears more rest between use, I might have been able to adjust to them at some point. But it was just too uncomfortable and felt like it was getting worse. Now that I've been using my new pair for some time, I'm no longer feeling the inner ear pain I had been, but it was very uncomfortable for the week I was using the Melomanias

Next: Connectivity/audio distortions. This problem MAY have been caused purely by whatever defect was present in the earbuds. Without a second pair to compare, I don't know. And it was not something that happened frequently, but even the few occasional times that it did stick in my memory. There would be a dip in connection or the audio became distorted in some way. It only lasted a moment, but other wireless earbuds or headphones I've had, I had not experienced anything similar unless I was approaching the range limit of the Bluetooth. But I would have the device in my pocket or just a few feet away and still have it happen intermittently.

I don't know if this point is directly related to the previous issue or possibly another defect, but the connectivity range of the earbuds was abysmal. As mentioned, I've used numerous other pairs of earbuds and headphones in the past and at this point, I have also gotten a new pair to replace the returned Melomanias. All my other wireless audio devices including the newest pair, I have been able to leave my phone by my computer to go to my kitchen or bathroom and maintain connection with my device. Both are ~20 feet away at the absolute max and while there is a wall, the walls have an open door way. All my past headphones and also the earbuds I got as a replacement were able to maintain a connection easily at that distance with that obstacle without losing audio. The Melomania earbuds were the only ones I had ever had which I pretty consistently could not do this with. I found myself either needing to leave my earbuds at my desk or take my phone with me if I wanted to get up for a couple minutes for a drink or restroom break.

Lastly, the shape of the buds. The earbuds are peg shaped. I don't particular mind from an aesthetic point of view, I think that LOOKS fine, but functionally it did cause some trouble. Minor trouble, but trouble nonetheless. I don't know if this is part of the reason why they are uncomfortable inside the ear, but the issue I have with the circular peg shape doesn't conform to the shape of the more outer areas of the ear like a more comma shaped earbud. Every single time I would put them in, I would invariably end up hitting the built in button on the earbud and end up playing/pausing or changing the volume (which was a particularly annoying situation considering the defect these buds had). Adjusting them while in my ears was also annoying usually resulting in a button press, but because there isn't a shape that conforms to my ear, I just felt like I was jamming them as deep as they could go in my ear. And while I didn't have much/any issue taking them out, I did have issues of what to do when I took them out. Unless I put the bud directly in the case, setting them down on a surface like a table risked them rolling around and falling off. Other earbuds that do not have a shape conducive to rolling wouldn't experience similar concerns.

title: STICK TO A BRUSH!
text:
At first impression, this is a fantastic product. You can clearly see the dirt and dust left on the tacky. It is relatively simple to clean and even more-so to use. I used it for one year after every record, sometimes even between sides. Now, this probably amounted to some 100 or so uses, and recently I’d begun wondering if I needed to replace my stylus. I have a AT-VMN540ML, so it should last for 1000 hours give or take a hundred or so, according to documentation. That’s about roughly about 1300 records, so I should be nowhere near needing a replacement. After buying a usb microscope and stand, I removed the stylus from the cartridge and inspected it.

Wow. Just. WOW. My impression changed. Best as I can surmise from other reviews and my visual inspection, the tacky cleaner did two things terribly wrong.
1) It left tacky residue that dirt and dust will cling to.
2) What dirt couldn’t make contact with the product was pushed up the stylus and stayed there.
I had to use my fingernail to scrape some of the grime off!

I could have let the photos speak for themselves, but I wanted to wax just a little. I almost showed an “after” photo where I’ve managed to clean my stylus up some, but thought people might get the opposite impression of this product, and I wanted to make myself clear.

DO NOT BUY THIS TYPE OF PRODUCT. STICK TO A DRY STYLUS BRUSH.

title: sound lack base.  Cannot turn buds off without the charging case. noise cancellation sucks.
text:
I was looking forward to this pair of echo buds 2 given the good reviews, however, I am quite disappointed. First, the pairing is not as easy as it sounds. I already have the alexa app installed on my android phone due to other echo dot products. The pairing did not happen as written in the instructions until I repeated the process multiple times. Second, the sound seems to lack base, but I assume this can be fixed by using the equalizer in the app, so this is not a major issue for now. Third, I heard no difference in the low rumble of the dish washer with the noise cancelling on or off. I understand this type of noise cancellation is only good for lower frequency sounds. Lastly which is the worse design decision possible, is not to include a way to turn off the buds without placing them into the charging case. Every other pair of buds I have can be turned off by some gesture control. Sometimes one just wants to turn off the buds without continuously charging them. The construction appears to be solid but slightly too bulky. Since it sticks out of the ear a bit, the weight distribution out side of the ear makes the buds to fall out easier unless the tips are securely fitted inside the ear canals. The wing tips might help, but I generally do not like to use them as they are not comfortable. With alexa voice commands, it does offer some convenience as to control the buds without touching them, but some command had to be repeated multiple times. Hopefully I can find a good use for these pair of buds somewhere.
Updated 4/13/2022
After getting accustomed to these buds, I am updating it from 1 star to 3 stars. I really want the future gen 3 of these buds to succeed. 1) The sound might not be the best, but it does not tire out your ears with an hour of listening as with some other brands of buds. For the current reduced price, the price to sound quality ratio is very good. 2) Need to start the Alexa app everytime to guarantee voice commands get recognized. 3) With the proper fitting, passive noise cancellation with active noise cancelling does an ok job, but since I go for walks on the streets with these buds, some background rumbles to warn me of nearby cars are preferred. 4) No off feature still sucks, but I have learned to use the case. Make sure to push on the buds after placing them back into the case which ensures a proper contact is made. When this pushing is not done, many times the case get drained of battery very quickly without using the buds.

Overall these buds did grow on me. The construction is solid and appears to be reliable. The connection to bluetooth has been consistent and reliable. The way it stick out of the ears is still inconvenient where wave of the arm might knock it out of one's ear, so it does take some getting used to.

Updated 7/7/2022
Took these buds on vacation. What a disappointment. Could not use these buds most of the time due depleted charges. Would charge it up for an hour or so at the hotel, but when the time comes to use these buds, the battery is empty. This is an electronic device, and it is of no use when there it does not have juice regardless of the wonderful features it has. Should have brought my other pair of ear buds, which clearly tells me 'the device is turning off' when I manually turns it off. My suspicion is the Echo Buds turns on in the casing during travel, however I cannot be sure. The only sure thing is it was useless during my vacation. Reduing the rating to one star again.

However, the latest 2000 model includes Wi-fi connectivity, thereby defeating the very purpose of buying the product -- which was to avoid having wi-fi radiating devices in the house. I'm glad to say that this is excellent, I'm sure my Sony 85 f1.8 is technically faster but I can't tell. Distortion is pretty well handled which was another knock on the Tamron 20mm f2.8 1:2. I also love the added button which I use to switch to APS-c mode which give me 36mm at about 19MP on my A7R3, I also used the Lens Dock to change the switch to AF/MF this makes the lens more convient to use and definitely adds value. My one gripe is that there isn't a lens profile for the lens yet in Lightroom, but hopefully it comes soon.

If you're looking for a sharp excellent focusing,feature packed wide angle prime this is it. There isn't anything else even close in the price range. Ofcourse I'm sure the Sony 24mm f1.4GM is superior but for my budget and the fact that I'm just a hobbyist I'll save $900.

title: Excellent sound, let down by spotty connectivity
text:
I *really* wanted to like these. I've had great experiences with KZ's wired earphones, and as far as audio reproduction goes, these have a similar sound signature to KZ's ZS line. The dual drivers give it a decently wide sound stage, and bass and treble come through nicely without either being overpowering. Battery life also seems to be as advertised - around 6 hours at medium volume, which is still more than sufficiently loud, and the charging case is extremely quick to recharge them.

So why the mediocre review? Although the audio quality is wonderful, the Bluetooth side of these has been a serious letdown.

Like many newer TWS earbuds that I've tried out, these switch seamlessly between left and right earbuds from a single pairing record, and I was really hopeful that the connection would be as stable as other Bluetooth 5.2 buds that I've tried. Unfortunately, over several days of testing around my apartment, I've encountered multiple occasions when one earbud's connection would drop for several seconds while the other kept playing, while standing only a couple feet from my phone. I've sometimes even been able to reproduce this by just cupping my hand over one ear while wearing both earbuds. On a few occasions, I've even had both earbuds drop their connection for several seconds on end, or one of them lose a connection long enough to give me the "turn off" voice prompt.

This is nothing like the connectivity issues I've experienced even in the least expensive Qualcomm-based Bluetooth 5.2 earbuds I've tried, and this may be in part due to the Bluetooth chip used. Although the Amazon item description claims that these earbuds use a Qualcomm chip and support AptX, this does not appear to be the case - instead, they appear to use a Realtek chip, and only support AAC and SBC codecs. (Possibly a leftover line from the sell sheet of the similar SKS earbuds, which are confirmed to use a Qualcomm chip?)

This may just be a fluke with certain pairs or manufacturing batches; I've seen some reviews of these that report similar issues to what I've encountered, and others who had no connection problems even on walks outside. In that case, this merits a "buyer beware" at the very least, as it's impossible to tell whether a given pair will be affected.

title: Overheats. Do not buy if in a warm climate or experience summer or drive for more than 30 minutes
text:
Are you looking for a dashcam that has great 4K recording but has features that don't work and overheats after about 30 minutes of use? Then this dashcam is perfect for you. If you want something reliable and functional, get something else. WiFi connectivity worked for 1 day then just locks up when attempted again. Dashcam was received with latest firmware, reflashing it made no difference, nor did resetting to defaults nor trying iOS or Android. Parking mode using Viofo HK3 just records all the time, even when it's set to only record incidents. Camera overheats in parking mode and then doesn't turn on with ignition. Worked correctly once or twice with a cool night but then stopped when the temperature got warmer. Gave up on WiFi and parking mode and just used it with the cigarette lighter USB adapter to find that it overheats with about 30 minutes of use using that too. Taking the memory card out when the camera locks up at this point almost results in burnt finger tips the memory card is so hot. For the 30 minutes the camera works the recording image quality is fantastic at 4K front and 1080P rear. I have had a number of other dash cams in my vehicle and never had one that overheats.

Don't be tempted to get this on sale like I did. Get a different 4K dashcam from another brand like Thinkware or BlackVue. Wish I could return this useless product but it's passed the return window now. I would give negative stars if that was possible.

title: There is Dead Space on the Screen
text:
Overall, this tablet is alright. I'm satisfied with what I paid for it, because I'm easy going. But there's one glaring issue with it that needs to be addressed bc I think it's something that's pretty unacceptable (even though I put up with it)

The dead space......... Basically, dead space is an area on a touch screen where it's not touch sensitive. It doesn't react to your finger or the stylus. My tablet has one, and at first while I was using my drawing program I thought that maybe I had added something in-program that prevented that space from being drawn on. Upon closer inspection, I saw that the stylus cursor was actually moving AROUND that area on the screen, away from where my stylus pen was actually pointed. title: Decent, but don't expect amazing picture quality
text:
Overall the product is decent for the price. But after using it for a while (for soldering) the picture quality has become frustrating enough that I'm looking at other options.

I don't use many of the features on it, just simply turn it on (I keep it plugged into external power via usb) and solder away. And assuming your board doesn't have details that are too small, it works okay for that.

But if you look at the picture you can see what I'm talking about on the quality. Granted those solder balls in the middle are pretty small - about 0.4mm pitch. But the image is too grainy and I can't really see what I'm doing on something like this. Another thing is while it has 4 levels of zoom, they do not appear to actually change anything related to the lens, but instead only take the same exact image and make it bigger on the screen (i.e. you can see the same blurry, fuzzy image bigger - it doesn't magnify with the lens any differently).

Some good things about it are:
- refresh rate is very fast, almost no visible lag at all on the screen (not sure about using an external display, haven't tried it)
- it goes up high enough that I can easily work and do soldering under it
- light gets pretty bright, no problems with it being too dark (I have to turn it down a bit actually, knob on the side)
- zoom is somewhat decent (but again, only if you can suffer the quality)

If you want something inexpensive and easy to use, it's a decent product. But if you don't want to run into problems like those shown in the image, go with something else (and probably pay fair bit more).

title: Good Sound Quality
text:
After remodeling our family room, my wife insisted that we get rid of our 7.1 surround system just because she did not want to see all the speaker wires going around the base boards and up the walls to all the speakers. This system only has three or four wires, (two from the subwoofer to the rear satelite speakers) and one or two connecting the sound bar to the TV, there are also two power supply cords one for the subwoofer and one for the soundbar.
After getting it all set up, I was happy with the sound quality, it isnt as good as the surround system it replaced but it cost less than 1/4 what I paid for the system it replaced and this soundbar sounds good enough that I will be ok with it for my daily TV movie watching, for a full theater experience, I will need to go to my home theater.
The remote control has an LED screen that is difficult to read because of its low backlighting and poor contrast between the letters and background, but even though it is hard to read, there are enough options for setting up the speakers that you can get a good custom sound for your space, I ended up pushing my subwoofer too much, and I ended up needing to reduce the subwoofer volume and base intensity because it was vibrating/shaking through the walls on the main floor of our house. Overall, I am happy with this soundbar system and I think it will be an ok alternative for my basic daily movie watching where I am used to having a full surround system, this replicates the surround sound good enough for daily use and more than enough for people who are used to just using built in TV speakers, for anyone who is ok with TV speakers, this system will be an amazing upgrade, but if you are hoping to replace a good quality surround system, this will just be an average to OK replacement that may or may not be as good as what you are used to using.
I am only happy with it for the price I paid and for the fact that I could hide the subwoofer under a piece of furnature in the back of my room and I can almost entirely hide the satelite speaker wires from my view For a system with these hidden wiring requirements it seems like it will be a good alternative for my new family room.

title: This is an "Isolation Transformer- Based Power Conditioner", NOT an isolation transformer!
text:
So who gets the one star? Not the product; that's probably fine when used for its intended purpose. It's Amazon that gets 1 star for listing this as an isolation transformer.

The manufacturer calls this product an "Isolation Transformer- Based Power Conditioner". The outputs are NOT floating and can't be used for test equipment isolation as-is. (Other reviewers point out that it can be converted to an isolation transformer by modifying its internal wiring. There goes your warranty.)

The manufacturer's description is correct, it's a power conditioner, not an isolation transformer, because it bonds one pole of the output transformer to ground. That point becomes "Neutral", and the other output lead 'Hot'. They have a ground reference and are not floating.

It's unfortunate Amazon's product description misses the mark so badly.
