title: Amazing Dolbly Atmos Sound
text:
I have multiple Sound bar systems ranging from Bose, Nakamichi Shockwafe Elite, Samsung, and Lower end Vizio units.

This unit comes out on top even over the Nakamichi Shockwafe Elite. The automated elevating outer Atmos speakers lets you know the signal is true Atmos and properly fires to the ceiling. It sounds more immersive then the Nakamichi Shockwafe Elite system which is honestly NOT true Atmos with True directional upper ward firing speakers, but rather a firmware update to simulate it.

Out of the box the unit is easy to set up, but is a large unit, easily the length of a 65" TV. To hook it up correctly i Hooked the Xbox series X and PS5 directly to the sound bar HDMI input, then the output HDMI to the TV which detected it as the correct sound bar for configuration. (Samsung 4k RU7100).

XBOX SERIES X: (OUR MEDIA CENTRAL UNIT) Change sound setting to Bitstream then select Dolby Atmost as the second Option. To test download the Dolby Atmos App on Xbox Marketplace, choose homet heater setup, and it self configs. Run on of the Bottom Atmos demos and you will see the speakers auto move to position showing it is working. Enjoy Atmos movies in movie apps that support it or 4k Blu-ray. Enjoy Dolby Atmos supported games. (ENJOY)

PS5: You can config support for Atmos in Movies only. the PS5 DOES NOT support Atmos games, but rather sony's priority. Games will still sound good but not be as immersive with this unit. In movies you need to open the menu while it playing and select bitstream to trigger atmos use on that console. If you ahve both consoles, I highly recommend you use the Xbox for movies rather then the extra steps in the ps5.

DEFAULT SETTINGS:

The sub is to strong by default, use the remote to decrease the sub to abotu two marks above Zero. Adjust as needed. This sub blows the Nakamichi Subs out of the water. Nakamichi did not goes as low in frequency and you did't hear now feel it as well. Not the case with the Vizio Elivate which is powerful, maybe a tad to powerful at default. Lower it a bit.

Highs: raise the highs for even crisper sound. About 3 -4 marks over mid. PERFECTION.

You can also adjust the voices. The default or 2-3 above is perfect. with 18 speakers, you hear every voice perfectly and separate from the regular sounds of the center channel.

You can adjust the rotating speakers manually. If you want a more bubble effect you can set them to always up (except when the unit powers off they will lower-then raise again when on) or leave them automatic. If they rotate in atomic then you know the Atmos signal has been received during playback.

Compared to the other bars I have had, I never can go over half volume without it being far to loud, meaning you have room for larger rooms. We sit about 6-7 feet away and anything over mid is way to loud. So if we get a very large room I know we will now have the power.

You can also adjust the atmos up firing front and rear channels independent of other speakers (front L R, Center, Dialog, Rear surrounds. This helps for the height of your ceilings. However ATMOS really only works with flat ceilings not arched or other shapes. You can have a ruff surface but it needs to be flat over head.

THIS SYSTEM IS AMAZING!

title: Versatile Tube Preamp That Pairs Well With Aiyima A07
text:
I was trying to decide between this Aiyima T8 and the Douk P1, but this one won me over due to the remote control and optical in, which the P1 both lack. This (with the Aiyima A07 power amp) is replacing an SMSL AD18 that's going to my garage. I needed a versatile, inexpensive, and small preamp unit for my bedroom, and this is perfect for my needs. This and the A07 are currently feeding Emotiva B1+ speakers. My audio source is a Chromecast Audio connected to the T8 via optical in, and while the Sabre ES9018K2M isn't the newest DAC chip around, it is still very capable. I also tried the RCA, USB, and bluetooth inputs, and they all work well.

One thing to note is that there's been a bit of confusion regarding the tube signal output. Some online reviews have stated that if you want the tube sound, you need to use the front 3.5mm headphone out only. After emailing with Aiyima, they confirmed that the tube signal also goes to the rear RCA out. In fact, there is no audio output at all if no tube is inserted. Anyway, I've been using a NOS 6N3P-E tube and am happy with the sound.

Lastly, the bass and treble adjustments are nice feature. Since I'm using this in an upstairs bedroom where I do not want a subwoofer placed, a slight increase in bass EQ is all that my speakers need to sound more full-bodied when playing music. A slight negative though is that from what I know, the only way to adjust treble and bass is thru the remote control. If you lose or damage the remote, you're out of luck with EQ adjustments.

Overall, I like this T8 a lot. I'm a fan of small budget hifi components, and this is perfect for my needs. This paired with the small and excellent A07 sound better than my outgoing AD18.

title: Problem when you have more than one device in the same home
text:
My wife's watch was working get great until last week when I could no longer get it to synchronize with the phone app. After calling Fitbit support and having them walk me through the resolution, here's the fix. First let me explain our setup. I have a Fitbit ALTA HR which works fine and I have no problems managing it. My wife owns the newer VERSA 2 smart watch. I've been managing both from my cellphone which was working OK until last week when I could no longer get the VERSA 2 to synch. Here's what I've learned.

a) Do not try to manage more than one device on one phone.
b) Make certain that the two devices are not in the same room when you try to synch them.

This has been working fine for that last few days.

title: Great Sound Quality, Feature-Packed. GREAT CUSTOMER SUPPORT.
text:
This is hands down the best microphone i've owned.
Everything about it feels premium: The weight, the base, the product presentation (box, booklets, manual) and the build quality of the microphone itself.

I wanted a dual-purpose microphone that would allow me to do:

- Game Comms: With and without headphones, on Cardioid mode it'll only pick the sounds coming from the front of the microphone, no issues with Discord being activated by the sound coming from the speakers, if the sound is coming from behind, it does not get picked up, this is a great relief for those instances when i don't feel like wearing headphones but i don't want the sound of my game broadcasted/interrupting communications.

- Hi-Res Voiceovers: I am getting into the YouTube world and i voice-over videos now and then, this Mic does an outstanding job with it's 96 KHz. You can adjust the gain on the back and based on how you position your mic and the pickup pattern you use, you can achieve different effects, great!

- Stream: I don't do a lot of streaming, but i do, and based on the Voiceover i made and the quality it sends thru Discord for gaming, it'll be great for that.

The controls are simple and easy: Two knobs on the back one for volume (for headphones through the aux port on the bottom, and one for microphone gain (that'll affect how loud your voice would come, think amplification).
On the front we have the Mute button (that my only wish is that it had memory to remember if i left it muted, or actually even better to be defaulted Mute and activate it when you want to use it, you know... for privacy reasons.

The other one is the Pickup Pattern Mode button, which has the cardioid, omnidirectional, bidirectional and stereo modes, if you don't need what these mean: YouTube is definitely your friend.

I loved the multi-color LED ring under it, and you can pick the color of your preference by pushing the button on the bottom.

Unfortunately, i received a faulty USB-C code with this product, i thought it was a driver issue, but when i tried a different cable, it worked, i kind of missed the L-Shaped convenience of the included cable and contacted Thronmax and they immediately replied letting me know they'll send a replacement cable, THIS COMPANY STANDS BEHIND THEIR PRODUCTS.

Overall, a solid solution, feature-packaged at an affordable price, i am the happy owner of this Microphone and based on what i see, it'll last me a long time. Recommended.

title: Great plug and play DVD player for my MacBook Air (2020)!
text:
The one thing that made this DVD player stand out from the others I was looking at was the fact that it had a USB-C adapter already attached to the player. I have a MacBook Air (2020) that only has USB-C ports so this was important to me. I’ve checked and both the USB and USB-C adapters work beautifully.

I did not have to install a driver as Mac already has a driver included in their system. I had to search for it because it doesn’t appear in the Mac Launchpad or in the utilities folder like in previous MacBooks. The easiest way to find it is to do a search using “spotlight” (the magnifying glass icon on the top right of your screen).

Another plus is that the DVD tray where you insert your DVD actually pops out at the press of the button on the DVD player itself. My last external DVD player did not have this and I had to eject it from within the app or by right clicking on the DVD icon from my computer. This didn’t always work out so well.

I haven’t tried writing anything to a DVD yet, but I don’t normally do that anymore anyway. But for my purposes, this DVD player works beautifully.

This DVD player does not work when connected directly to a projector. But there is a work around. If you connect your computer to your projector and the DVD player is connected to your computer, you’ll be able to project your movies onto any surface.

It’s also important to note that this DVD player does not connect to other devices like tablets or phones. Again, it only works when connected to a computer.

Over all, I’m pretty pleased with this DVD player! It’s portable and the wires fold away nicely for storage. It does everything I need it to do.

title: Hard pass on Ring Doorbell
text:
I've been running it about two weeks now.
The Good:
- Viewing Angle: sees everything I wanted it to from a viewing standpoint.
- Clarity: Is pretty good, even at night.
- Neighborhood Alerts: Depending on your view of things it's nice or it's annoying. I found it nice to know when there were porch pirates around stealing things, but it was always the next day. The police alerts were nice and those I appreciated. The amount of theft happening around me is staggering, so that was a bit unnerving. But I guess I'd rather know.

The Meh:
- Battery Life: I have to have all setting maxed (motion sensitivity, motion frequency) for it to register anything and that chews battery.
- Support: They did ship me the missing piece (still haven't received yet) but they "access" your amazon account that is tied to the doorbell. I wasn't thrilled about that. You provide them "temporary" access but there was no way to know when or if that was revoked. I just unlinked my account, hoping that would be enough. That could be poor communication on their part as to how that all is handled but really they shouldn't be doing it at all. If it hadn't been for the resolution, I'd have put this in the next category.

The Not:
- Motion Detection: Is my number one issue with this system. I have been trying to optimize settings every day. The motion detection is garbage. I have done every recommended tweak out there. Unless it's max sensitivity and max frequency, nothing is picked up. Even then, it picks up cars going by (with the detection zone no where near the road!) and it DOESN'T pick up anyone walking in the detection zone!
I've spent days testing and tweaking and no dice. I have packages that get dropped off right in front of it without it catching the delivery person. Pointless to have this thing since that is what I got it for (lots of theft in our area).

If someone presses the button it will start to record, but.. yea thieves aren't nice enough to let you know they are stealing your packages. The voice works well enough to talk to the person at your door (assuming you know they are there..) but it's just a nice to have, not a core function for me.

- The Ring App: Tells me I have great wifi connection signal, yet I still have issues with lagging notifications and the app not updating while in use. Also, if you use this on multiple devices, it doesn't update in the other devices if you make a change. After removing it off devices down to one, I still have the aforementioned issues.

-The contents of the Package: I was missing a drillbit and had to contact support. I get that stuff happens, but to me that's a hassle I didn't need. I'm waiting now for the replacement to arrive so I can include it when I send it back. Luckily, I was able to attach the doorbell with two screws but it's not very secure. I could have bought a bit set I guess but it was supposed to come with one so .. why spend more money?

Overall there is a decent start here but it's definitely not worth the money, headaches, and time in my experience. Other people have had better luck. Or maybe they just don't expect much (or don't know what footage they are missing..). For me this is a Hard Pass, sadly.

title: Disappointing Audio Quality, Same Overall Alexa Functionality, Better Energy Saving Ability
text:
I purchased this 4th Gen Echo Dot to use in my office. I already have a 3rd Gen Echo Dot there, so this gave me the opportunity to play the same material through one or the other and compare performance between the two. To say I'm disappointed is an understatement. The 4th Gen audio is tinny and lacks presence. In addition, it's significantly quieter for a given volume level (i.e., 50% on a 4th Gen is easily 25% quieter than 50% on a 3rd Gen). In terms of something positive, both units do fine at recognizing my voice, the wake word, commands, and so on, and Alexa functionality is unchanged.

So, if you're wanting to have full audio that has good presence and a reasonably flat EQ curve for a normal sized room, definitely save your money and go with the 3rd Gen Echo Dot. If, on the other hand, you have a small room that has problems with lower frequency background noise, then maybe the 4th Gen Echo Dot might be better for you.

Pros:
Pleasant visual aesthetic
Light-ring is at bottom so it's reflecting off the surface you have the Dot on, not off the ceiling
Power-saving mode when not in use (with a few exceptions)
Easy setup/Alexa integration
Microphone is sufficiently sensitive

Cons:
Poor audio quality (tinny, not very present sounding) compared to 3rd Gen Dot
Minimal bass even with EQ turned up in the Alexa app
Taller than 3rd Gen Dot
Cord/Plug is white even though the unit is black, so it's super noticeable (and not in a good way)
Seems to have low overall volume compared to 3rd Gen Dot
Will only stereo/multi-pair with other 4th Gen Dots (and Subwoofer)

Recommendation:
If you're going to be listening to audio through your Dot (either Bluetooth or streaming), stick with the 3rd Generation Echo Dot model. There's no compelling reason to downgrade to a 4th Gen Dot.

title: Enormous in every way (size, capability, range)
text:
(Purchased from Costco)
This router was the top or a top recommendation across multiple review sites and articles, especially for those seeking Wifi6 or dedicated gaming/streaming bands. I installed two of these (my home and another family member's home) in the past few weeks and have had a wonderful experience.

Signal Strength:

Both locations are 2 level homes with a full basement. In one home the router is on the middle floor and at a far end (exterior wall). In another home the router is on the top floor and in the middle of the home. In both cases we get strong 2.4 and 5 GHz signal strength in all parts of the home. In both homes a Roku was hooked up in the farthest parts of the home on the 5 GHz band and had an "excellent" signal strength (short 1 bar of full).

SSIDs / Network Bands:

This router can have up to 3 network bands (1x2.4 and 2x5 GHz) with corresponding guest networks for each. I have set up 4 SSIDs (1x2.4, 2x5, and 1 guest network on the 2.4 band). Non-guest SSIDs can either be linked to have the same network information, passwords, etc. and the router can auto-select the best SSID or you can set all of them up individually and pick the SSID for each device to join. I did the latter reserving 2.4 GHz for IoT devices, 5-1 GHz for regular devices (phones/laptops), and 5-2 GHz for gaming/streaming. I use a separate 2.4 GHz guest network for friends/family outside the home to use when visiting. Setup was easy either on the web or via the Tether App, I have used both. I even have my family member's router tied to my T-Link/Tether account so I can monitor their network remotely.

Speed:
I have had no issues with internet speeds. I have 100Mbps upload/download service so can't test it's 1 Gbps capability, but wired connections consistently hit 101-102 Mpbs. Wireless devices near the router hit 95+ Mbps on all bands. At distance (30+ feet) and in the opposite corners of the home speeds have varied between 80-90 Mbps across all bands (with 2.4 GHz most consistently higher).

We have had no streaming issues with any devices at any location in the home. No lag or buffering concerns utilizing Apple devices (phone, Mac, iPad), HP laptop, or Roku.

Feature Set:

I won't go into them all - but it has almost any feature you could need (including QoS). Unless you are the mightiest of power users and networkers this doesn't lack anything.

Physical Device:

This thing is a beast. If I were to knock anything it would be its size and the fixed antennas. You cannot directionally aim the antennae, they are where they are once installed. This will also take up a lot of space wherever you put it - it's almost more of a show piece / art piece than a router. But, if that's what it takes to work as well as it does, so be it.

Overall:

I'm very pleased. We replaced a previous router that was having connection issues and required rebooting on a recurring basis. IoT devices kept falling off. With over 52 connected devices (13 wired), the TP-Link hasn't blinked an eye. We have two people working from home and a high schooler in remote learning and no issues whatsoever.

Highly recommend

There are no clips on the tripod so that the wire hangs loose beside the tripod. The length of the wire between the power supply and the lamp was too short. When the lamp is mounted on the tripod at full extension, the transformer is suspended off the ground and places strain on the lamp power connector. The wire is about 20 cm too short to allow the power controller to sit on the ground at the base of the tripod.

The tripod ships with a plastic cap on the threaded end of the tripod. The instructions do not instruct the user to remove this cap, but (see pics) the lamp does not sit on the tripod properly with the cap in place, so it must be removed.

The bag has individual slots for the lamp and tripod components which is super-convenient. The bag does not include a pocket for each of the transformers, which was really odd because they clearly thought about how useful the pockets are.

I took pictures of the lamp at full brightness. My aim with the lights was to find imperfections in the drywall finish and the lights accomplish this. A much brighter light would do a much better job for my task but I think this will do.

I need to decide whether I will tolerate the light level for my application. That's not a function of the product, but my demand for a brighter light than this provides.

title: All around excellent value
text:
This is my first pair of true wireless headphones, I'm listening as I write this, and I haven't written a review in years. I'm not a fan of bluetooth, so I was skeptical of buying these, but needed something for a long flight. For reference, I'm not an "audiophile", but my home hifi system cost 10k, is very minimalist (Hegel H190 w/ KEF Ref1s) and sounds pretty amazing.

About ten years ago, it occurred to me that we would soon have an audio version of Google Glass, and it has been entertaining watching this slowly manifest in these types of headphones. This concept is very much in its infancy and I'm not surprised to see an overlap in market between tech users and the hearing impaired community. Soon, I imagine that there will be intelligent noise cancellation (select for/against certain "waveprints" i.e. FOR your friends voice at a crowded restaurant and AGAINST the crying baby sitting across the room) and the unique waveprint of your voice will be included with your general contact information. Infinite other applications, but I digress.

I was surprised to see the breadth of the market, with so many companies doing gymnastics to distinguish themselves, and failing miserably in the reviews. And you would think that humanity would have mastered bluetooth pairing and connection by now, but for so many of these products, that is not the case. Sooo many dumb dumb dumb products out there, poorly designed and with little to no product testing or quality control, banking on what's left of their brand coupled with the nuisance of having to return a terrible product. But this isn't one of them.

I think that Sony has nailed it with these headphones. There is definitely room for improvement, but not at this price point. The product arrives in a tiny little biodegradable box (which I love) with no frills or desperate attempts to gain first impressions. Cost has been reduced on the carrying case materials (good!) and there are little magnets which hold the buds in place (love it!). I plugged them in to charge for a bit, then put them in my ears. I was pleasantly surprised to hear them automatically pair, upon release from the charger, and connect to my Samsung Galaxy A50. I then put on Spotify, which has a somewhat poor bitrate to begin with (320 kbps) and is cheapened even further by bluetooth, and got about what I was expecting: a totally adequate though far from stellar sound that was largely out-shined by the newfound convenience and extreme comfort of this ergonomically well designed and executed technology. I then tried them with some high quality recording on high quality FLAC files. I really don't have much to say about the sound except that it is not offensive. Again, my baseline is a 10K system. The extra space over conventional wired earbuds facilitates bass presence, but there is nothing transcendent or even particularly precise about the mids or highs and no noticeable soundstage. They could possibly benefit from an "open back", but then you lose the privacy.

But no one buys these for hifi sound quality. Most people have never even heard hifi. And so much of hifi depends on the physical environment (i.e. the room) that you could never hold this type of product up to those standards. Certainly not at this price. This success of *this* product carries an extra burden of comfort, convenience, and ease of use. In spite of my system, I have actually found myself wearing these around the apartment so I can listen at higher volumes late at night. They are ridiculously comfortable as so many other products fail so miserably at this most basic and essential function, and I honestly forget that I am wearing them. And the controls are simple and intuitive and don't have any stupid design flaws that make you want to strangle the designer. AND YOU DON'T HAVE TO USE AN APP (though one is available) WHICH MEANS YOU DON'T HAVE TO GIVE YOUR PERSONAL DATA TO A PSYCHOPATH! And again, the sound is adequate and inoffensive, and in my lack of experience, I am unconvinced that a much better sound could be produced, even for another $200/unit. But, this is my first pair, so what do I know?

title: Easy to install, works super well
text:
I had seen reviews saying the install was difficult or that you were forced to subscribe to some dumb security service or something. Luckily none of that was true.
Installation was a breeze, took me about 20 min to get all three units going. And most of that time is just waiting for the devices to initialize and connect to each other.
Installation was as follows:
1. Open box, see two satellite units, 1 router unit. (they are labeled as such with a temporary wrapper, but also are permanently labeled on the bottom).
2. Plug ethernet cord from my current (internet provider provided) router/modem combo into the new router unit. Then plug it in for electricity.
3. Wait for the light on the front to cycle through flashing and turn solid blue.
4. Plug in the two satellite units (to electricity) and let them do their thing until their lights are solid blue (I did this with them all just sitting next to each other in the same room).
5. On my phone, connect to the wifi network they are broadcasting (the network ssid and password at written on the bottom of the router unit).
6. Open browser on phone and go to the address listed on the installation card that came in the box.
7. The website suggests that I download and install their phone app, I declined to do so. Maybe that is where they try to sell you on some security package?
8. Follow the steps on the page to set up the devices (setting your admin password etc).
9. Then actually log into the router (in your browser, on your phone, same address as before... use the password you just set.)
10. To make things easy I chose to name my network the exact name of my old network. So first I also logged into my old router and switched off both wifi networks it was broadcasting (2.4 and 5 ghz). And then on the new router I set up the wifi network with the same name and password. Note: If you name the new wifi network something new, or give it a different password, then of course you're going to have to update every device in your house that you want to connect to it to provide it with the new name and password.
11. I had to wait a couple of minutes for all devices in my house to come on line (like 50 things), but they all connected just fine.
12. Now everywhere in my house I have full strength wifi signal.

title: Was great for the few weeks it worked.  Design flaw (overheats) and support is worthless.
text:
I was having intermittent drops with my old Asus router so bought this as an upgrade. I have a smart home and 40+ devices connected so I figured the upgraded dual-core processor was probably what I needed. At first, it worked.... no drops! Then (after just a few weeks) the drops started. Not 5-6 times a day like before, but still... daily. Then I noticed... the log didn't show core 2. It was running as a single core. I opened a ticket with tech support and jumped through all their hoops (factory reset, send screenshots, logs, etc.) They kept escalating to another team. Every few weeks I'd get a response... then it went a month. When I asked where we stood they said "it doesn't happen in the lab." Well no kidding! If this happened in the lab you would be guilty of selling a single core router marketed as "dual core"! Obviously this is not standard behavior. Ugh.
They suggested that I keep the router out in the open to let it cool down and then check back. I sent back a picture of my router sitting out in the open the way it has been since day one, but the "cool down" comment made me do some online research. Whatdaya know? They have a design flaw which causes overheating if you use the LAN ports and/or some advanced features. So you can have dual core, but you have to give up the features that you also paid for?!?!?

The worst part was when I told them I obviously had a defective unit and they said: "It happens. Here's the link for the RMA returns process". This is after months of back and forth where they obviously knew what the issue was (it's well documented in user communities) but stalled with me until I'm well beyond the Amazon return window. So now I can PAY to ship it back to them where they will put it in the (supercooled) lab without all the LAN ports hooked up and say: "It worked fine here!" and send it back.

The software used to tell you the core temperature. That feature was removed. (Why would they do that? ;-) Just kidding they do that so people do not know they are selling products that overheat and fail). You can still find it by going to http://router.asus.com/ajax_coretmp.asp I am currently sitting at 106 C. I'm lucky the whole thing hasn't blown up yet.

Buyer beware. If you intend to use the ports... your router will over heat.

Update: Dissconnected all but one lan port and connected a switch. Rigged some fans. Now 70 C. I shouldn't have to rig my new router Asus!

title: Did what I wanted Better than I Wanted
text:
My wife and I (until just recently) had only non-smart TVs or smart TVs that were no longer being supported with any new apps (Vizio). While we still had access to Netflix and Amazon, that was about it, and our TVs couldn't directly play our own digital movie content from hard drives. So, we took the plunge and used a Raspberry Pi to create a home media center, and went ahead and bought the Air Mouse to act as the controller. And honestly, I loved it.

First, I have to point out one tiny problem - whenever you turn the remote's light on, I would always be met with the warning "Battery running low." No, it wasn't - I never needed to change batteries across any of the 3 Air Mouses we ended up buying. Aside from that, the only other con I can think of is that when you flip between remote and keyboard while the light is on, try to be stable with it, because it seems to use a gyro sensor to determine how you are holding it, and only lights up the side it thinks it needs to (it was annoying typing on a keyboard to have it suddenly go dark lol). My wife - who always held the remote very still and level - never had this problem.

On to the positive. This thing is GREAT. It uses gyro sensing to operate like a mouse on a computer screen, BUT you don't have to use it that way, as I almost never did. A button on the remote allows you to disable and enable that feature, and with it disabled you can just use the basic arrow keys to move around. The keyboard on the back was an amazing life-saver for entering in any kind of typed commands or searches or anything. Then, there are five programmable buttons - four at the bottom, one at the top (the "power" button). I kept the power button as it was, but then reprogrammed the other four to control TV power, volume down and up, and TV input. What I especially loved about this is that one of our TV remotes had issues with the volume registering, so after programming it into this the one time, I didn't need to deal with that anymore.

I will say the instructions for doing this are terrible - so let me provide better ones. Point your Air Mouse and the old remote DIRECTLY AT EACH OTHER and within an inch of one another. Then follow the instructions: hold the TV button down, wait for the light to signal correctly, push the old remote's button you want to transfer, push the button you want to transfer it to, and push the TV button again. The instructions say "put the remotes parallel to each other," but never in a hundred years would I have taken "parallel" to mean "at each other."

The only other thing I want to mention is that the review asked me to rate the Air Mouse on voice recognition, and it has none that I'm aware of. I'm an old school guy, I guess, and I really haven't caught on with the voice command stuff (too creepy for me). As a result, the Air Mouse had just about everything I could want. Now that my wife and I have finally gotten a modern smart TV (NOT Vizio... ugh) we don't need one of our Pi media centers, and are giving it to my in-laws along with the old TV. That means I'll be giving them one of the Air Mouses, but I do so with a twinge of sadness, as I don't love our new remote that goes with the TV, but don't know that I really have a reason to just buy a universal remote similar to the Air Mouse. Oh well.

I loved this thing, and my purchase of two more after the first helps solidify that opinion.

text:
This is unquestionably the worst television I have ever owned. I waited just over a year to write this review because I figured my problems with it could very well just be differences between it and my old TV and I just needed to adjust to it.

The remote has to be pointed at precisely the right spot on the TV or you might as well be across the street with it. I had a television in 1996 that would respond to the remote from quite literally on the other side of a wall. There is no reason this stupid thing needs to be pointed at a .5 square inch dot on the front of the TV in the year TWO THOUSAND AND TWENTY ONE.

There is a 1.7 second delay between when you press a button on the remote and when the TV reacts to it. This must be by design because it is EXACTLY 1.7 seconds and it happens with EVERY button, EVERY time.

Combine that with needing to make sure the remote is aimed directly at one specific spot on front of the TV and you have a garbage TV. And that’s exactly where it’s going. In the garbage. title: Mostly good, somewhat of a manufacturing issue.
text:
When I opened the package I could see that there was a problem. inside the static bag that held the regulators there were several loose capacitors. (see first picture) I contacted Amazon and they are overnighting a replacement, so kudos to Amazon. The product though, still gets a ding for the faulty soldering.

Next up, I needed a fixed 5V output so I followed the procedure in the description to cut the trace and put a solder bridge on the 5V jumper. That trace is tiny, heck everything about this is tiny. My tired old eyes and shaky hands gave up rather quickly on the trace cutting part. The point of cutting the trace is to remove the potentiometer from the circuit, so instead I used my close nippers to cut the wiper off of the top of the pot. (see second picture) Much easier, faster, and with a better certainty of a successful result.

Overall, I am pleased with this product and would (will) buy them again.

title: A few too many issues
text:
Pros: If you're hard of hearing you probably will find a setting that helps you hear your TV better.

Cons: To me, too many issues to find acceptable hearing settings.

Controls are awful. Settings are indicated by blinking blue light that only operates while you are selecting a setting. Once the setting is selected the light indicator no longer is illuminated. You cannot determine what setting you are on unless you push the settings button (which then changes the setting you are on)
Settings only go in one direction. So, if you are on setting 3 and want to go back to setting 2 you must advance through 3-4-5-1 to get back to setting 2. Maybe Not that big of a deal breaker but, todays TV programing audio signals vary greatly from channel to channel.
You may have the sound/audio set on the ZVOX perfect for the channel your watching. But switch the channel to a different program and the ZVOX will likely again need to be reset to your hearing needs. Go back to the original channel you were watching and you have to reset it again. Keep in mind the only indicator of your setting is a temporary blinking blue light.
If youre a channel surfer like me, It becomes pretty frustrating. You will spend more time trying to set your audio than watching your. program !!
The remote adds to your frustration. Poorly designed layout. If your watching your TV in the dark you’ll have to turn on the lights to use the remote. All buttons are the same size, round, and inline with no difference in feel to your thumb. The remotes symmetrical rectangle shape is such that you cant feel the difference from the top or bottom.
The volume control is also indicated by blinking blue and yellow lights that do not indicate what your setting is. It just blinks while you are using it. Blue for volume down and yellow for volume up.mThe volume settings are preset. In my opinion the volume control is not finite enough. More often than not i have to settle for too loud or not loud enough.
I have already ordered a regular powered extension speaker sound bar that will let me use my TV’s audio remote control settings. I suspect i will get as good or better results with it.
I’m pretty sure i will be returning this unit before the 30 trial expires.

title: Appearance might seem cheap; sound quality decent, though could be louder; BT worked great
text:
I got this S39 speaker for its Bluetooth function, though I do like that it can handle a microSD card, USB sources and has a 3.5mm jack. I’m sure other people might need other ports, so this might not work for everyone, though I presume that if you need some of those other connectivity options, you probably are buying a higher end sound system.

This device also has physical buttons on it for changing modes (audio sources) as well as turning the LEDs on/off, and basic controls like pause/play, fast forward, and rewind (which can also be used to move forward and backward in your playlist and pause/play videos such as from Youtube). There is also a volume knob and a power on/off switch and a remote control. Internally, there is a battery that can be charged with the included USB cable.

I personally like the form factor as it kind of looks like an older style stereo speaker as opposed to a stream bar. As far as Bluetooth goes, I had no issues pairing this with an Android phone, a Windows 10 PC, a Chromecast with Google TV, and a newer FireTV stick. I could not pair it with an older FireTV (not a FireTV stick or the FireTV Cube but the one that’s a small, squat square that I don’t think is being made anymore).

I’m not an audiophile. Good enough is good enough for me. The sound quality from this is definitely better than bare minimum. I think it sounds pretty good. It’s not tinny. It has some depth of sound to it. I feel it’s a bit limited as far as volume goes. I want to use this with a projector and have it beneath the screen, but I may need to bring it up closer or have it behind me as I’m not sure the volume will be sufficient if it’s like 20 feet away and there’s ambient noise.

Although I think this is a good speaker for the price, I could see someone wanting something a little sleeker or with a higher end look to it. It does have a non-premium plastic exterior with a plastic handle that you may not want to put too much trust into. If you’re looking for an inexpensive speaker with good sound and features, though, you’ll probably be happy with this.

text:
I have had my Beats Solo headphones for years and naturally the ear foams were starting to deteriorate. Finally the last straw was when the ear foams started depositing little white flakes all the side of my face and hair. Since I didn't want to look like I had a a sudden and severe dandruff problem, I had two options: replace my $200 headphones or see if replacement ear foams were an option.

I stumbled upon these and decided why not?

Size wise, the new ones are a little bigger than the old ones but not enough to where they don't fit on the headphones.

title: Very useful
text:
I can see why this is considered a tool for children, but I found it very useful for myself as a means of note-taking. I used to use so many post-its to give myself reminders, but it felt so much like a waste of paper. This LCD screen makes it a really easy reminder "notepad" for me. It also is a lot cleaner than the white boards, which often leave a messy residue. I don't like that I have to erase everything if I wanted to erase something, but I suppose it's a give-and-take. So far this board is working really well for me.

There are a few downsides to this particular board, though. First, the stylus comes with an elastic lanyard, but there's no set place for that lanyard to go, in order to keep it attached to the tablet. My fix was just to attach it to the battery cover, using the little screw to hold the lanyard in place. So far it works, but a set hole on the tablet would be nice.

The second issue that is very annoying for me is that the magnet (which allows the stylus to attach to the board) is found only on the RIGHT side. I really have a strong disliking for tools like this which show a right-hand bias. As a left-hander, they should at least put a magnet on the top of the board (to make it more ambidextrous), or on the left side of the board in addition to the right. I suppose I could cut the little magnet sticker to size, and stick it on the left, or I could turn this board upside down and use it that way. However, that would be tedious or imperfect. A left-handed perfectionist like me would find it very annoying (which is why I strongly recommend adding a magnet to the left side for the stylus).

title: Significant amount of condensation inside the ear cups
text: The condensation issue is real. Google AirPods Max condensation to learn more. There is significant amount of condensation built up inside the ear cup and directly on the drivers. This is not sweat. This is likely due to the aluminum ear ups acting as a heat dissipation device to keep the AirPods Max cool enough to condense water vapors that keep getting drawn into the warmer air near the ear inside the ear cups through the porous mesh and memory foam material used in the ear pads. This is a major design issue that is likely to cause significant damage to the internal electronics and battery through corrosion by liquids. There is likely to be a full scale recall of those AirPods Max by Apple.

title: May not be a good choice for a high-end system.
text:
This review is based on my experience, which will most likely be different than yours.

I have a 4K Apple TV, and an XBox One X which supports gaming at 4K resolutions, as well as UHD 4K movies that I had hooked up to a 4K projector. I had an older surround sound system that I wanted to upgrade, and had high hopes for this receiver.

My hopes were dashed when I tried to play a 4K movie purchased from Apple. The sound was horribly distorted and unintelligible (it sounded like a loud, stuttering white noise). The sound when playing the movie trailer was exceptional. Also, when playing Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, etc., through my Apple TV. As well as playing Blu Ray movies through my XBox One X.

Also, when my very high quality HDMI cables are connected directly to my projector, my project displays the input as being 4K from a 4K source. However, when connected to the receiver, my projector shows 1080p as the resolution when from a 4K source.

Also, when attempting to use HDR with my Apple TV, it fails when my HDMI cables are connected to the receiver, but not when connected directly to the projector.

Following is my opinion about these challenges: I don't believe this receiver works with HDR content, and I don't believe it is able to decode 4K video, and the audio from a DRM source (such as Apple content).

Also, it makes a loud popping sound whenever you change FM channels, or inputs. A couple of other things that are annoying is the power on/standby LED light. It is way to bright, and blinks when on standby. And, the display is difficult to read because it is way too dim.

I believe that a lot of people would be happy with this receiver, because the sound is exceptional. However, if playing DRM content, HDR, and 4K are important, you may not be.

I am not, and have returned it in favor of a Yamaha product.

I hope this review helps!
